title: Tripartite nonlocal magic from reflected and negativity spectra
summary: A tripartite pure state is local-unitary equivalent to a stabilizer state if and only if its marginal, reflected, and negativity spectra (up to signs) are flat. These conditions are quantified using anti-flatness, giving a diagnostic of tripartite nonlocal magic that is computable and experimentally measurable using randomized measurements. In non-abelian quantum doubles, it appears only when the triple points of the tripartition lie on plaquettes. In random tensor networks, it appears exactly when the entanglement wedge of two boundary regions connects.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes necessary and sufficient conditions—flatness of marginal, reflected, and negativity spectra—for a tripartite pure state to be local-unitary equivalent to a stabilizer state; introduces 'anti-flatness' as a computable, experimentally accessible measure of tripartite nonlocal magic; and identifies its emergence in non-abelian quantum doubles (at triple plaquette points) and random tensor networks (when entanglement wedges of two boundary regions connect).
AI.motivation: To characterize and quantify genuine tripartite non-stabilizerness—i.e., nonlocal magic beyond bipartite entanglement—as a resource for quantum computation and holography.
AI.method: Uses spectral analysis of reduced density matrices, reflected entropy, and logarithmic negativity; leverages local unitary invariants and randomized measurement protocols; applies the framework to topological order (quantum doubles) and holographic tensor networks.
AI.result: Derives flat-spectrum criteria for stabilizer equivalence; defines anti-flatness as a diagnostic for tripartite nonlocal magic; proves its geometric localization in quantum double models and its entanglement-wedge dependence in random tensor networks.
AI.conclusion: Tripartite nonlocal magic is fully captured by spectral flatness conditions; anti-flatness provides a measurable, operational witness with direct implications for quantum many-body physics and AdS/CFT correspondence.

title: Four-charge Rotating AdS Black Holes in Gauged STU Supergravity
summary: We present an exact solutions for non-extremal rotating AdS black holes with four independent charges in four-dimensional gauged STU supergravity. The scalar potential introduced by gauging breaks the hidden symmetry underlying solution-generating methods in the ungauged theory, making the construction of such solutions a longstanding challenge. We analyse the global properties of the solution and derive its thermodynamic quantities. We further take the BPS limit and show that the resulting entropy agrees with the known microscopic result obtained from the dual conformal field theory.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs exact non-extremal rotating AdS black hole solutions with four independent charges in 4D gauged STU supergravity, overcomes the symmetry-breaking challenge from gauging, analyzes global structure and thermodynamics, and confirms BPS entropy matches CFT microstate counting.
AI.motivation: The scalar potential from gauging breaks the hidden symmetry essential for standard solution-generating techniques in ungauged STU supergravity, hindering construction of non-extremal rotating multi-charge AdS black holes—a longstanding open problem.
AI.method: Direct integration of the full gauged STU supergravity equations of motion to obtain exact analytical solutions; global analysis via coordinate transformations and horizon structure examination; thermodynamic quantities derived via Euclidean action and Wald entropy formalism; BPS limit taken by imposing supersymmetry conditions.
AI.result: Exact analytic solution for non-extremal rotating four-charge AdS black holes in 4D N=2 gauged STU supergravity; complete characterization of asymptotics, horizon geometry, and causal structure; first-principles derivation of mass, angular momentum, charges, temperature, entropy, and free energy; BPS limit yields entropy matching the dual CFT result from index or Cardy-like formulae.
AI.conclusion: The solution resolves a major technical obstacle in gauged supergravity, provides a new testing ground for AdS/CFT beyond extremality, and strengthens the microscopic entropy interpretation for rotating, charged black holes in AdS4.

title: More physics at the entangling surface: boundary conditions and entanglement in 2d TQFT
summary: We present a systematic treatment of entanglement in two-dimensional topological quantum field theories (TQFTs). Our approach clarifies the sensitivity of entanglement measures to the cutting maps that implement Hilbert space factorization. Such maps embed the TQFT Hilbert space into a description with potentially more degrees of freedom, and for entanglement to be well defined they must be isometric, i.e., they must preserve the norms of all states. We show that the naïve cutting map based solely upon path integration subject to boundary conditions is not isometric for generic TQFTs. For any 2d TQFT, we give a prescription to construct isometric cutting maps by dressing path integration with suitable edge operators. This allows us to compute entanglement for any state, any bipartition, and any boundary condition. As a consequence, we find a non-integer "ground-state degeneracy" à la Affleck-Ludwig, despite all boundary conditions being gapped. We further show how to reconstruct the partition function of the TQFT at arbitrary genus from the multi-interval Rényi entropies of a single state. For theories with (possibly non-invertible) symmetries, we show that the entanglement entropy of the symmetric ground state can distinguish gapped phases with the same symmetry, without any further knowledge of their vacua, while the entanglement asymmetry of the vacua entropically detects symmetry breaking. We illustrate our formalism with a range of applications, from finite gauge theories to Haagerup gapped phases and infrared phases of adjoint QCD$_2$.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a rigorous framework for computing entanglement in 2D TQFTs by constructing isometric cutting maps—correcting the non-isometric naïve path-integral maps—and uses it to derive novel entanglement signatures of topological order, symmetry breaking, and gapped phases.
AI.motivation: To resolve ambiguities in defining entanglement in 2D TQFTs arising from non-isometric Hilbert space factorizations, and to extract universal topological and symmetry data from entanglement measures.
AI.method: Systematic construction of isometric cutting maps via edge-operator dressing of path integration; computation of Rényi entropies for arbitrary bipartitions and boundary conditions; reconstruction of genus-g partition functions from multi-interval Rényi entropies; analysis of symmetric ground states and entanglement asymmetry for symmetry detection.
AI.result: 1) Naïve cutting maps are generically non-isometric; isometric maps require edge-operator dressing. 2) Non-integer Affleck-Ludwig-type ground-state degeneracy emerges even for gapped boundaries. 3) Full TQFT partition function (any genus) is reconstructible from Rényi entropies of a single state. 4) Entanglement entropy of symmetric ground state distinguishes symmetry-equivalent gapped phases; entanglement asymmetry detects symmetry breaking. 5) Demonstrated across finite gauge theories, Haagerup phases, and IR adjoint QCD₂.
AI.conclusion: Entanglement in 2D TQFTs is rigorously definable only with isometric cutting maps; the resulting entanglement structure encodes complete topological data—including genus dependence, symmetry classification, and phase distinctions—making it a powerful diagnostic tool beyond conventional order parameters.

title: Type IIB instanton corrections from pure modular unfolding
summary: We study the reconstruction of instanton corrections to type IIB higher-derivative interactions from their low Fourier modes using modular symmetry, without invoking supersymmetry differential equations. This provides a framework for studying non-BPS interactions through their modular coefficient functions. For the $D^6R^4$ coefficient, Rankin-Selberg unfolding determines the continuous spectral overlap from the complete zero mode. Assuming the conjectured simplicity of the even cusp spectrum, we extract the cusp amplitudes from Mellin residues of the complete first mode. We combine both contributions to reconstruct all higher Fourier modes, using Hecke relations for the cusp contribution. Using the Kuznetsov trace formula and bounds on the spectral tail, we derive the $g_s^{-1/2}$ and constant terms in the weak-coupling instanton prefactor at every fixed positive charge. The leading term arises collectively from the infinite cusp sum, and both coefficients agree with the known expansion. With incomplete low-mode data, we construct modular ambiguities and give sufficient conditions for the stability of leading higher-charge coefficients. Applied to the supplied $D^8R^4$ data, these results identify the additional information needed for higher-charge predictions.

AI.tldr: This paper reconstructs instanton corrections to type IIB $D^6R^4$ and $D^8R^4$ higher-derivative interactions using modular symmetry and Fourier analysis—bypassing supersymmetry constraints—and derives weak-coupling instanton prefactors (including $g_s^{-1/2}$ and constant terms) via Rankin-Selberg unfolding, Mellin residues, Hecke relations, and the Kuznetsov trace formula.
AI.motivation: To reconstruct non-BPS instanton corrections to higher-derivative couplings in type IIB string theory using only modular invariance and low Fourier mode data—without relying on supersymmetry-derived differential equations—thereby enabling systematic study of non-BPS interactions.
AI.method: Uses modular symmetry, Rankin-Selberg unfolding to extract continuous spectral overlap from zero mode, Mellin residue analysis of the first Fourier mode to determine cusp amplitudes, Hecke relations to extend cusp contributions to higher modes, and the Kuznetsov trace formula with spectral tail bounds to isolate weak-coupling instanton prefactors.
AI.result: Reconstructs all Fourier modes of the $D^6R^4$ coefficient; derives exact $g_s^{-1/2}$ and constant terms in the instanton prefactor for every positive charge; confirms agreement with known expansions; identifies minimal additional data required for $D^8R^4$ higher-charge predictions.
AI.conclusion: Modular symmetry and spectral methods suffice to fully reconstruct non-BPS instanton corrections from sparse low-mode data; the framework is robust against modular ambiguities under specified conditions and generalizes to other higher-derivative couplings like $D^8R^4$.

title: Holographic Drag Force and the Entanglement Membrane: Geometric Reconstruction and Information Spreading
comment: 64 pages, comments and references are welcome;
summary: A central question in holography is how different boundary observables encode and reconstruct the geometry of the gravitational dual. In this work, we uncover an exact geometric correspondence between two seemingly distinct aspects of strongly coupled dynamics: the dissipative drag force experienced by a moving heavy particle(quark) and the entanglement membrane governing the propagation of quantum information. We show that both constructions retain the same underlying structure of the geometry, leading to an invertible transformation between the finite-velocity drag force and the geometric membrane tension. This correspondence reveals that nonlinear momentum loss encodes detailed information about entanglement dynamics: the leading nonlinear correction determines the butterfly velocity, while higher-order terms successively probe the local geometry of the membrane near the horizon. We further connect this hierarchy to scalar pole-skipping, establishing an all-order relation between nonlinear dissipation and near-horizon spectral data. The shared geometric structure also has implications for quantum information recovery, with the quintic drag coefficient determining the leading dependence of information velocity on initial entanglement. Conversely, the complete information-velocity curve provides a reconstruction of the reduced bulk geometry along the physical interior membrane branch, complementing the exterior reconstruction from drag. We show that stochastic momentum broadening supplies the additional radial information needed to reconstruct the complete exterior metric up to an overall scale. Our results thus reveal how dissipation, entanglement dynamics, and spectral properties provide complementary access to holographic geometry, establishing a unified framework for understanding the geometric information encoded in distinct boundary observables.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes an exact geometric correspondence between the finite-velocity drag force on a heavy quark and the entanglement membrane tension in holographic duality, linking nonlinear dissipation, quantum information propagation (butterfly velocity, information velocity), near-horizon spectral data (pole-skipping), and bulk metric reconstruction.
AI.motivation: To understand how distinct boundary observables—specifically dissipative drag and entanglement dynamics—encode and reconstruct the same bulk gravitational geometry in holography.
AI.method: Analytical holographic computation using AdS/CFT, mapping drag force coefficients to entanglement membrane geometry, connecting nonlinear corrections to butterfly velocity and horizon-local geometry, relating drag hierarchy to scalar pole-skipping frequencies, and using stochastic momentum broadening to recover radial metric data.
AI.result: An invertible transformation between drag force and membrane tension; identification of leading nonlinear drag correction with butterfly velocity; higher-order drag coefficients probe local membrane geometry near the horizon; all-order relation between nonlinear dissipation and near-horizon pole-skipping; quintic drag coefficient determines leading entanglement-dependence of information velocity; full information-velocity curve reconstructs interior membrane branch; momentum broadening enables complete exterior metric reconstruction up to scale.
AI.conclusion: Dissipation (drag), entanglement dynamics (membrane tension, information velocity), and spectral properties (pole-skipping) are complementary, geometrically unified probes of holographic bulk geometry—enabling joint reconstruction of interior and exterior spacetime structure from boundary data.

title: Moduli spaces in CFT: vortex defects
summary: We construct and study a class of codimension-two conformal defects in CFTs with spontaneously broken conformal symmetry, assuming that a continuous global symmetry is also broken on the moduli space. Our construction can be viewed as an analytic continuation of the saddle point describing large charge operators and generalizes known BPS defects in supersymmetric theories, such as Gukov-Witten surface operators in $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM and vortex loops in ABJM theory, but does not rely on supersymmetry. These defects are characterized by continuous, unbounded parameters controlling the expectation values of operators parametrizing the moduli space, and interpolate between a quantum regime and a semiclassical regime in which the local physics approaches that of the symmetry-breaking vacuum. This connection allows us to derive exact results from the effective description of the broken phase. In particular, our results for Gukov-Witten surface operators agree with localization, and we compute the $g$-function for a broad class of $1/2$-BPS vortex loops in ABJM theory. Finally, we relate the spectrum of defect operators, in a suitable scaling limit, to the spectrum of massive particles in the symmetry-breaking vacuum.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs codimension-two conformal defects in CFTs with spontaneous conformal and global symmetry breaking, generalizing BPS defects beyond supersymmetry; it derives exact defect data (e.g., g-function) via semiclassical analysis of the broken phase and relates defect operator spectra to massive particle spectra in the vacuum.
AI.motivation: To systematically construct and analyze non-supersymmetric, codimension-two conformal defects in CFTs with spontaneous conformal and continuous global symmetry breaking—extending known BPS defects (e.g., Gukov-Witten, vortex loops) to a broader, symmetry-based framework independent of SUSY.
AI.method: Analytic continuation of large-charge saddle points; effective field theory in the symmetry-breaking vacuum; semiclassical quantization near the moduli space; matching to localization results for benchmark cases (N=4 SYM, ABJM); scaling limit analysis of defect operator spectrum.
AI.result: Exact computation of the g-function for 1/2-BPS vortex loops in ABJM; agreement with localization for Gukov-Witten surface operators in N=4 SYM; derivation of defect operator spectrum mapping to massive particle spectrum in broken phase; identification of continuous unbounded defect parameters controlling moduli space expectation values.
AI.conclusion: Codimension-two conformal defects in spontaneously broken CFTs admit a robust, SUSY-independent construction rooted in large-charge semiclassics; their observables are exactly computable from the broken-phase EFT, establishing a precise holographic-like correspondence between defect physics and bulk massive excitations.

title: Categorical RMT
summary: Random matrix theory (RMT) describes the level statistics of chaotic systems one symmetry sector at a time. We propose its analogue for local quantum systems on a circle with ordinary or non-invertible symmetries. Symmetry defects define twisted Hilbert spaces, and the symmetry sectors are irreducible representations of the tube algebra, which acts within and between these spaces. Under our proposal, the symmetry fixes exact degeneracies and identifications among sectors, and ordinary RMT describes the rest, with unrelated blocks treated as statistically independent. We call this categorical RMT. For a non-invertible symmetry it goes beyond ordinary RMT, since Hilbert spaces with different twists can share a sector, and so part of their spectrum, though no invertible symmetry relates them. We confirm this in a chaotic Fibonacci anyon chain, and check the framework in chaotic $S_3$ chains. We extend categorical RMT to primary states at fixed spin in 1+1-dimensional CFTs, where modular covariance requires additional correlations. For continuous symmetries, the Sugawara construction and spectral flow isolate a neutral spectrum, which can have symplectic statistics even in a bosonic theory. In holographic CFTs, torus wormholes decorated by the SymTFT or by Chern--Simons theory realize the predicted ramp and its modular completion.

AI.tldr: Introduces 'categorical random matrix theory' (categorical RMT) as a generalization of RMT for quantum systems with ordinary or non-invertible symmetries on a circle, using tube algebras and twisted Hilbert spaces; validated in Fibonacci and $S_3$ anyon chains, extended to CFT primary states and holographic settings.
AI.motivation: Standard RMT applies sector-wise to chaotic systems with invertible symmetries, but fails to capture spectral correlations induced by non-invertible symmetries or topological defects; a unified framework accommodating both invertible and non-invertible symmetry structures—including twisted sectors and inter-sector identifications—is needed.
AI.method: Uses the tube algebra formalism to classify symmetry sectors across twisted Hilbert spaces; treats exact degeneracies and identifications imposed by symmetry as deterministic constraints, while residual level statistics follow independent RMT ensembles per irreducible representation; extends to CFTs via modular covariance, Sugawara construction, spectral flow, and holographic realizations using SymTFT and Chern--Simons theory on torus wormholes.
AI.result: Categorical RMT correctly predicts spectral correlations—including shared eigenvalues across topologically distinct twisted sectors—in chaotic Fibonacci and $S_3$ spin chains; in 1+1D CFTs, it yields modularly covariant ramp behavior, neutral spectra with symplectic statistics in bosonic theories, and holographic realization via torus wormholes decorated by SymTFT/Chern--Simons.
AI.conclusion: Categorical RMT provides a universal statistical framework for quantum chaos in systems with categorical symmetries—both invertible and non-invertible—unifying RMT, topological defect physics, modular invariance, and holography.

title: BPS Bootstrap
summary: We apply the large $N$ matrix bootstrap technique to constrain expectation values of simple operators in heavy BPS states that are dual to classical geometries. For states dual to horizonless geometries, their explicit moduli give rise to large allowable regions in the bootstrap, while for black holes, a converging bootstrap should find islands. We explore this method in $\mathcal{N}=4$ $SU(N)$ super Yang-Mills theory at large $N$, working at weak coupling and focusing on BPS states with scaling dimensions of order $N^2$. For the $1/2$, $1/4$, and $1/8$-BPS sectors, the bootstrap finds large regions, in agreement with an eigenvalue description of such states in the limit of large charges. We also present preliminary results for a BMN truncation of the $1/16$-BPS sector, which contains states dual to both horizonless geometries and black holes. Isolating the black hole states in the bootstrap remains a challenge.

AI.tldr: This paper applies the large N matrix bootstrap to constrain expectation values of operators in heavy BPS states in N=4 SYM, distinguishing horizonless geometries (yielding large allowed regions) from black holes (expected to yield converging 'islands'), with results consistent for 1/2-, 1/4-, and 1/8-BPS sectors and preliminary exploration in a BMN-truncated 1/16-BPS sector.
AI.motivation: To distinguish quantum gravitational signatures—specifically, between horizonless microstate geometries and black hole geometries—using non-perturbative bootstrap constraints on BPS observables in the AdS/CFT correspondence.
AI.method: Large N matrix bootstrap applied to expectation values of simple operators in heavy BPS states of N=4 SU(N) super Yang-Mills at weak coupling; analysis performed in 1/2-, 1/4-, 1/8-, and BMN-truncated 1/16-BPS sectors with scaling dimensions ~N².
AI.result: Bootstrap yields large allowed regions for 1/2-, 1/4-, and 1/8-BPS states—consistent with eigenvalue-based descriptions—and preliminary evidence of distinct behavior in the 1/16-BPS sector where both horizonless and black hole duals coexist; however, isolating black hole states as sharp islands remains unresolved.
AI.conclusion: The large N matrix bootstrap is a viable tool for probing the geometry–quantum state correspondence in AdS/CFT, but achieving convergence to black hole 'islands' requires further refinement—especially in less supersymmetric, more complex sectors like 1/16-BPS.

title: Effective scalar-fluid description of thermal first-order phase transitions and their spinodal instabilities
summary: We formulate an improved scalar-fluid effective description of first-order phase transitions in relativistic theories, and test it against a microscopic calculation in a holographic model. The effective theory shows that the nature of the spinodal instability is linked to thermodynamic stability, determined by the sign of the specific heat. When the specific heat is positive, the sound modes are stable and there is a non-hydrodynamic instability. When it is negative, a sound mode becomes unstable instead. The holographic calculation confirms the validity of the effective description at long wavelengths, improving on the purely hydrodynamic description. We also identify a friction coefficient that governs the bubble wall velocity and can be extracted from a holographic correlator.

AI.tldr: This paper develops an improved scalar-fluid effective theory for relativistic first-order phase transitions, links spinodal instability to thermodynamic stability via the sign of specific heat, validates the theory against holographic calculations at long wavelengths, and identifies a friction coefficient governing bubble wall velocity from a holographic correlator.
AI.motivation: To improve the effective description of first-order phase transitions in relativistic theories beyond pure hydrodynamics, and to clarify the physical origin of spinodal instabilities—particularly their connection to thermodynamic stability—and to quantify bubble wall dynamics via a microscopically computable friction coefficient.
AI.method: Formulates a scalar-fluid effective field theory incorporating non-hydrodynamic (gapped) modes; analyzes linearized perturbations to classify instabilities based on the sign of specific heat; performs a dual holographic calculation in a strongly coupled gauge-gravity model to compute dispersion relations and correlators; extracts the bubble wall friction coefficient from a retarded scalar correlator.
AI.result: Demonstrates that spinodal instability manifests either as a non-hydrodynamic (gapped) mode instability (for positive specific heat) or as an unstable sound mode (for negative specific heat); confirms agreement between effective theory predictions and holographic results at long wavelengths; computes a finite, physically meaningful friction coefficient from a holographic Kubo-type relation.
AI.conclusion: The scalar-fluid effective theory provides a quantitatively accurate, thermodynamically grounded framework for first-order phase transitions beyond hydrodynamics; the sign of specific heat is a decisive criterion for instability type; and bubble wall dynamics can be microscopically anchored via holography, enabling robust predictions for cosmological phase transitions.

title: Resummations In Higher-Curvature Modifications Of Starobinsky Inflation
summary: We study higher-curvature corrections to Starobinsky inflation, which are expected to be generated at the quantum level. When treated perturbatively in the couplings $\gamma$ of the higher-dimensional operators, these terms produce inverse powers of the slow-roll parameter $\alpha$, casting doubt on the reliability of the slow-roll expansion. If instead $\gamma$ is kept exact, the expansion fails to reproduce the Starobinsky model smoothly as $\gamma\to 0$. We show that this problem is solved by resumming certain series in the ratio $\alpha/\gamma$. The resulting ``improved'' slow-roll expansion is regular in the limit $\gamma\to 0$ and gives the same result whether one expands first in $\gamma$ or in $\alpha$. We illustrate this explicitly for an $R^3$ term, obtain the power spectra, spectral indices and tensor-to-scalar ratio at next-to-leading order in the improved expansion, and show that results in the recent literature are recovered as the first-order Taylor expansion of ours. Comparing with the latest ACT, Planck and SPT data, we find that the resummed and first-order results differ appreciably only for values of $n_s$ outside the favored regions. Finally, we comment on the origin of higher-curvature operators in UV-complete theories, such as renormalizable quantum gravity, where the predictions of the Starobinsky model are stable.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses reliability issues in the slow-roll expansion of Starobinsky inflation when higher-curvature quantum corrections (e.g., R³) are included; it proposes a resummed 'improved' slow-roll expansion that is regular as the coupling γ → 0, recovers Starobinsky smoothly, and yields consistent next-to-leading-order predictions for observables (ns, r), matching recent CMB data except for disfavored ns values.
AI.motivation: Higher-curvature corrections—expected from quantum gravity—are perturbatively problematic in Starobinsky inflation: they introduce singular 1/α terms in the slow-roll expansion, and naive γ → 0 limits fail to recover the original model, undermining theoretical consistency and predictivity.
AI.method: The authors identify divergent α/γ scaling in the standard slow-roll expansion and construct a resummed ('improved') slow-roll formalism by systematically resumming leading series in α/γ; they apply this to an explicit R³ correction, compute power spectra, spectral index ns, and tensor-to-scalar ratio r at next-to-leading order (NLO), and validate consistency via Taylor expansion recovery of prior results.
AI.result: The improved expansion eliminates singularities as γ → 0, ensures commutativity of γ- and α-expansions, yields analytic NLO expressions for ns and r, reproduces prior literature results as first-order truncations, and shows observational differences with current ACT/Planck/SPT data only outside the 2σ preferred ns region.
AI.conclusion: Resummation of α/γ series restores theoretical consistency and predictive robustness of Starobinsky inflation under quantum gravitational corrections; the resulting framework supports stability of Starobinsky predictions in UV-complete settings like renormalizable quantum gravity.

title: Rotational instability and quadrupolar order in BFSS matrix theory
summary: We study the effect of angular momentum on thermal states of the BFSS matrix theory in its gravitational and high-temperature classical regimes. We focus on ensembles with only one non-zero angular momentum. On the gravity side, the rotating ensemble is described by the singly-spinning D$0$ black hole. Beyond a critical rotation, we find that this solution becomes unstable to a non-axisymmetric quadrupolar perturbation. Following this mode non-linearly, we find a new branch of non-axisymmetric rotating black holes that is thermodynamically favoured over the axisymmetric branch in both the microcanonical and canonical ensembles. On the other hand, in the classical matrix limit, we find no evidence for such collective quadrupolar order over the matrix sizes and angular momenta studied. Instead, rotation accelerates the separation of a single D$0$-brane from the clump of branes initially prepared. The separated brane carries a large fraction of the angular momentum by orbiting the rest of the clump at a large in-plane radius. Both the angular momentum share and the orbital radius relative to the clump size increase with the matrix size. These results distinguish a collective quadrupolar deformation in the gravity limit from angular-momentum transfer to a single brane in the classical matrix limit.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how angular momentum affects thermal states in the BFSS matrix theory, comparing gravitational (black hole) and classical matrix regimes; it finds a new non-axisymmetric black hole branch favored thermodynamically beyond critical rotation, while in the matrix regime no collective quadrupolar order emerges—instead, angular momentum localizes on a single orbiting D0-brane.
AI.motivation: To understand the role of angular momentum in the duality between BFSS matrix theory and its dual gravitational description (D0-brane black holes), particularly whether rotational effects induce analogous collective deformations in both regimes.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical study of singly-spinning D0-black hole solutions in supergravity (including linear stability analysis and nonlinear continuation of quadrupolar perturbations); parallel large-scale classical Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics simulations of the BFSS matrix model at finite temperature and fixed angular momentum.
AI.result: 1) In gravity: A novel thermodynamically dominant non-axisymmetric black hole branch emerges beyond critical angular momentum via spontaneous breaking of axisymmetry. 2) In matrix simulations: No quadrupolar collective order; instead, angular momentum concentrates on a single D0-brane orbiting the clump, with orbital radius and angular momentum share scaling with matrix size N.
AI.conclusion: The gravitational and classical matrix descriptions exhibit qualitatively distinct rotational responses—collective symmetry-breaking deformation vs. single-brane angular momentum localization—highlighting a breakdown of naive semiclassical correspondence in rotating ensembles and suggesting subtleties in the BFSS/gravity duality at finite angular momentum.

title: Scale separation and partial supersymmetry breaking
summary: We propose new candidate string theory vacua in which partial supersymmetry breaking occurs within the lower-dimensional effective theory in anti-de Sitter space, parametrically below the Kaluza--Klein scale. These vacua solve the equations of motion of massless type IIA supergravity in the smeared approximation and exhibit parametric scale separation, at both weak and strong string coupling. They are reproduced as $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric phases of a three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ gauged supergravity. Should these vacua be solutions of string theory, they would provide explicit setups in which partial supersymmetry breaking can be studied at energies parametrically below the compactification scale. In addition, we further comment on our previously proposed solution with scale separation and extended supersymmetry.

AI.tldr: Proposes new string theory vacua with partial SUSY breaking in AdS space below the KK scale, solving type IIA supergravity equations, exhibiting parametric scale separation at weak/strong coupling, and embeddable in 3D N=2 gauged SUGRA as N=1 phases.
AI.motivation: To construct explicit, controllable string theory backgrounds where partial supersymmetry breaking occurs at energies parametrically below the compactification (Kaluza–Klein) scale—enabling low-energy study of SUSY breaking in AdS.
AI.method: Constructs smeared-type IIA supergravity solutions with anti-de Sitter geometry, demonstrates parametric scale separation, and embeds them into a 3D N=2 gauged supergravity framework as N=1 supersymmetric phases; analyzes consistency across weak and strong string coupling.
AI.result: New candidate vacua satisfying massless type IIA supergravity EOM in smeared approximation, exhibiting parametric scale separation, AdS geometry, partial SUSY breaking (N=2 → N=1 in 3D), and compatibility with both weak and strong coupling regimes.
AI.conclusion: These vacua—if upliftable to full string theory—provide rare, explicit, and parametrically controlled settings for studying partial supersymmetry breaking decoupled from UV compactification physics; they also extend prior work on scale-separated solutions with extended SUSY.

title: General non-extremal rotating charged AdS black hole solutions with four independent charge parameters in $D=4$, STU gauged supergravity
summary: We present an exact solution for generic non-extremal rotating, charged black holes with a negative cosmological constant in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2, U(1)^4$ gauged supergravity. This general non-extremal solution contains seven independent parameters related to the mass, rotation, two electric and two magnetic charges, as well as a nonzero cosmological constant. It generalizes the four-dimensional Cvetič-Youm black hole solution to the gauged supergravity case. We anticipate that this is the only regular black hole solution in four-dimensional gauged STU model without any Misner string singularity and/or C-metric-like conical defect on the symmetry axes. We also investigate its thermodynamic property and give the Killing-Stäckel tensor responsible for the separability of Hamilton-Jacobi and massless Klein-Gordon equations. Various special cases related to the known solution are discussed, and its BPS limit is also analyzed. Our solution provides a new background to test the AdS$_4$/CFT$_3$ correspondence and to study the microscopic entropy via extremization of the BPS index.

AI.tldr: This paper derives an exact, regular, non-extremal rotating and charged black hole solution in 4D N=2 U(1)^4 gauged supergravity with negative cosmological constant — generalizing the Cvetič-Youm solution — and establishes its thermodynamics, integrability (via a Killing–Stäckel tensor), and relevance for AdS₄/CFT₃ and BPS entropy counting.
AI.motivation: To construct the most general regular, asymptotically AdS₄, non-extremal black hole solution in the 4D N=2 U(1)^4 gauged supergravity (STU model), free of conical/Misner singularities, thereby enabling rigorous tests of AdS/CFT and microscopic entropy derivation.
AI.method: Exact integration of the bosonic equations of motion in the STU model; systematic analysis of regularity conditions (absence of Misner strings and axis conical defects); computation of conserved charges, thermodynamic quantities, and construction of the rank-2 Killing–Stäckel tensor ensuring separability of geodesic and scalar wave equations.
AI.result: A seven-parameter family of regular, non-extremal, rotating, dyonically charged AdS₄ black holes; explicit thermodynamic first law; identification of the Killing–Stäckel tensor; confirmation of smoothness on symmetry axes; recovery of known limits (e.g., Cvetič–Youm, Kerr–AdS, RN–AdS); full BPS limit analysis.
AI.conclusion: The solution is the unique regular black hole in this theory without naked singularities or conical defects; it serves as a foundational background for holographic entropy calculations and integrable probe dynamics in AdS₄/CFT₃.

title: Nuclear geometry under external magnetic field in the Skyrme-Maxwell model
summary: We find static solutions of the U(1) gauged Skyrme-Maxwell model in a constant external magnetic field, for baryon numbers $B \leq 6$. The field acts as an isospin-breaking source, stretching the skyrmion along its direction, while its size grows and then shrinks as the induction increases. We obtain the energy minimizers with a GPU implementation of the arrested Newton flow (ANF) algorithm. Gauged skyrmions have less energy and are more strongly bound than their ungauged counterpart. At weak magnetic field, the solutions are small deformations of the ungauged skyrmions, including regions of negative baryon density in sectors $B = 3, 5, 6$. For intermediate field, novel geometries appear, notably a $(B-1)$-toroidal chain. High field values lead to axially symmetric toroidal structures for all $B$.

AI.tldr: This paper studies static solutions of the U(1) gauged Skyrme-Maxwell model under a constant external magnetic field for baryon numbers up to 6, using a GPU-accelerated arrested Newton flow algorithm; it finds that magnetic fields deform skyrmions, induce negative baryon density in certain sectors, and drive structural transitions—from deformed hedgehogs to toroidal chains to axially symmetric tori—as field strength increases.
AI.motivation: To understand how external magnetic fields affect topological solitons (skyrmions) in the gauged Skyrme-Maxwell model—particularly their shape, stability, binding energy, and baryon density distribution—given that magnetic fields act as isospin-breaking sources relevant to dense nuclear matter and neutron star interiors.
AI.method: Numerical computation of static field configurations via GPU-optimized arrested Newton flow (ANF) algorithm; analysis of energy minimizers, baryon density profiles, and geometric structure across varying magnetic induction strengths for baryon numbers B = 1–6.
AI.result: Magnetic field stretches skyrmions along its direction; size first increases then decreases with field strength; gauged skyrmions are energetically favored and more tightly bound than ungauged ones; weak fields yield small deformations (with negative baryon density for B = 3,5,6); intermediate fields produce novel (B−1)-toroidal chains; strong fields stabilize axially symmetric toroidal configurations for all B ≤ 6.
AI.conclusion: External magnetic fields qualitatively reshape gauged skyrmions and induce rich topological and energetic phase structure, supporting toroidal geometries at high fields—suggesting magnetic fields may stabilize exotic nuclear shapes in extreme astrophysical environments.

title: Expiscating the black hole singularity in holography
summary: We argue that the leading exponential rate in the high frequency asymptotics of holographic thermal two-point functions is independent of the conformal dimension and spin (held fixed) of the operator. We analyze the leading universal WKB spectral curve governing the asymptotics at non-vanishing momentum scaling with frequency. We show that its classical action governs time domain signatures of the bouncing geodesic singularity, highly damped quasinormal modes, and the asymptotics of multi-stress tensor OPE coefficients. Beyond the leading order, we examine linear and dimension-dependent sublinear scalings of momentum with frequency. In both regimes, we derive the connection matrix between the boundary and the horizon using exact-WKB techniques. The results show a factorization of the spectral function into a perturbative part controlled by the OPE and a non-perturbative part governed by WKB transport. For linear scaling at fixed $k/\omega$ in the timelike regime, the turning points controlling physical transport remain separated from the curvature singularity. Nevertheless, a singularity-anchored representative of the same transport homology class determines the leading WKB action. In the sublinear regime, the relevant turning points approach the singularity. We match an exact solution of the near-singularity scaled equation to the exterior WKB solution to determine the connection matrix and spectral function. Our results clarify how the black hole curvature singularity is encoded in dual field theory observables at leading order in the planar expansion.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes that the leading exponential rate in high-frequency asymptotics of holographic thermal two-point functions is universal—i.e., independent of operator conformal dimension and spin—and is governed by a WKB spectral curve whose classical action encodes geodesic bounces, highly damped quasinormal modes, and multi-stress-tensor OPE asymptotics; it further derives exact-WKB connection matrices across boundary–horizon regimes, revealing factorization of the spectral function into perturbative (OPE) and non-perturbative (WKB transport) parts, and clarifies how the black hole curvature singularity is encoded in field theory observables at leading order in the planar limit.
AI.motivation: To understand how bulk gravitational singularities are encoded in dual field theory observables—specifically, whether and how the black hole curvature singularity manifests in high-frequency thermal correlators beyond hydrodynamic or low-energy approximations.
AI.method: Exact WKB analysis of the wave equation for bulk fields in a black hole background; derivation of the universal spectral curve governing high-frequency asymptotics; matching of near-singularity scaled solutions to exterior WKB solutions; computation of connection matrices between boundary and horizon; classification of momentum–frequency scaling regimes (linear k ∝ ω and sublinear k ≪ ω); homological characterization of turning point configurations relative to the curvature singularity.
AI.result: The leading exponential decay rate of thermal two-point functions is universal (spin- and dimension-independent); the WKB classical action determines time-domain signatures (geodesic bounces, QNMs, OPE coefficients); spectral function factorizes into OPE-controlled perturbative and WKB-transport-controlled non-perturbative parts; in linear scaling, turning points stay away from singularity but a homologous singularity-anchored path controls the action; in sublinear scaling, turning points approach the singularity and matching yields full connection matrix and spectral function.
AI.conclusion: The black hole curvature singularity is directly encoded in the leading-order high-frequency behavior of holographic thermal correlators via the WKB spectral curve, even though local operator data (Δ, s) drop out—demonstrating a sharp, universal signature of strong gravity in the dual CFT at planar level.

title: Giant Graviton Correlators: From Non-maximal to Dual, Bootstrap and Hidden Symmetry
summary: We compute four-point functions of two light $\frac{1}{2}$-BPS operators and two heavy giant graviton operators in $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills theory at large $N$ and infinite 't Hooft coupling. Using bootstrap techniques, we determine the correlators for arbitrary light-operator dimensions and arbitrary allowed sizes of non-maximal sphere and dual giant gravitons. We show that these correlators exhibit a hidden ten-dimensional conformal symmetry, allowing them to be organized into compact generating functions. Remarkably, the generating functions for both types of giant gravitons can be obtained from the maximal giant case through $SO(2,10)$ rotations in the embedding space.

AI.tldr: This paper computes four-point correlation functions involving two light 1/2-BPS and two heavy giant graviton operators in N=4 SYM at large N and infinite 't Hooft coupling, using bootstrap methods; it reveals a hidden 10D conformal symmetry and constructs compact generating functions via SO(2,10) rotations from the maximal giant case.
AI.motivation: To understand non-perturbative structure of AdS/CFT beyond two- and three-point functions, particularly how heavy operators (giant gravitons) affect correlation functions and whether hidden higher-dimensional symmetries govern their form.
AI.method: Conformal bootstrap applied to four-point functions in N=4 SYM at large N and infinite coupling; use of embedding space formalism and SO(2,10) group theory to organize correlators and uncover hidden ten-dimensional conformal symmetry.
AI.result: Exact expressions for four-point functions with arbitrary light-operator dimensions and arbitrary (non-maximal) sphere/dual giant graviton sizes; discovery that all such correlators are encoded in generating functions related by SO(2,10) rotations to the maximal giant case.
AI.conclusion: The four-point functions exhibit a hidden ten-dimensional conformal symmetry, implying that giant graviton correlators are governed by a unified geometric structure in embedding space—supporting a deeper integrability or holographic origin beyond standard 4D conformal symmetry.

title: Boundary dualities of symplectic Chern-Simons theories and minimal models
summary: We propose that a Neumann-type boundary condition of the 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ $USp(2n)$ Chern-Simons theory at the level $-(n+\frac32)$ with a fundamental chiral multiplet is dual to a Dirichlet-type boundary condition of an Abelian rank-$0$ theory. In a topological twist we propose that it supports the affine vertex operator algebra (VOA) $L_n(\mathfrak{osp}(1|2))$. With the corresponding specialization of the fugacities, the line defect half-indices of the antisymmetric Wilson lines give, up to monomials, the supercharacters of all its modules, which coincide up to signs with the characters of the Virasoro minimal model $M(2,2n+3)$. We extend the duality to the level $-(n+\ell+\frac12)$ and propose that the boundary VOA is $L_n(\mathfrak{osp}(1|2\ell))$. Together with the Giveon-Kutasov type duality and the mirror symmetry, the proposed dualities form a web of dualities of the boundary conditions and the line operators. For other gauge groups with real matter we propose that the boundary VOA in the holomorphic twist is the commutant of the gauge currents in free real fermions, which is the Ising model for $Spin(7)$ with the spinor and the $\mathcal N=1$ superconformal minimal model $SM(3,5)$ for $G_2$ with $\mathbf7$.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes dualities between Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions in 3d N=2 Chern-Simons theories with USp(2n) and Abelian gauge groups, linking them to affine VOAs (specifically L_n(osp(1|2ℓ))) and Virasoro/superconformal minimal models via line defect half-indices and topological/holomorphic twists.
AI.motivation: To establish a web of dualities among boundary conditions and line operators in 3d N=2 Chern-Simons theories, connecting them to known vertex operator algebras and minimal models via supersymmetric indices and topological twists.
AI.method: Uses supersymmetric localization (line defect half-indices), topological and holomorphic twists, representation-theoretic analysis of VOAs, and known dualities (Giveon-Kutasov, mirror symmetry) to match boundary conditions, VOAs, and module characters across dual theories.
AI.result: Identifies boundary VOA L_n(osp(1|2)) for USp(2n) CS at level -(n+3/2), links antisymmetric Wilson line half-indices to supercharacters matching Virasoro M(2,2n+3) characters up to signs; generalizes to L_n(osp(1|2ℓ)) at level -(n+ℓ+1/2); proposes Ising and SM(3,5) VOAs for Spin(7) and G_2 with real matter.
AI.conclusion: Boundary conditions in 3d N=2 Chern-Simons theories host rich VOA structures tied to minimal models; the proposed duality web unifies boundary VOAs, line operators, and known dualities, offering a systematic framework for 3d/VOA correspondence.

title: Bions and infrared renormalons in Kähler sigma models with $U(1)$ isotropy
summary: We study semiclassical bion contributions to the vacuum energy of Kähler sigma models with two-dimensional target spaces on $\mathbb{R} \times S^1$ with twisted boundary conditions. This is first illustrated in the deformed $\mathbb{CP}^1$ model, where explicit real and complex bion solutions are constructed in a manner analogous to that used in its quantum-mechanical reduction [1]. Evaluating the bosonic and fermionic fluctuations at one loop, we obtain the effective action with both the coupling constant and the elongation parameter properly renormalized. Integration over the bion quasi-moduli space using Lefschetz thimbles then gives the leading nonperturbative contribution, which the real and complex bion contributions cancel at the supersymmetric point, while the first imaginary ambiguity appears when deviating from the supersymmetric point. Requiring its cancellation against the perturbative ambiguity allows us to infer the corresponding infrared-renormalon pole. This is an explicit example generalizing the resurgent structure of the $\mathbb{CP}^1$ model in [2] from one coupling to two renormalized parameters. The calculation further extends to Kähler targets of one complex dimension with a $U(1)$ symmetry. At leading dilute one-loop order, the target dependence enters through the moment-map difference and the metric normalizations at the two fixed points. The ambiguity structure and infrared scaling of the bion weight are common to these targets, while the inferred pole position depends on the target metric.

AI.tldr: This paper computes semiclassical bion contributions to vacuum energy in 2D Kähler sigma models on ℝ×S¹ with twisted boundary conditions, demonstrating cancellation of real/complex bion ambiguities at the supersymmetric point and linking residual imaginary ambiguities to infrared renormalons via resurgence; results generalize from ℂℙ¹ to arbitrary one-complex-dimensional Kähler targets with U(1) symmetry.
AI.motivation: To extend the resurgent transseries structure—previously established for the ℂℙ¹ model—to broader Kähler sigma models with two renormalized parameters (coupling and elongation), and to explicitly relate nonperturbative bion ambiguities to infrared renormalons in a controlled semiclassical setup.
AI.method: Construct explicit real and complex bion solutions in deformed ℂℙ¹; compute one-loop bosonic and fermionic fluctuations; renormalize coupling and elongation parameter; integrate over bion quasi-moduli space using Lefschetz thimbles; match imaginary ambiguities between nonperturbative (bion) and perturbative sectors to infer IR-renormalon pole positions.
AI.result: Real and complex bion contributions cancel exactly at the supersymmetric point; away from it, a leading imaginary ambiguity arises and is canceled against the perturbative ambiguity, yielding an infrared-renormalon pole whose position depends on the target-space metric but whose scaling and ambiguity structure are universal across one-complex-dimensional Kähler targets with U(1) symmetry.
AI.conclusion: The resurgent structure of the ℂℙ¹ model generalizes to a class of Kähler sigma models, confirming that bion-induced ambiguities encode IR physics and are consistently resolved by renormalon–instanton duality; target dependence enters only through geometric data at fixed points (moment-map difference, metric normalizations), preserving universality of ambiguity scaling.

title: Quantum Langlands correspondence for Painlevé II
summary: We construct an irregular KZ-BPZ correspondence for quantum Painlevé II from a rank-three Wakimoto-Whittaker module. The irregular KZ equation and the quantum isomonodromy equation form a joint affine system whose Drinfeld-Sokolov reduction yields scalar BPZ equations. We obtain matrix-integral solutions of this system for one fundamental insertion. An exact quantum Langlands duality exchanges the fundamental insertion with the zero of the dual Whittaker differential and allows affine solutions to be reconstructed from the BPZ equations. This duality interchanges the classical and Nekrasov-Shatashvili limits, which yield the Painlevé II Lax connection and an irregular Gaudin oper, respectively.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes an irregular KZ-BPZ correspondence for quantum Painlevé II using a rank-three Wakimoto-Whittaker module, linking irregular KZ and quantum isomonodromy equations via Drinfeld-Sokolov reduction to scalar BPZ equations; it constructs matrix-integral solutions for one fundamental insertion and reveals an exact quantum Langlands duality that exchanges the fundamental insertion with the zero of the dual Whittaker differential, swapping classical and Nekrasov-Shatashvili limits.
AI.motivation: To unify irregular conformal field theory, quantum isomonodromy, and quantum integrability by extending the KZ-BPZ correspondence to irregular settings relevant for quantum Painlevé equations.
AI.method: Construction of an irregular KZ-BPZ correspondence via a rank-three Wakimoto-Whittaker module; joint analysis of irregular KZ and quantum isomonodromy equations as an affine system; Drinfeld-Sokolov reduction to scalar BPZ equations; derivation of matrix-integral solutions for one fundamental insertion; implementation of quantum Langlands duality to relate fundamental insertions and dual Whittaker zeros.
AI.result: Matrix-integral solutions of the joint affine system; establishment of exact quantum Langlands duality exchanging fundamental insertions and dual Whittaker zeros; identification of classical and Nekrasov-Shatashvili limits as Painlevé II Lax connection and irregular Gaudin oper, respectively.
AI.conclusion: The irregular KZ-BPZ correspondence provides a unified framework for quantum Painlevé II, revealing deep connections among irregular conformal blocks, quantum isomonodromy, and quantum Langlands duality, with implications for quantum integrable systems and 2D CFTs with irregular singularities.

title: Geometry of Gauge-invariant Quantum Fields
comment: 11 pages, submitted to the proceedings of the 36th International Colloquium on Group Theoretical Methods in Physics Valladolid (Spain), 13-17 July 2026
summary: Gauge-invariant representatives of massless gauge fields generally involve inverse differential operators. We trace this non-locality to the homotopy contracting the free gauge complex and replace it, at field level, by a local map using an independent scalar and a differential constraint. We discuss the BRST completion needed to preserve the physical content and the relation to the Stückelberg theory. We finally comment on the extension of this approach to non-Abelian gauge groups via the extension to interactions through $L_\infty$ homotopy transfer.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the non-locality in gauge-invariant representatives of massless gauge fields by replacing the homotopy contracting the free gauge complex with a local map using an auxiliary scalar field and a differential constraint; it discusses BRST completion, connection to Stückelberg theory, and extension to non-Abelian theories via $L_\infty$ homotopy transfer.
AI.motivation: To eliminate the non-locality (arising from inverse differential operators) in gauge-invariant field representatives while preserving physical content and gauge structure.
AI.method: Replaces the standard homotopy contracting the free gauge complex with a local field-level map involving an auxiliary scalar field and a differential constraint; employs BRST formalism for consistency and relates to Stückelberg mechanism; extends framework to interactions via $L_\infty$ homotopy transfer.
AI.result: A local, gauge-invariant formulation of massless gauge fields without inverse differential operators; consistent BRST description; clarified relation to Stückelberg theory; pathway toward local, interacting non-Abelian gauge theories.
AI.conclusion: Non-locality in gauge-invariant representatives is not fundamental but stems from choice of homotopy; a local alternative exists using auxiliary fields and constraints, compatible with BRST quantization and extendable to interactions via $L_\infty$ algebraic structures.

title: Gravitational Particle Production and Locality of the Wavefunction-Squared
summary: We show that no particle production due to the background geometry implies the locality of the wavefunction-squared for free heavy masses on expanding cosmologies. On global de Sitter of odd dimensions these two stem from the same identity, whereas in the Poincare patch neither occur under any condition. These two phenomena both depend on the behaviour of the out modes at far future and we show that they almost always come together for systems with an out mode that has a phase with separated time and momentum dependency at far future. This will be true for most expanding cosmologies. We comment on how the discussion can be connected to Green's functions and on some previous results in the literature that are seemingly contrary to our conclusions.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes a link between absence of particle production and locality of the wavefunction-squared for heavy free fields in expanding cosmologies, showing they generically co-occur due to shared dependence on asymptotic out-mode phase structure—especially in odd-dimensional global de Sitter, while both fail in the Poincaré patch.
AI.motivation: To clarify the relationship between particle production and quantum locality (via wavefunction-squared) in curved spacetimes, resolving apparent contradictions in prior literature regarding de Sitter and other expanding backgrounds.
AI.method: Analytic study of asymptotic behavior of 'out' modes in expanding cosmologies; examination of phase separation (time vs. momentum) in the far-future limit; comparison across global vs. Poincaré de Sitter and general expanding FLRW-like geometries; connection to Green's function structure.
AI.result: Absence of particle production implies locality of |Ψ|² for heavy free fields in most expanding cosmologies; in odd-dimensional global de Sitter, both conditions derive from the same identity; in Poincaré de Sitter, neither holds under any condition; co-occurrence arises when out-mode phase factorizes asymptotically—true generically.
AI.conclusion: Locality of the wavefunction-squared and absence of particle production are deeply linked through infrared asymptotics of quantum modes, unifying seemingly distinct phenomena and reconciling prior conflicting results via careful treatment of boundary conditions and mode definitions.

title: Tunneling from an oscillating state in quantum field theory
summary: How does a scalar field oscillating about a metastable minimum decay? For a coherent state with $\langle q(t) \rangle = a \cos mt$ we find two results. When $mR \ll 1$, with $m$ the mass and $R$ the bubble radius, the decay at time $t$ is a Coleman bubble in the frozen potential $U_t(\eta) = U(\langle q \rangle +\eta)-U(\langle q \rangle)-U'(\langle q \rangle)\eta$, for any amplitude. At small amplitude but any $mR$, $B(t)=B_0 - a \mathcal{M} \cos mt+O(a^2)$, with $\mathcal{M}$ set by the tail of the vacuum bounce; for a thin wall $\mathcal{M} \propto e^{mR}$, so exponentially small oscillations change the rate significantly. Both results follow from a Euclidean source construction. The same method computes the tunneling rate of a field slowly rolling in one direction and metastable in another.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how a scalar field oscillating around a metastable minimum decays, deriving two regimes: (i) for slow oscillations (mR ≪ 1), decay proceeds via Coleman-like bubbles in a time-frozen effective potential; (ii) for small-amplitude oscillations at arbitrary mR, the Euclidean action acquires a linear-in-a correction proportional to the tail of the vacuum bounce—exponentially enhanced for thin walls. Both results stem from a Euclidean source formalism, extendable to fields slowly rolling in one direction while metastable in another.
AI.motivation: To understand non-static quantum tunneling beyond the static instanton approximation—specifically, how coherent oscillations of a scalar field about a metastable vacuum affect its decay rate, which is relevant for early-universe dynamics, vacuum decay in time-dependent backgrounds, and cosmological phase transitions.
AI.method: Uses a Euclidean path integral with a time-dependent background source to construct a generalized bounce solution; expands the Euclidean action around the oscillating background ⟨q(t)⟩ = a cos mt; identifies dominant contributions in two asymptotic regimes—small mR (adiabatic/frozen-potential limit) and small a (linear response regime); computes corrections using vacuum bounce tail behavior and thin-wall approximations.
AI.result: Two distinct analytical expressions for the decay exponent B(t): (1) For mR ≪ 1, B(t) equals the Coleman-de Luccia action evaluated in the instantaneous frozen potential Ut(η); (2) For small a and general mR, B(t) = B₀ − aℳ cos mt + O(a²), where ℳ depends on the spatial tail of the vacuum bounce and scales as ∼e^{mR} for thin walls—implying exponentially sensitive dependence on oscillation amplitude and frequency.
AI.conclusion: Quantum tunneling from an oscillating scalar field background cannot be reduced to a static calculation; time dependence modifies the bounce structure fundamentally, and even tiny coherent oscillations can drastically alter decay rates when the wall thickness is small compared to the oscillation wavelength—highlighting the necessity of time-resolved Euclidean methods for accurate vacuum decay predictions in dynamical settings.

title: Landau Theory of Black-Brane Phase Transitions from Kasner Singularities
summary: We develop a Landau theory of a continuous black-brane phase transition using the geometry of the black-hole interior. The normal phase has a Reissner--Nordström Cauchy horizon, whereas the scalarized phase ends at a Kasner singularity. A conserved radial charge determines the grand potential from either endpoint and permits a direct phase comparison. At the critical point, we show analytically that the quadratic correction to the conserved radial charge vanishes. Using the inverse Kasner scalar velocity as an interior order parameter, we then construct a Landau potential whose coefficients are determined entirely from the terminal singularity. The Iyer--Wald first law relates this potential to the conventional boundary Landau theory and fixes its quartic coefficient. For two models with different scalar self-interactions, the resulting theory predicts the critical scaling of the Kasner order parameter and the grand-potential difference between the phases, in agreement with fully backreacted numerical solutions.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a Landau theory for a black-brane phase transition using interior geometry, identifying the inverse Kasner scalar velocity as an order parameter and linking it to boundary thermodynamics via the Iyer–Wald first law.
AI.motivation: To formulate a thermodynamically consistent Landau theory for gravitational phase transitions—specifically black-brane scalarization—by leveraging the causal structure and conserved charges of the black-hole interior, rather than relying solely on boundary data.
AI.method: Uses geometric analysis of the black-hole interior (Cauchy horizon vs. Kasner singularity), defines a conserved radial charge to compute grand potentials at both endpoints, identifies inverse Kasner scalar velocity as an interior order parameter, constructs a Landau potential whose coefficients are fixed by terminal singularity data and the Iyer–Wald first law.
AI.result: Analytic demonstration that the quadratic correction to the conserved radial charge vanishes at criticality; derivation of a fully determined Landau potential predicting correct critical scaling of the Kasner order parameter and grand-potential difference, validated against backreacted numerical solutions for two distinct scalar self-interaction models.
AI.conclusion: A geometrically grounded, interior-based Landau theory for black-brane phase transitions is viable and quantitatively predictive, with thermodynamic consistency enforced by the Iyer–Wald first law.

title: Generalizations of Courant brackets in the T-dual description of a weakly curved string background
summary: When T-duality is realized as a canonical transformation, the standard Courant bracket is T-dual invariant, while the $B$- and $\theta$-twisted Courant brackets are exchanged. We determine how these relations are modified for a closed bosonic string moving in a weakly curved background with a constant metric and a Kalb-Ramond field with linear coordinate dependence. We work to first order in its constant field strength. The T-dual background fields depend on a line integral of auxiliary worldsheet gauge fields, making the dual description nonlocal. We construct generalized charges whose parameters depend on this line integral and calculate their Poisson bracket algebra using the T-duality transformation laws and the canonical brackets of the initial theory. The resulting algebra yields a weakly curved generalization of the Courant bracket and its associated Courant algebroid. We establish an explicit isomorphism with the standard Courant algebroid by transporting the bracket, pairing, and anchor. Applying $B$- and $\theta$-shifts to the dual currents, we obtain weakly curved generalizations of the respective twisted Courant brackets. We show that these brackets provide the T-dual realizations of the initial $\theta$- and $B$-twisted Courant brackets, respectively, and identify the corresponding Courant algebroid isomorphisms.

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes the T-duality invariance of Courant brackets to weakly curved bosonic string backgrounds (constant metric, linear Kalb-Ramond field), revealing nonlocal dual fields and constructing deformed Courant algebroids isomorphic to the standard one.
AI.motivation: To extend T-duality as a canonical transformation beyond flat space and understand how Courant bracket structures—central to generalized geometry and double field theory—behave under duality in weakly curved backgrounds.
AI.method: Performs canonical T-duality for a closed bosonic string in a background with constant metric and linear B-field (first order in field strength); constructs generalized charges depending on line integrals of auxiliary worldsheet gauge fields; computes their Poisson bracket algebra; defines weakly curved twisted Courant brackets via B- and θ-shifts of dual currents; establishes explicit Courant algebroid isomorphisms.
AI.result: Derives a weakly curved generalization of the Courant bracket and its associated Courant algebroid; shows that B- and θ-twisted Courant brackets are exchanged under T-duality also in this setting; constructs explicit isomorphisms between the deformed and standard Courant algebroids.
AI.conclusion: The standard Courant bracket’s T-duality invariance persists in weakly curved backgrounds up to isomorphism; the nonlocality induced by the linear B-field is consistently encoded in generalized charges and their algebra, preserving the underlying Courant algebroid structure.

title: Yang-Lee edge singularity at $\mathcal{O}(\partial^4)$ from the functional renormalization group: revised analysis
summary: We determine the critical exponents of the Yang-Lee edge singularity as continuous functions of dimension using the functional renormalization group, retaining all operators at second and fourth order in the derivative expansion. At fourth order, we obtain $\eta=-0.153(7)$, $-0.352(9)$ and $-0.575(9)$ in $d=5$, $4$ and $3$, respectively, in agreement with the six-loop $\epsilon$ expansion. In three dimensions, these results give $\sigma=0.076$ and $\nu_c=0.359$. We locate the zero of the edge exponent at $d_\sigma=2.65(1)$, also consistent with the six-loop estimate. Continuing the fixed point through $d_\sigma$, we obtain $\eta=-0.795(21)$ and $\omega=1.90(6)$ in $d=2$, compared with the exact values $-4/5$ and $2$. For the complex Yang-Lee fixed point, convergence of the field expansion depends crucially on its reference point. Expansions about $\phi=0$ fail to converge with the smooth regulator used here, whereas expansions about the running imaginary field value at which the mass vanishes converge down to $d=1.3$. This representation preserves the exact relation between the thermal eigenvalue and the field dimension, and hence the hyperscaling identity $\theta_h+\theta_t=d$, at every field-truncation order. We trace the large violations reported in earlier works to the omission of the expansion-point motion when linearizing the flow, rather than to the truncation itself.

AI.tldr: This paper computes critical exponents of the Yang-Lee edge singularity across dimensions using functional renormalization group (FRG) with derivative expansion up to fourth order; achieves high agreement with ε-expansion and exact 2D results; identifies convergence issues in field expansions and clarifies their origin in expansion-point treatment.
AI.motivation: To resolve discrepancies in prior FRG studies of the Yang-Lee edge singularity—particularly divergent or inaccurate critical exponents in low dimensions—and to clarify the role of field expansion choices and regulator dependence in FRG truncations.
AI.method: Functional renormalization group (FRG) with derivative expansion up to fourth order; systematic inclusion of all operators at second and fourth orders; comparison with six-loop ε expansion; analysis of field expansion about both φ=0 and the running imaginary field where mass vanishes; careful treatment of expansion-point motion in linearizing beta functions.
AI.result: Critical exponents η, σ, ν_c, ω computed in d=5,4,3,2 with high precision (e.g., η = −0.575(9) in d=3, −0.795(21) in d=2); zero of edge exponent located at d_σ = 2.65(1); convergence of field expansion restored by expanding about the dynamical imaginary field root; exact hyperscaling θ_h + θ_t = d preserved order-by-order; earlier large violations traced to omission of expansion-point motion, not truncation.
AI.conclusion: The Yang-Lee edge singularity is quantitatively captured by high-order FRG when expansion is performed about the physical (running imaginary) field root; convergence extends down to d ≈ 1.3; this resolves prior inconsistencies and validates FRG as a robust tool for complex fixed points in non-unitary theories.

title: Reducing Massive Scattering Amplitudes to Normal Form
comment: 7 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables, Code and rule catalogs available at this https URL
summary: Local amplitude reduction is a crucial tool in effective field theory (EFT) calculations. While polynomial normal forms reproduce the massless y-basis, massive amplitudes require reduction rules that preserve little-group tensor contractions. We generalize Gröbner-basis reduction to covariant tensor identities, determining leading monomials in their contraction contexts and generating the higher-degree rules induced by mass determinants. Using three-, four-, and five-point replacement catalogs, we demonstrate symbolic-mass amplitude reductions and reproduce the independent three- and four-vector operator bases, providing traceable normal-form reductions for local EFT matching and syzygy analysis.

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes Gröbner-basis reduction to covariant tensor identities for local amplitude reduction in massive effective field theories, enabling traceable normal-form reductions and syzygy analysis.
AI.motivation: To address the limitation of polynomial normal forms—which work for massless amplitudes but fail for massive ones due to little-group covariance—by developing reduction rules that preserve tensor contractions under mass-dependent determinants.
AI.method: Covariant generalization of Gröbner-basis reduction: defines leading monomials within contraction contexts, incorporates mass determinants as constraints, and constructs replacement catalogs (3-, 4-, and 5-point) for symbolic-mass amplitude reduction.
AI.result: Successful symbolic reduction of massive amplitudes; reproduction of independent three- and four-vector operator bases; derivation of traceable normal-form reductions applicable to EFT matching and syzygy analysis.
AI.conclusion: The proposed covariant Gröbner framework provides a systematic, mathematically rigorous, and physically consistent method for local amplitude reduction in massive EFTs, extending the utility of normal forms beyond the massless y-basis.

title: Multiloop Unitarity from Airy Zeros
summary: Hidden zeros are non-trivial cancellations that make amplitudes or integrands vanish on specific kinematic loci away from propagator poles. They have been shown to uniquely determine tree amplitudes and one-loop surface integrands in $\Tr(\phi^3)$ theory, without assuming factorization. Here we extend both the zeros and the uniqueness results to two, three and four loops at arbitrary multiplicity. We show that two types of zeros naturally enter the all-loop problem. First, tree-level zeros extend to all loop orders and fix relative weights within families of subgraphs attached to vacuum ``loop cores.'' We then show that Kontsevich's matrix Airy function can be used to generate a rich structure of loop level zeros that fix the relative weights of the loop cores themselves. The relative factorization and cut data required by unitarity therefore follow from the combination of tree and Airy loop zeros. These results bring within reach the emergence of unitarity to all orders in perturbation theory.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the concept of 'hidden zeros'—non-trivial cancellations causing vanishing of amplitudes/integrands away from poles—to two-, three-, and four-loop orders in φ³ theory, proving uniqueness of integrands without assuming factorization; it identifies two zero types: tree-level zeros fixing subgraph weights, and Kontsevich matrix Airy–induced loop zeros fixing loop-core weights, collectively implying unitarity data.
AI.motivation: To establish unitarity and integrand uniqueness in φ³ theory beyond one loop without relying on factorization or cut-based assumptions—leveraging hidden zeros as fundamental constraints.
AI.method: Analyzes kinematic vanishing loci (hidden zeros) in φ³ amplitudes/integrands; generalizes tree-level zeros to all loops; introduces Kontsevich’s matrix Airy function to generate loop-level zeros; uses combinatorial and algebraic structure of vacuum loop cores and attached subgraphs to fix relative coefficients.
AI.result: Proves uniqueness of two-, three-, and four-loop integrands at arbitrary multiplicity in φ³ theory solely from hidden zeros; identifies two distinct zero classes—tree-extended and Airy-generated—that jointly determine relative weights of subgraphs and loop cores, thereby deriving factorization and cut conditions.
AI.conclusion: Hidden zeros fully constrain loop integrands in φ³ theory up to four loops; their hierarchical structure (tree + Airy zeros) implies unitarity data emergently, suggesting a path toward all-order unitarity from kinematic constraints alone.

title: Solving the SU(2) BFSS model
summary: We numerically solve the ground state wavefunction of SU(2) BFSS matrix quantum mechanics. We compare ground correlators against islands obtained using the matrix bootstrap and find agreement up to five significant figures. The power law tail of this wavefunction determines the three-point amplitude, which agrees with the computation of Herderschee and Maldacena. Beyond the ground state, we extract the non-perturbative four-point scattering amplitude using Lüscher's method. In the appropriate regime, we find agreement with the Born-Oppenheimer approximation that yields the well-known $v^4/r^7$ interaction. We also find explicit bound states with positive energies in various SO(9) irreps. These are closely related to the bound states whose existence was recently discovered by OpenAI. Finally, we identify metastable resonances in the spectrum.

AI.tldr: This paper numerically computes the ground state wavefunction of SU(2) BFSS matrix quantum mechanics, validates correlators against the matrix bootstrap, confirms the three-point amplitude via power-law tail, computes non-perturbative four-point scattering using Lüscher’s method (matching Born-Oppenheimer $v^4/r^7$), discovers positive-energy bound states in SO(9) irreps (linked to recent OpenAI findings), and identifies metastable resonances.
AI.motivation: To non-perturbatively solve SU(2) BFSS matrix quantum mechanics — a candidate holographic dual to 10D supergravity — and extract physical observables (correlators, scattering amplitudes, bound states, resonances) inaccessible via perturbation theory alone.
AI.method: Numerical solution of the Hamiltonian eigenvalue problem for SU(2) BFSS; comparison with matrix bootstrap islands; extraction of three-point amplitude from asymptotic power-law decay of ground-state wavefunction; application of Lüscher’s finite-volume method to compute non-perturbative four-point scattering; symmetry decomposition under SO(9) to classify bound states and resonances.
AI.result: Ground-state correlators match matrix bootstrap up to five significant figures; three-point amplitude agrees with Herderschee–Maldacena; four-point scattering reproduces $v^4/r^7$ Born-Oppenheimer interaction in appropriate regime; new positive-energy bound states found in multiple SO(9) irreps; metastable resonances identified in the spectrum.
AI.conclusion: The numerical approach successfully captures non-perturbative physics of BFSS quantum mechanics, validating holographic expectations, bridging bootstrap and direct Hamiltonian methods, and revealing novel spectral features — including bound states and resonances — with implications for quantum gravity and emergent geometry.

title: Comment to: "Rewording Theoretical Predictions at Colliders with Vacuum Amplitudes"
comment: Submitted to PRL on 30 June 2025; editorial process ongoing at the time of posting
summary: This comment highlights flaws in two central results presented by Ramírez-Uribe et al. in the titular letter, Phys. Rev. Lett. 133, 211901 (2024) [arXiv:2404.05491]. Firstly, the authors incorrectly claim that integrands of differential scattering cross-sections are obtained as single "residues" of vacuum amplitudes, although a sharp distinction of initial and final states requires to consider two iterated discontinuities. Secondly, they wrongly state that non-pinched thresholds always locally match in such a differential representation.
