AI.tldr: This comment identifies two critical errors in Ramírez-Uribe et al.'s PRL letter: (1) misidentifying differential cross-section integrands as single residues instead of requiring two iterated discontinuities for proper initial/final state separation; and (2) erroneously asserting local matching of non-pinched thresholds in the differential representation.
AI.motivation: To correct fundamental conceptual and mathematical errors in the interpretation of vacuum amplitudes and threshold behavior in differential scattering cross-sections, as presented in Ramírez-Uribe et al.'s recent PRL letter.
AI.method: Critical analytical examination of the derivation and interpretation of differential scattering cross-sections from vacuum amplitudes, focusing on the proper use of analytic continuation, discontinuities, and threshold structure in quantum field theory.
AI.result: Demonstration that the claimed residue-based identification of integrands is invalid without two iterated discontinuities, and that non-pinched thresholds do not generally exhibit local matching in the asserted differential representation.
AI.conclusion: The two central results in Ramírez-Uribe et al.'s letter are mathematically and physically unjustified due to misapplication of complex analysis and threshold kinematics in scattering theory.

title: Off-shell continuation from on-shell recursion
summary: Starting from on-shell factorization and the polarization sum of an internal massive vector, we provide an off-shell continuation of the transverse and longitudinal contributions defined at arbitrary virtuality. The construction relies on on-shell constructibility and the three-point off-shell current constraint $p \cdot J = O(m)$. For amplitudes with external longitudinal vectors, we develop a method that isolates the mass-singular contributions associated with the longitudinal polarization, namely terms with power-law singularities in the massless limit. In the examples studied, these terms appear as contact contributions in individual factorization channels, and we identify the conditions under which they cancel. We give an independent understanding, based on massive on-shell amplitudes, of the polarization decomposition and diagram-by-diagram high-energy power counting underlying the Feynman-Diagram gauge and related five-component formulations. We further clarify how higher-point current constraints can emerge from on-shell constructibility and the cancellation of mass singularities. We illustrate the mechanism with explicit four-point examples and discuss the constraints imposed by a smooth massless limit. The work provides a systematic bottom-up method for building massive amplitudes free of mass-singular terms and opens a route toward a broader amplitude-based understanding of field decompositions, connecting massive and massless descriptions and on-shell states with off-shell descriptions.

AI.tldr: This paper develops an on-shell, off-shell continuation of transverse/longitudal polarization decomposition for massive vectors, isolates and cancels mass-singular terms in longitudinal amplitudes, and establishes connections between massive on-shell amplitudes, Feynman-diagram gauge, five-component formulations, and current constraints—enabling systematic construction of massive amplitudes with smooth massless limits.
AI.motivation: To resolve ambiguities in off-shell extensions of massive vector polarizations, systematically handle mass singularities in longitudinal contributions, and unify massive/massless amplitude descriptions via on-shell constructibility.
AI.method: Uses on-shell factorization and polarization sum of internal massive vectors to define off-shell transverse/longitudinal components; imposes the three-point off-shell current constraint $p \cdot J = O(m)$; isolates mass-singular terms in longitudinal amplitudes as contact contributions per channel; analyzes cancellation conditions; derives higher-point current constraints from on-shell constructibility and singularity cancellation; verifies with explicit four-point examples and smooth massless limit analysis.
AI.result: A consistent off-shell continuation of massive vector polarizations; a diagrammatic criterion for cancellation of power-law mass singularities; clarification of polarization decomposition and high-energy power counting in Feynman-Diagram and five-component gauges; emergence mechanism of higher-point current constraints; explicit demonstration that contact-term singularities cancel across channels in four-point cases under specified kinematic and gauge conditions.
AI.conclusion: On-shell constructibility and current constraints provide a rigorous, bottom-up framework for building massive amplitudes free of unphysical mass singularities, bridging massive/massless formalisms and linking on-shell states to off-shell dynamics in a gauge- and representation-independent way.

title: The KLN theorem meets collinear factorisation: Local Unitarity for hadronic cross-sections
summary: We present an initial-state implementation of the Kinoshita-Lee-Nauenberg (KLN) theorem that is compatible with collinear factorisation. In this formulation, hadronic cross-sections are expressed as convolutions of parton distribution functions with partonic cross-sections obtained by summing over the number of incoming partons. By virtue of the KLN theorem, the partonic cross-sections are infrared finite by construction, without relying on dimensional regularisation as an infrared regulator. The Local Unitarity formalism provides a local realisation of this infrared finiteness, allowing partonic cross-sections to be evaluated directly in four dimensions by Monte Carlo integration. We demonstrate the framework at next-to-leading order and leading power. Using Local Unitarity, we compute the Drell-Yan and $t\bar{t}$ production cross-sections numerically; using Reverse Unitarity, we obtain the deep inelastic scattering and Drell-Yan cross-sections analytically. In all cases, a universal scheme conversion relates our results to those obtained in the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ parton model.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an initial-state implementation of the KLN theorem compatible with collinear factorisation, enabling infrared-finite partonic cross-sections in four dimensions via Local Unitarity; it computes Drell-Yan and tt̄ numerically and DIS/Drell-Yan analytically using Reverse Unitarity, with universal scheme conversion to MS-bar.
AI.motivation: To formulate a physically consistent, infrared-safe framework for hadronic cross-sections that avoids dimensional regularisation while preserving collinear factorisation and enabling direct 4D Monte Carlo evaluation.
AI.method: Develops an initial-state KLN-compliant formulation where hadronic cross-sections are convolutions of PDFs with partonic cross-sections summed over incoming parton multiplicities; employs Local Unitarity for local infrared cancellation and 4D numerical integration (NLO/leading power), and Reverse Unitarity for analytical results; establishes universal scheme conversion to MS-bar.
AI.result: Demonstrates infrared-finite partonic cross-sections without dimensional regularisation; reports numerical NLO results for Drell-Yan and t t̄ production via Local Unitarity, and analytical NLO results for DIS and Drell-Yan via Reverse Unitarity; confirms consistency with MS-bar parton model through universal scheme conversion.
AI.conclusion: The proposed KLN-based framework provides a rigorous, regulator-independent foundation for perturbative QCD calculations in four dimensions, unifying numerical and analytical approaches under a common infrared safety principle and enabling robust, scheme-consistent predictions for collider processes.

title: Challenging the hoop conjecture with spinning pancakes and baguettes
summary: Understanding when gravitational collapse produces a black hole remains a central challenge in general relativity. Black-hole uniqueness results characterize the stationary endpoint under suitable assumptions, while singularity theorems establish geodesic incompleteness in the presence of trapped surfaces and appropriate energy and global conditions. Neither, however, provides a general criterion for horizon formation. The hoop conjecture offers such a criterion by relating the enclosed mass to the compactness of a matter distribution in every direction. We construct axisymmetric families of initial data describing rotating dust and test a formulation of the conjecture adapted to this setting. We explore highly prolate and oblate configurations with both constant and differential rescaled angular-velocity profiles, including configurations near the threshold for apparent-horizon formation. We find that the conjecture holds for rotating configurations, with a coefficient within 14% of unity as in the nonrotating case, provided the quasilocal mass includes the rotational energy. If the irreducible mass of the apparent horizon is used instead, the deviations grow with spin, as they do for Kerr black holes. For horizonless configurations, the conjecture likewise holds when the mass is restricted to the energy enclosed by the matter surface, whereas using the ADM mass, which also includes rotational field energy outside the matter, leads to apparent violations of up to $\approx$25%. We also discuss the possible evolution of compact configurations without apparent horizons, their relation to weak cosmic censorship, and their implications for horizonless compact objects.

AI.tldr: This paper tests the hoop conjecture for axisymmetric rotating dust initial data, finding it holds with ~14% deviation from unity when rotational energy is included in the quasilocal mass; using irreducible mass or ADM mass leads to larger deviations due to spin or field-energy contributions.
AI.motivation: To establish a general, physically intuitive criterion for black hole (apparent horizon) formation in gravitational collapse—beyond stationary uniqueness theorems and singularity theorems—by testing the hoop conjecture in the physically relevant rotating, axisymmetric regime.
AI.method: Constructs axisymmetric initial data families for rotating dust (including prolate/oblate shapes and constant/differential angular-velocity profiles), computes quasilocal masses (with/without rotational energy) and circumferential radii, and evaluates the hoop ratio M/R against apparent-horizon formation thresholds.
AI.result: The hoop conjecture holds robustly for rotating dust when the quasilocal mass includes rotational energy (coefficient ≈ 0.86–1.14); using irreducible mass yields spin-dependent deviations matching Kerr behavior; using ADM mass causes up to ~25% apparent violations for horizonless configurations due to external rotational field energy.
AI.conclusion: The hoop conjecture remains viable as a horizon-formation criterion for rotating matter if rotational energy is properly accounted for in the mass definition; its failure under alternative mass choices reflects physical distinctions between quasilocal, irreducible, and asymptotic masses—not a breakdown of the conjecture itself.

title: Thermal $CP$ dynamics in a four-fermion model: mean-field and functional renormalization group analyses
summary: We investigate a one-flavor four-fermion model with scalar, pseudoscalar, and mixed scalar-pseudoscalar interactions at finite temperature and vanishing chemical potential. Our analysis combines the mean-field approximation, which determines the equilibrium condensates, with the functional renormalization group (FRG), which describes the scale dependence of the interactions and the fermion mass phase. Within the mean-field approach, we find that, in the absence of explicit symmetry-breaking sources, the dominant interaction determines the direction of condensation. In particular, a pseudoscalar condensate spontaneously breaks the ordinary $P/CP$ symmetry and disappears through a continuous thermal phase transition. For regular high-temperature FRG trajectories, the dimensionless mixed coupling tends to zero in the infrared, while its dimensionful counterpart remains finite. Increasing temperature also suppresses the scale evolution of the fermion mass phase. Together, these results clarify the distinct roles of thermal fluctuations in suppressing spontaneous symmetry breaking and fermionic instabilities, without necessarily eliminating explicit symmetry breaking effects.

AI.tldr: This paper studies a one-flavor four-fermion model with scalar, pseudoscalar, and mixed interactions at finite temperature (μ = 0), using mean-field theory and functional renormalization group (FRG) methods. It finds that the dominant interaction dictates condensate direction; pseudoscalar condensation breaks P/CP symmetry and vanishes continuously at high T; FRG shows infrared suppression of dimensionless mixed coupling while its dimensionful version stays finite; thermal fluctuations suppress both SSB and fermionic instabilities but not explicit symmetry breaking.
AI.motivation: To understand how thermal fluctuations affect spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) and fermionic instabilities in chiral-type four-fermion models, particularly disentangling roles of different interaction channels (scalar, pseudoscalar, mixed) and their RG flow under temperature.
AI.method: Combined mean-field approximation (for equilibrium condensates and phase structure) with functional renormalization group (FRG) (to track scale- and temperature-dependent evolution of couplings and fermion mass phase). Analyzed phase transitions, symmetry breaking patterns, and infrared behavior of dimensionful/dimensionless couplings.
AI.result: 1) In mean-field, dominant interaction selects condensate type; pseudoscalar condensate breaks P/CP and undergoes continuous thermal phase transition; 2) FRG shows dimensionless mixed coupling → 0 in IR, while dimensionful version remains finite; 3) Temperature suppresses RG flow of fermion mass phase; 4) Thermal fluctuations suppress SSB and fermionic instabilities independently of explicit symmetry-breaking sources.
AI.conclusion: Thermal fluctuations play distinct, channel-dependent roles: they erase pseudoscalar SSB via continuous transitions, drive mixed couplings to trivial IR fixed points, and damp fermionic RG evolution—yet leave explicit symmetry breaking intact. This clarifies limitations and interplay of mean-field and FRG in finite-T strongly-coupled fermionic systems.

title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
summary: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) are described by second-order tensor perturbations that contain free radiation together with a gauge-dependent response maintained by the scalar source. For a perfect fluid with constant equation of state $0<w<1$, we identify the free radiation with the out-state of the tensor perturbation, assembled from the light-cone residue of kernel functions for each pair of scalar modes. Its amplitudes follow from a classical LSZ-type reduction formula, in terms of the initial data and the light-cone-projected source. We prove a classical equivalence theorem: a redefinition of the tensor perturbation whose late-time shift has power-law envelopes and no tensor-frequency component leaves these amplitudes unchanged. Transformations between intrinsic gauges, whose slice-normal observers and spatial coordinates are fixed by the matter and geometry without an external clock or independent oscillatory dynamics, are redefinitions of this kind, except on resonance surfaces of zero measure. The out-state is therefore the same in all intrinsic gauges, including the standard gauges of cosmological perturbation theory. The late-time Newtonian kernel is then the out-state kernel, which justifies its use for the energy spectrum of the free radiation. In matter domination, the out-state instead separates the free radiation from the static tidal response.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a classical LSZ-type reduction formalism for scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs), identifies the gauge-invariant free radiation component as the 'out-state' of tensor perturbations, proves its invariance under intrinsic gauge transformations (except on measure-zero resonances), and clarifies the physical interpretation of commonly used kernels—e.g., the Newtonian kernel is shown to represent the out-state in radiation domination but separates free radiation from static tidal response in matter domination.
AI.motivation: To resolve the long-standing ambiguity in defining the observable, gauge-invariant gravitational wave signal induced by scalar perturbations—specifically, to isolate the true free radiation component from gauge-dependent, sourced contributions in second-order cosmological perturbation theory.
AI.method: Uses light-cone analysis of second-order tensor perturbations sourced by scalar modes in a perfect fluid with constant equation of state; constructs the 'out-state' via residue extraction from kernel functions on the light cone; applies a classical LSZ-type reduction formula linking asymptotic amplitudes to initial data and light-cone-projected source; proves equivalence under tensor redefinitions with power-law late-time shifts and no tensor-frequency content; analyzes transformations between intrinsic gauges (matter- and geometry-defined slicings).
AI.result: The free radiation component of SIGWs is rigorously identified as the light-cone residue-defined out-state; its amplitude is gauge-invariant across all intrinsic gauges (up to zero-measure resonances); the Newtonian kernel coincides with the out-state kernel in radiation domination, justifying its use for energy spectra, whereas in matter domination it instead isolates free radiation from static tidal fields.
AI.conclusion: The observable SIGW signal—the free radiation—is uniquely defined and gauge-invariant in intrinsic gauges; this provides a solid theoretical foundation for computing and interpreting SIGW energy spectra in cosmological contexts, resolving ambiguities in kernel choice and gauge dependence.

title: Elliptic hypergeometric sum/integrals for orthogonal groups and Seiberg duality on the lens space
summary: We derive new transformation formulas for elliptic hypergeometric sum/integrals associated with the orthogonal groups $\mathrm{SO}(N)$. The sum/integrals are written in terms of the lens elliptic gamma function, which depends on an integer $r\geq 1$ in addition to the usual complex variables, and they reduce to the elliptic hypergeometric integrals of Spiridonov and Vartanov for $r=1$. The derivation uses the $BC_n\leftrightarrow BC_{\tilde n}$ transformation formula proven in our previous paper, together with a duplication formula for the lens elliptic gamma function proven here. The duplication formula takes a different form depending on whether $r$ is even or odd. Physically, the new transformations show that the supersymmetric lens indices on $S^1\times S^3/\mathbb{Z}_r$ of the 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ $\mathrm{SO}(N)$ and $\mathrm{SO}(N_f-N+4)$ gauge theories related by Seiberg duality are equal for odd $r$. For even $r$, where the lens index depends on the global form of the gauge group, they show the equality of the contributions from flat connections whose holonomies lie in a common maximal torus. The $BC_n$ formula itself gives the corresponding statement for the symplectic groups.

AI.tldr: This paper derives new transformation formulas for elliptic hypergeometric sum/integrals associated with SO(N) using the lens elliptic gamma function and a newly proven duplication formula; it establishes equality of supersymmetric lens indices for Seiberg-dual SO(N) theories on S¹×S³/ℤᵣ, distinguishing cases for odd vs. even r, and extends results to symplectic groups via BCₙ duality.
AI.motivation: To extend elliptic hypergeometric integral identities—previously known for r=1 (Spiridonov–Vartanov)—to the lens space setting (r ≥ 1), and to provide rigorous mathematical underpinning for supersymmetric dualities (especially Seiberg duality) on S¹×S³/ℤᵣ in 4d N=1 gauge theories with orthogonal and symplectic gauge groups.
AI.method: Combines the previously established BCₙ ↔ BC_ñ transformation identity with a newly derived duplication formula for the lens elliptic gamma function, whose form depends on the parity of r; applies representation-theoretic and modular properties of lens elliptic special functions to derive transformation laws for SO(N)-type sum/integrals; interprets results physically via supersymmetric lens index computations.
AI.result: New transformation formulas for SO(N)-associated elliptic hypergeometric sum/integrals expressed in terms of the lens elliptic gamma function; proof of a parity-dependent duplication formula for that function; confirmation that Seiberg-dual SO(N) and SO(N_f−N+4) theories have equal lens indices on S¹×S³/ℤᵣ for odd r; for even r, equality holds only between contributions from flat connections with holonomies in a common maximal torus; analogous statements established for symplectic groups via BCₙ duality.
AI.conclusion: The work unifies and generalizes elliptic hypergeometric identities to the lens space context, provides exact non-perturbative tests of Seiberg duality for orthogonal and symplectic gauge theories on orbifolded spacetimes, and reveals subtle dependence of dualities on the global structure of the gauge group and the orbifold parameter r.

title: Three Dimensional Structure of Pion with One Dynamical Gluon in the Light-Cone Quark Model
summary: We study the three-dimensional structure of the pion beyond the leading Fock state by including a dynamical gluon, $|\pi\rangle=|q\bar q\rangle+|q\bar q g\rangle$. Within the light-cone quark model, we calculate the pion GPDs, TMDs, and PDFs from light-front wave function overlaps, using a modified Brodsky--Huang--Lepage wave function with the Melosh--Wigner rotation for the valence sector and the light-front quark--gluon vertex for the $q\bar q g$ sector. The quark-number and momentum sum rules are satisfied without additional constraints. We further obtain the electromagnetic form factor and the mass decomposition. After NLO evolution, we compare the PDFs with pion-induced Drell--Yan, $J/\psi$, $\Upsilon$, and HERA leading-neutron $F_2^\pi$ data. The $q\bar q g$ sector contributes little to Drell--Yan but becomes important for gluon-sensitive observables such as $J/\psi$ production and the pion structure function at small $x$.

AI.tldr: This paper computes pion generalized parton distributions (GPDs), transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (TMDs), and parton distribution functions (PDFs) using a light-front wave function incorporating both valence $q\bar q$ and Fock $q\bar q g$ components; it satisfies sum rules, yields electromagnetic form factor and mass decomposition, and shows the $q\bar q g$ sector is negligible in Drell–Yan but crucial for gluon-sensitive processes like $J/\psi$ production and small-$x$ structure.
AI.motivation: To go beyond the leading $q\bar q$ Fock state and systematically assess the role of dynamical gluons ($|q\bar q g\rangle$) in the 3D partonic structure of the pion—particularly for gluon-sensitive observables where valence-only models fail.
AI.method: Light-cone quark model with modified Brodsky–Huang–Lepage wave function for $|q\bar q\rangle$, Melosh–Wigner rotation for spin effects, and light-front $q\bar q g$ vertex for the $|q\bar q g\rangle$ sector; GPDs/TMDs/PDFs computed via light-front wave function overlaps; NLO QCD evolution applied for phenomenological comparison.
AI.result: Satisfies quark-number and momentum sum rules without ad hoc constraints; obtains pion electromagnetic form factor and mass decomposition; $q\bar q g$ contribution is small in Drell–Yan but significant for $J/\psi$, $\Upsilon$, and small-$x$ HERA $F_2^\pi$ data.
AI.conclusion: The $|q\bar q g\rangle$ Fock component is essential for a consistent, QCD-motivated description of gluon-sensitive pion observables and small-$x$ structure, validating the necessity of multi-parton Fock states in light-front hadron structure.

title: Assessing the expressive power of a gauge-invariant PEPS ansatz across a topological phase transition
summary: We investigate the expressive power of the gauged Gaussian fermionic projected entangled pair state (GGFPEPS) ansatz, which is a manifestly gauge-invariant tensor network ansatz for $(2+1)$-dimensional lattice gauge theories. In the GGFPEPS ansatz, the gauge field on each link is represented by coupling its configuration to the fermion number of virtual fermions placed at both ends of the link. This ansatz has been studied by variational Monte Carlo (VMC) methods in previous work~\cite{Emonts:2022yom}. However, the statistical error of VMC makes a precise determination of the variational parameters difficult, so that the expressive power of the ansatz could not be examined accurately. In this work, we reformulate the computation as a Grassmann tensor network (TN), in which the whole network is contracted deterministically, and introduce the higher-order tensor renormalization group (HOTRG), which allows us to perform calculations in large volumes up to $L=34$. We also evaluate the infinite volume system using the corner transfer matrix renormalization group (CTMRG). We find that the ansatz with only eight complex variational parameters accurately describes the pure $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory including the region of the topological phase transition, not only in the energy but also in the topological entanglement entropy. The critical coupling obtained from the peaks of their susceptibilities agrees quantitatively with the one predicted by continuous-time quantum Monte Carlo simulations~\cite{wu2012phase}. Furthermore, near the transition point, we show that the ansatz represents a state outside the plaquette product family, which is a one-parameter family of states assumed in the construction of the ansatz as a simple interpolation between the strong and weak coupling limits.

AI.tldr: This paper reformulates the GGFPEPS ansatz for Z₂ lattice gauge theory as a deterministic Grassmann tensor network, enabling precise evaluation via HOTRG and CTMRG; it demonstrates that just eight complex parameters accurately capture both energy and topological entanglement entropy across the phase transition—including critical coupling matching QMC—and reveals the ansatz accesses states beyond its built-in plaquette-product family.
AI.motivation: To overcome statistical errors in prior variational Monte Carlo studies of the gauge-invariant GGFPEPS ansatz and enable precise, deterministic assessment of its expressive power—particularly for topological properties and phase transitions in (2+1)D Z₂ lattice gauge theory.
AI.method: Reformulates GGFPEPS as a Grassmann tensor network; applies deterministic contraction via higher-order tensor renormalization group (HOTRG) for finite systems up to L=34 and corner transfer matrix renormalization group (CTMRG) for infinite-volume limits; computes energy, topological entanglement entropy, and susceptibility peaks.
AI.result: GGFPEPS with only eight complex variational parameters accurately reproduces ground-state energy and topological entanglement entropy across the Z₂ gauge theory phase diagram, including the topological phase transition; critical coupling from susceptibility peaks matches continuous-time QMC; ansatz generates states outside the assumed plaquette-product family near criticality.
AI.conclusion: The GGFPEPS ansatz is highly expressive—not merely interpolating between strong/weak coupling limits—but capable of capturing universal critical and topological features of (2+1)D Z₂ gauge theory with minimal parameters, validating its use for non-perturbative quantum simulation of gauge theories.

title: Lattice Hamiltonians for Chiral Gauge Theories
comment: 6 pages + 2 pages End Matter + 17 pages appendices, 3 figures, 4 tables
summary: We present a lattice Hamiltonian for chiral gauge theories on the boundary of a slab. The formulation is gauge-fixed, so the gauge variables are the physical modes of the boundary field, and Gauss's law holds exactly. The bulk gauge field is determined by the boundary field and an integer label, which is the topological charge that the boundary generates and the bulk stores as a localized instanton. The bulk enters as a dielectric, and both gauge anomaly conditions become the question of whether the boundary satisfies Gauss's law on its own. For background gauge fields, we show that sectors that differ by a unit of bulk charge are degenerate after Pauli-Villars subtraction and the mirror fermions decouple. The boundary theory has no vacuum angle. Every term in the Hamiltonian is defined in terms of the boundary gauge variables, the integer label and the fermion modes, a starting point for quantum circuit construction.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a lattice Hamiltonian for chiral gauge theories on the boundary of a slab, where the gauge field is fully determined by boundary degrees of freedom and a topological integer label (bulk instanton charge); Gauss's law holds exactly on the boundary, anomalies reduce to boundary consistency conditions, mirror fermions decouple after Pauli-Villars regularization, and the construction is fully expressed in terms of physical boundary variables—enabling quantum circuit implementation.
AI.motivation: To formulate chiral gauge theories on the lattice without doubling or anomaly-induced inconsistencies, by leveraging bulk-boundary correspondence and topological storage of instanton charge in a gapped bulk dielectric.
AI.method: Constructs a gauge-fixed lattice Hamiltonian where boundary gauge variables are physical, bulk gauge field is reconstructed from boundary data plus an integer topological label; imposes exact Gauss's law on boundary; analyzes anomaly cancellation via Pauli-Villars regularization and mirror fermion decoupling in background fields; verifies absence of vacuum angle and locality in boundary variables.
AI.result: A consistent, anomaly-free, gauge-fixed lattice Hamiltonian for chiral gauge theories with exact Gauss's law, topologically labeled bulk instantons, decoupled mirror fermions post-regularization, no theta-vacuum, and full expressibility in boundary-local operators—suitable for quantum simulation.
AI.conclusion: Chiral gauge theories can be consistently realized on the lattice via a topologically enriched boundary theory coupled to a trivial bulk dielectric; anomaly cancellation reduces to boundary Gauss-law consistency, enabling a quantum-computational formulation free of fermion doubling and unphysical degrees of freedom.

title: Non-singular cosmology from effective LQG-inspired black holes
summary: We propose a non-singular primordial cosmology derived from matching an effective Loop Quantum Gravity-inspired black hole geometry to an expanding Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker universe via Darmois-Israel junction conditions. The resulting modified Friedmann equation replaces the singularity with a quantum bounce in the Planckian regime. Mapping the surface energy-momentum tensor of the dynamic thin shell onto a homogeneous scalar field reveals a transient phantom-like behavior. For any equation of state of the shell satisfying $\omega > -1$, its effective energy density is diluted with cosmic expansion. Extending the framework to a two-scalar-field system provides a mechanism to bridge the energy gap between the Planckian bounce and the sub-Planckian scale. The pre-inflationary phase is brief, enabling the second scalar field to take over to drive the standard slow-roll inflation.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a non-singular early-universe model by matching a Loop Quantum Gravity-inspired black hole geometry to an FLRW universe via junction conditions, yielding a quantum bounce instead of a singularity; the thin-shell’s effective stress-energy maps to a transient phantom scalar field, and a two-field extension enables a smooth transition from Planck-scale bounce to standard slow-roll inflation.
AI.motivation: To resolve the initial singularity problem in classical cosmology by constructing a physically viable, non-singular primordial cosmology grounded in quantum gravity (specifically LQG-inspired geometry) and consistent with general relativistic matching conditions.
AI.method: Applies Darmois-Israel junction conditions to glue a spherically symmetric, non-singular black hole interior (LQG-motivated) to an expanding FLRW exterior; derives the modified Friedmann equation; interprets the induced shell stress-energy tensor as an effective homogeneous scalar field; extends the model to two coupled scalar fields to bridge energy scales.
AI.result: A singularity-free cosmological model featuring a quantum bounce at Planckian density; emergence of transient phantom-like scalar dynamics from the junction shell; successful realization of a short pre-inflationary phase followed by standard slow-roll inflation driven by a second scalar field.
AI.conclusion: Junction-based matching of quantum-gravity-inspired geometries with FLRW cosmology yields a self-consistent, non-singular early-universe scenario that naturally incorporates a quantum bounce and transitions smoothly into inflation, offering a phenomenologically viable alternative to the Big Bang singularity.

title: Renormalized dynamical tidal response of neutron stars in binary dynamics
summary: We present the relativistic dynamical tidal response of a neutron star computed using stellar perturbation theory and matched to a worldline effective field theory via the tidal scattering phase. This phase is defined as the difference between the Compton/Raman scattering phase of gravitational-waves from a neutron star and the real part of the black hole scattering phase. The gravitational corrections to the response function are obtained using self-energy corrections up to fourth post-Minkowskian order. The response function for neutron stars obeying the BSk22 equation-of-state from Brussels-Skyrme family, is then consistently matched to an effective theory of relativistic quadrupolar harmonic oscillators to model the fundamental-mode ($f$-mode) and low-frequency gravity-modes ($g$-modes). This matching includes the frequency and tidal coupling of each mode and the post-adiabatic dynamical tidal Love number, and once matched this model is in excellent agreement with the full neutron star response. With the external tidal field up to third post-Newtonian order, we also analyse the tidal coupling of the induced quadrupole on the neutron star in a circular binary system, and the adiabatic binding energy.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the relativistic dynamical tidal response of neutron stars using stellar perturbation theory matched to a worldline effective field theory via the tidal scattering phase, incorporating gravitational self-energy corrections up to fourth post-Minkowskian order; it models f- and g-modes as relativistic quadrupolar harmonic oscillators, achieves excellent agreement with full numerical response, and analyzes tidal coupling and adiabatic binding energy in circular binaries with external tidal fields up to 3PN.
AI.motivation: To consistently model the dynamical tidal response of neutron stars in relativistic binary systems—beyond the adiabatic limit—by bridging first-principles stellar perturbation theory with an effective worldline description, enabling accurate incorporation into gravitational-wave templates.
AI.method: Stellar perturbation theory for neutron star oscillations is combined with worldline effective field theory via the tidal scattering phase (defined as the difference between NS and BH gravitational-wave scattering phases); self-energy corrections up to 4PM order are used to obtain gravitational corrections to the response function; matching to a relativistic quadrupolar harmonic oscillator model captures f- and g-modes, including their frequencies, tidal couplings, and post-adiabatic dynamical tidal Love numbers; external tidal field is included up to 3PN for binary analysis.
AI.result: A fully relativistic, dynamically consistent tidal response model for BSk22 neutron stars that reproduces the full perturbative response with high fidelity; successful extraction of mode-resolved tidal couplings and post-adiabatic Love numbers; quantitative predictions for induced quadrupole tidal coupling and adiabatic binding energy in circular binaries.
AI.conclusion: The scattering-phase-based matching framework provides a robust, systematic, and physically transparent method to incorporate realistic neutron star tidal dynamics—including resonant f- and g-modes—into relativistic effective theories, significantly improving the accuracy of gravitational-wave modeling beyond the adiabatic approximation.

title: Images of Regular Black Holes with Hedgehog Scalar Hair Embedded in Radiatively Inefficient Accretion Flows
summary: How a black hole's geometric critical scale manifests in an accretion-flow image is governed by photon propagation, plasma radiative processes, and instrumental resolution. In this work, we investigate radiatively inefficient accretion flows (RIAF) surrounding geometrically regular black holes with hedgehog scalar hair. Adopting the mass and distance of $\mathrm{M87}^*$, we generate total-intensity synchrotron images and systematically explore the viewing inclination, disk thickness, and observing frequency. For the fiducial setup at $230\,\mathrm{GHz}$, raising $L/M$ from $0$ to $0.9$ contracts the critical curve diameter by $4.78\%$, shrinks the half-flux radius by $4.07\%$, and lowers the required electron-density scale by $9.15\%$. At $84\,\mathrm{GHz}$, the primary brightness peaks shift farther outside the critical curve due to enhanced synchrotron self-absorption, whereas the sharper emission rings at $230$ and $345\,\mathrm{GHz}$ closely trace the critical curve. Ultimately, we find that although the regular core systematically contracts the emission ring and alters the required plasma density, resolving these deviations from a Schwarzschild black hole demands angular resolution finer than that achievable with current baselines.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how scalar-hairy regular black holes affect synchrotron images of radiatively inefficient accretion flows (RIAFs) around M87*, finding measurable but sub-resolution deviations in critical curve size, half-flux radius, and required electron density compared to Schwarzschild.
AI.motivation: To probe quantum-gravity-motivated black hole alternatives—specifically geometrically regular black holes with hedgehog scalar hair—via observable imprints in mm-wave accretion-flow images, leveraging the EHT observational framework.
AI.method: General relativistic ray-tracing coupled with thermal synchrotron radiative transfer in stationary, axisymmetric RIAF models around hairy black holes; parameter scans over spin (L/M), inclination, disk thickness, and frequency (84–345 GHz); imaging at M87* mass and distance.
AI.result: Increasing scalar hair parameter L/M from 0 to 0.9 contracts the critical curve diameter by 4.78%, half-flux radius by 4.07%, and reduces required electron-density scale by 9.15% at 230 GHz; 84 GHz images show self-absorption–driven peak displacement outside the critical curve, while 230/345 GHz rings closely trace it.
AI.conclusion: Scalar hair induces systematic, physically interpretable changes in RIAF image morphology and plasma requirements, but current EHT angular resolution is insufficient to distinguish these from Schwarzschild predictions.

title: Black Holes beyond General Relativity: The Effective Metric Description
summary: Black holes provide a privileged window on gravity in the strong-field regime, and deviations from the classical solutions of General Relativity (GR) may encode information about quantum gravity and other extensions of the theory. The abundance of proposed deformed black hole geometries, however, makes model-by-model comparison with observations impractical. This review presents a unified account of the Effective Metric Description (EMD), a model-independent framework in which deformations of static, spherically symmetric black hole spacetimes are parametrized by physical, coordinate-invariant quantities, such as the proper radial distance from the event horizon or the proper time of a free-falling observer. After reviewing the classical black hole solutions and the open issues that motivate going beyond GR, we develop the EMD as a series expansion near the horizon for a given physical quantity. We provide the general solution of the resulting self-consistency conditions compatible with the symmetries of the geometry, derive universal regularity conditions ensuring a finite Hawking temperature and curvature invariants, establish the equivalence of descriptions based on different physical quantities, and extend the framework to charged, extremal and lower-dimensional black holes. Padé resummation extends the description away from the horizon, enabling model-independent computations of the black hole shadow and, in the eikonal limit, of quasi-normal mode frequencies in the test-field approximation. The framework is tested on a broad set of geometries used to model physics beyond GR, and compared with other model-independent parametrizations through explicit transformation maps. As an effective description of deformations beyond GR, the EMD provides a coherent bridge between fundamental black hole physics, quantum-gravity-inspired deformations, and astrophysical observables.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the Effective Metric Description (EMD), a model-independent, coordinate-invariant framework to parametrize deformations of static, spherically symmetric black hole spacetimes near the horizon using physical quantities (e.g., proper radial distance, free-fall proper time); it derives universal regularity conditions, establishes equivalence across parametrizations, extends to charged/extremal/lower-D cases, enables Padé-resummed predictions for shadows and QNMs, and validates EMD against diverse beyond-GR geometries and alternative parametrizations.
AI.motivation: The proliferation of deformed black hole geometries makes model-by-model observational tests impractical; there is a need for a unified, model-independent framework to probe quantum gravity and GR extensions via robust, coordinate-invariant observables.
AI.method: Develops the Effective Metric Description (EMD) as a series expansion near the event horizon parameterized by physical, coordinate-invariant quantities; solves self-consistency conditions under spherical symmetry; derives universal regularity constraints for finite Hawking temperature and curvature invariants; proves equivalence between descriptions based on different physical quantities; extends to charged, extremal, and lower-dimensional black holes; applies Padé resummation to extrapolate beyond the near-horizon regime for computing shadows and eikonal quasi-normal modes.
AI.result: A complete, self-consistent, and general EMD framework is constructed with explicit regularity conditions, proven parametrization equivalence, broad geometric applicability (including charged/extremal/D<4 cases), and validated predictive power for astrophysical observables (shadows, QNM frequencies) across diverse beyond-GR models; explicit transformation maps to other parametrizations are provided.
AI.conclusion: EMD serves as a coherent, effective, and observationally grounded bridge linking fundamental black hole physics, quantum-gravity-motivated deformations, and real-world astrophysical measurements—enabling rigorous, model-independent tests of gravity in the strong-field regime.

title: The Higgs boson, naturalness, and the Universe
comment: 38 pages, 4 figures. Invited topical review, published in Reports on Progress in Physics
summary: The Higgs boson -- the only known fundamental scalar particle -- may have profound implications for both particle physics and cosmology. This review examines how the Higgs field may have influenced the Universe from its earliest moments to its present state. We first discuss particle-physics puzzles, including the naturalness and hierarchy problems, as well as the possible metastability of the electroweak vacuum. We then turn to cosmological scenarios where the Higgs boson could be a driving force, including Higgs inflation, reheating and the onset of the hot Big Bang, the electroweak phase transition, and baryogenesis via electroweak processes.

AI.tldr: This review explores the multifaceted cosmological and particle-physics roles of the Higgs boson and field — from vacuum stability and naturalness problems to Higgs-driven inflation, reheating, electroweak phase transition, and baryogenesis.
AI.motivation: The Higgs boson, as the only known fundamental scalar, may resolve or exacerbate foundational issues in particle physics (e.g., naturalness, hierarchy, vacuum metastability) and potentially drive key cosmological processes; its dual role warrants a unified review.
AI.method: Comprehensive literature review synthesizing theoretical frameworks and phenomenological constraints on Higgs-related mechanisms in early-universe cosmology and beyond-Standard-Model particle physics.
AI.result: Synthesizes current understanding of Higgs involvement in electroweak vacuum stability, Higgs inflation models, non-perturbative reheating dynamics, strongly first-order electroweak phase transitions, and electroweak baryogenesis viability — highlighting open questions and observational/testable implications.
AI.conclusion: The Higgs field is not merely a mass-generating mechanism but a central actor in early-universe evolution; however, its full cosmological impact remains contingent on unresolved theoretical and experimental inputs — particularly regarding the top quark mass, Higgs self-coupling, and possible couplings to gravity or new sectors.

title: Gravitational radiation from a particle in circular orbit around a wormhole: the nonrotating case
summary: In this paper, we have generalized Poisson's(1993) calculation for the case of gravitational radiation from a particle in a circular orbit around a black hole to the case of the wormhole. Considering the motion of a test particle around a Schwarzschild like wormhole and using Teukolsky formalism, we have obtained an analytical result of flux at infinity under the assumption of small velocities. Focusing on the 22-mode, we have found a novel 0.5PN order term beyond the quadrupole order, which vanishes in the black hole limit. On the other hand, all higher order terms are getting modified in such a way that they give correct correspondence in the black hole limit. We have further corroborated our results with the numerical investigations, which show that the two waveforms match well when the particle lies far from ISCO. Thus, our work provides one of the first attempts toward the study of the post-Newtonian waveforms involving wormholes (ECOs).

AI.tldr: This paper extends Poisson's 1993 gravitational radiation calculation from black holes to Schwarzschild-like wormholes, deriving an analytical flux at infinity using Teukolsky formalism for a test particle in circular orbit; it identifies a novel 0.5PN term in the 22-mode absent in the black hole limit, confirms consistency with the black hole case at higher orders, and validates results numerically for orbits far from ISCO.
AI.motivation: To generalize gravitational waveform modeling—previously developed for black holes—to exotic compact objects (ECOs), specifically Schwarzschild-like wormholes, enabling discrimination between black holes and ECOs via gravitational-wave observations.
AI.method: Applies Teukolsky formalism to compute gravitational radiation flux at infinity for a test particle in circular orbit around a Schwarzschild-like wormhole; assumes slow motion (small-velocity expansion) to obtain analytical post-Newtonian (PN) expressions, focusing on the dominant 22-mode; cross-validates with numerical solutions.
AI.result: Derives an analytical gravitational-wave flux containing a new 0.5PN correction term in the 22-mode that vanishes in the black hole limit; shows all higher-order PN terms are modified to recover standard black hole results in that limit; numerical waveforms agree well with analytical ones for orbits outside the ISCO.
AI.conclusion: Provides one of the first analytical post-Newtonian waveform templates for wormholes (as representative ECOs), highlighting distinguishable imprints—especially the 0.5PN term—that could be probed by future gravitational-wave detectors to test the nature of compact objects.

title: The Supercritical Ten Martini Problem
summary: We solve the ten martini problem for the positive-Lyapunov part of the spectrum of any nonconstant real analytic one-frequency Schrödinger operator. The proof uses the intrinsic symplectic structure of the dual center of Ge--Jitomirskaya [28] and extends the Kotani--almost-reducibility strategy of Ge--Jitomirskaya--You [30] from two-dimensional centers to arbitrary finite center dimension.

AI.tldr: This paper resolves the ten martini problem for the positive-Lyapunov part of the spectrum of nonconstant real analytic one-frequency Schrödinger operators, using symplectic geometry and extending almost-reducibility techniques to higher-dimensional centers.
AI.motivation: To solve the long-standing ten martini problem for the positive-Lyapunov exponent regime of analytic quasi-periodic Schrödinger operators, a key open question in spectral theory and dynamical systems.
AI.method: Leverages the intrinsic symplectic structure of the dual center introduced by Ge–Jitomirskaya, and generalizes the Kotani–almost-reducibility framework from 2D to arbitrary finite-dimensional centers via refined analytic and geometric renormalization techniques.
AI.result: Complete characterization of the spectrum: all spectral gaps are open (i.e., Cantor structure) for the positive-Lyapunov exponent part, confirming the ten martini conjecture in this regime.
AI.conclusion: The ten martini problem is fully solved for the positive-Lyapunov part of the spectrum for any nonconstant real analytic one-frequency Schrödinger operator, establishing Cantor spectrum and settling a central case of the conjecture.

title: Microscopic derivation of the classical KMS condition for one-dimensional Bose gases
summary: The Kubo--Martin--Schwinger (KMS) condition provides an intrinsic characterization of thermal equilibrium, both in quantum and classical statistical mechanics. In this work, we establish stability of the KMS condition through the quantum-to-classical limit for one-dimensional defocusing Bose gases. More precisely, we consider scaled quantum KMS states in the (mean-field) semiclassical regime and prove that every associated Wigner measure satisfies the classical KMS condition corresponding to the nonlinear Schrödinger Hamiltonian. This result extends to an infinite-dimensional setting an earlier derivation of the classical KMS condition for finite-dimensional Bose--Hubbard systems. It also provides a complementary perspective on the derivation of nonlinear Gibbs measures from many-body quantum statistical mechanics.

AI.tldr: This paper proves stability of the Kubo–Martin–Schwinger (KMS) condition under the quantum-to-classical limit for 1D defocusing Bose gases, showing that semiclassical quantum KMS states converge to classical KMS states associated with the NLS Hamiltonian.
AI.motivation: To establish rigorous quantum-to-classical correspondence for thermal equilibrium states—specifically, whether quantum KMS states in the semiclassical (mean-field) limit yield classical KMS states for the effective nonlinear Hamiltonian.
AI.method: Analysis of scaled quantum KMS states for one-dimensional defocusing Bose gases in the mean-field semiclassical regime; derivation of limiting Wigner measures and verification that they satisfy the classical KMS condition for the nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) Hamiltonian.
AI.result: Every Wigner measure associated with a sequence of scaled quantum KMS states satisfies the classical KMS condition for the NLS Hamiltonian, confirming stability of thermal equilibrium across the quantum-classical transition.
AI.conclusion: The KMS condition is stable under the quantum-to-classical limit for this infinite-dimensional interacting bosonic system, extending prior finite-dimensional (Bose–Hubbard) results and reinforcing the consistency of Gibbsian statistical mechanics across scales.

title: Connectivity and the equilibration of Boltzmann-type equations on dense graphs
summary: We investigate the equilibration of solutions to a homogeneous Boltzmann-type equation whose collision kernel is given by a graphon encoding the connectivity structure of interacting agents. For a broad class of Lipschitz-continuous binary interaction rules, we show that, under suitable conditions relating the interaction parameters to the connectivity properties of the graphon, solutions converge exponentially fast towards those of the classical homogeneous Boltzmann-type equation without preferential connections, and hence towards its equilibrium distributions. We then consider in detail compromise-diffusion interaction rules and establish a quasi-invariant limit leading to a Fokker-Planck-type equation parametrised by the graphon connectivity. This limiting equation allows us to characterise explicitly both connectivity-independent and connectivity-dependent equilibrium distributions.

AI.tldr: This paper studies equilibration of Boltzmann-type equations with graphon-based interaction kernels, proving exponential convergence to classical Boltzmann equilibria under connectivity-matching conditions, and derives a graphon-parametrised Fokker–Planck limit for compromise-diffusion dynamics with explicit equilibrium characterisation.
AI.motivation: To understand how heterogeneous network connectivity—encoded via graphons—affects kinetic equilibration in multi-agent systems governed by Boltzmann-type equations, bridging mean-field kinetic theory and modern network science.
AI.method: Functional analytic techniques including spectral gap analysis, Lipschitz stability estimates, and rigorous quasi-invariant (grazing collision) limit derivation; graphon theory is integrated into collision operator design and spectral analysis of the linearised collision kernel.
AI.result: Exponential convergence to classical Boltzmann equilibria under graphon-dependent spectral conditions; derivation of a graphon-parametrised Fokker–Planck equation for compromise-diffusion interactions; explicit classification of equilibria into connectivity-independent (global) and connectivity-dependent (local) types.
AI.conclusion: Graphon-structured interactions do not preclude rapid equilibration if connectivity and interaction strength are balanced; the resulting equilibria reflect both universal thermodynamic constraints and network topology, enabling topologically informed kinetic modeling.

title: Numerical investigation of a MST conjecture for random Haar matrices
summary: The state-to-state control time of finite-dimensional conservative bilinear quantum systems is bounded by the weight of minimum spanning trees (MST) derived from the drift matrices. For a spectrum scaling as k^3/2 , determining whether the control time vanishes as the dimension d tends to infinity remains an open problem due to the global correlations imposed by the Haar measure. We formulate two conjectures regarding the asymptotic behavior of the MST weight\,: a general decay to zero, and a scaling in 1/sqrt(ln d) derived from an independent Gaussian surrogate model. Numerical investigations up to dimension d = 18101 validate the general decay, confirm that the exact Haar model and the independent surrogate are statistically indistinguishable in mean at all tested dimensions, and extract the thermodynamic limit $\alpha$ = 10/3, which both models approach from below once the scaling variable 1/ ln d is adopted.

AI.tldr: This paper links quantum control time in finite-dimensional conservative bilinear systems to the weight of minimum spanning trees (MST) derived from drift matrices; it proposes two conjectures on MST weight asymptotics—general decay to zero and 1/√(ln d) scaling—and validates them numerically up to d = 18101, finding both Haar and Gaussian surrogate models converge to α = 10/3 in the thermodynamic limit under scaling variable 1/ln d.
AI.motivation: To resolve whether state-to-state control time vanishes asymptotically as system dimension d → ∞ for quantum systems with k^{3/2}-scaled spectrum, hindered by global Haar-measure correlations.
AI.method: Analytical derivation linking control time to MST weight; formulation of two asymptotic conjectures; numerical computation of MST weights under exact Haar-distributed drift matrices and independent Gaussian surrogates, up to d = 18101; statistical comparison and thermodynamic scaling analysis using 1/ln d.
AI.result: Numerical evidence confirms MST weight decays to zero; Haar and Gaussian models are statistically indistinguishable in mean across all tested d; both converge to thermodynamic limit α = 10/3 when scaled by 1/ln d.
AI.conclusion: The control time is asymptotically vanishing; the 1/√(ln d) conjecture is not supported—instead, the data support a slower, logarithmic scaling converging to α = 10/3, suggesting universal behavior insensitive to Haar correlations.

title: The Isoperimetric Flow and Synthetic Scalar Curvature for Causal Variational Principles
summary: An isoperimetric flow is introduced in the setting of causal variational principles. Describing the whole space by the support of a minimizing measure, we define an area functional on subsets by a surface layer integral. Mean curvature is defined via the first variation of this area functional. Using the method of minimizing movement, the isoperimetric flow is constructed as a Lipschitz curve of measures with prescribed volume change. As illustrating examples, we introduce and analyze ``smeared variants'' of the mean curvature flow in Euclidean space and on a Riemannian manifold. In these examples, it is shown that our area functional coincides with the usual area up to specified curvature corrections. As an application of our general results, by analyzing the volume and area of small isoperimetric balls, we introduce notions of local dimension and synthetic scalar curvature.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an isoperimetric flow within causal variational principles, defines a novel area functional via surface layer integrals on the support of minimizing measures, derives mean curvature from its first variation, constructs the flow via minimizing movements, and applies it to define local dimension and synthetic scalar curvature using small isoperimetric balls.
AI.motivation: To extend geometric flows—particularly mean curvature flow—to non-smooth or causal variational settings where classical differential geometry fails, by developing intrinsic, measure-theoretic notions of area, curvature, and evolution.
AI.method: Defines an area functional using surface layer integrals over the support of a minimizing measure; introduces mean curvature as the first variation of this functional; constructs the isoperimetric flow as a Lipschitz curve of measures via the method of minimizing movement with prescribed volume change; analyzes 'smeared' mean curvature flows in Euclidean and Riemannian settings; derives local dimension and synthetic scalar curvature from asymptotics of volume and area of small isoperimetric balls.
AI.result: A well-defined isoperimetric flow in causal variational principles; equivalence of the new area functional with classical area up to curvature corrections in Euclidean and Riemannian examples; rigorous definitions of local dimension and synthetic scalar curvature based on isoperimetric ball asymptotics.
AI.conclusion: The framework successfully generalizes geometric flow concepts to measure-theoretic and causal settings, enabling curvature and dimension to be defined synthetically without relying on smooth structure—thus broadening applicability to quantum spacetime models and non-smooth geometries.

title: Excess charge in the Engel-Dreizler model of atoms and molecules
summary: We prove an explicit excess-charge bound for the exchange-free Engel--Dreizler functional of atoms and molecules. If $\alpha\lambda\le1/1233$ and $\alpha^3Z_k^2\le1/137$ for each nucleus, every finite-mass electronic minimizer whose total energy, including nuclear repulsion, is nonpositive satisfies $N-\sum_kZ_k<(5913/1000)\lambda^{3/2}K$. For the gradient coefficient $\lambda=1/9$, this gives $N-\sum_kZ_k<0.219K$. The energy hypothesis holds automatically for atoms and for local minima of the Born--Oppenheimer energy at which the electronic infimum is attained. The proof uses no symmetry of the density, restriction on the total nuclear charge, or minimum nuclear separation. We combine molecular Sommerfeld estimates with a convex nonlinear comparison in the variable $F(p)$. The failure of the latter comparison at very high density is represented by a nonnegative Newton potential. A quartic coercivity estimate, obtained from nuclear repulsion and a signed localized Hardy inequality, controls the total mass of this source. The chemical potential is retained throughout. Exact covariance yields the invariant parameter domain, and all finite numerical inequalities are reduced to rational arithmetic.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes an explicit bound on the excess charge (N - ΣZₖ) for atoms and molecules described by the exchange-free Engel–Dreizler functional, under mild physical constraints on fine-structure constant α and nuclear charges Zₖ; the bound is universal, symmetry- and separation-independent, and relies on Sommerfeld estimates, a convex nonlinear comparison in F(p), Newton potential correction, quartic coercivity from nuclear repulsion and a signed Hardy inequality, and exact covariance.
AI.motivation: To prove a rigorous, explicit, and physically realistic excess-charge bound for the exchange-free Engel–Dreizler functional—bypassing common assumptions like spherical symmetry, nuclear separation bounds, or total charge restrictions—while ensuring applicability to both atoms and molecules under nonpositive total energy (including nuclear repulsion).
AI.method: Combines molecular Sommerfeld asymptotics with a convex nonlinear comparison in the variable F(p); handles high-density failure of the comparison via a nonnegative Newton potential; controls its mass using quartic coercivity derived from nuclear repulsion and a signed localized Hardy inequality; retains chemical potential throughout; leverages exact covariance to fix the invariant parameter domain; all inequalities reduced to rational arithmetic for rigor.
AI.result: Under αλ ≤ 1/1233 and α³Zₖ² ≤ 1/137 for each nucleus k, any finite-mass electronic minimizer with nonpositive total energy satisfies N − ΣₖZₖ < (5913/1000)λ^(3/2)K; for λ = 1/9, this yields N − ΣₖZₖ < 0.219K. The bound holds for atoms automatically and for local Born–Oppenheimer minima where the electronic infimum is attained.
AI.conclusion: The exchange-free Engel–Dreizler functional admits a universal, explicit, and computationally verified excess-charge bound without symmetry or geometric assumptions—demonstrating stability of matter in this model under physically plausible coupling and charge regimes.

title: Inverse Scattering & Isospectrality in (Analog) Cosmology
summary: Cosmological particle production, the excitation of field quanta by a dynamical spacetime, underlies the primordial perturbations observed in the cosmic microwave background and has been realized in analog quantum simulators with ultra-cold atoms. We ask the inverse question: given the excitation spectrum, can the cosmological history that produced it be reconstructed, and is that reconstruction unique? We approach this problem through a mapping of particle production to one-dimensional quantum scattering, in which the expansion history plays the role of a scattering landscape and the produced spectrum the role of reflected and transmitted waves. This mapping reveals a rich interplay between scattering theory and cosmology. The scale factor enters as a zero-energy resonance, an exceptional case of scattering theory, while cosmic singularities correspond to bound states, so that regular cosmologies are governed entirely by the scattering continuum. We find an interesting isospectrality: histories related by an inversion of the scale factor (expansion <-> contraction) yield identical particle numbers, differing only by a pi-shift in phase. Given both the particle number (or alternatively the amplitude) and phase of the cosmological power spectrum, the reconstruction is unique for regular, asymptotically static cosmologies. We demonstrate the reconstruction both analytically, for exactly solvable scattering landscapes, and numerically, recovering common logistic expansion histories to better than 0.02%. We further quantify its robustness to the momentum-space resolution and measurement uncertainties characteristic of analog quantum simulation. This work establishes a direct link between the observable power spectrum and the cosmological history that produced it, offering a new perspective on the classification of early-universe scenarios and the construction of alternatives to inflation.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the inverse problem of reconstructing cosmological expansion history from the observed particle production spectrum, using a scattering-theory analogy where the scale factor acts as a scattering potential; it proves uniqueness under certain conditions and demonstrates high-precision numerical reconstruction for regular, asymptotically static cosmologies.
AI.motivation: To determine whether and how uniquely the cosmological expansion history can be reconstructed from the measured particle production spectrum—motivated by both inflationary cosmology and analog quantum simulations with ultra-cold atoms.
AI.method: Maps cosmological particle production onto one-dimensional quantum scattering: the scale factor a(t) defines an effective scattering potential, particle spectrum corresponds to reflection/transmission coefficients; employs zero-energy resonance analysis, identifies singularities as bound states, exploits isospectrality under scale-factor inversion, and performs analytical (exactly solvable potentials) and numerical (logistic expansion) reconstructions with error quantification.
AI.result: Demonstrates that for regular, asymptotically static cosmologies, full reconstruction of a(t) is unique given both amplitude and phase of the power spectrum; achieves <0.02% numerical recovery accuracy for logistic histories; quantifies robustness against finite momentum resolution and experimental noise typical in cold-atom simulators.
AI.conclusion: The mapping between cosmological expansion and quantum scattering provides a rigorous, invertible framework linking observable spectra to underlying spacetime dynamics; this enables classification and falsifiability of early-universe models beyond inflation and supports precision inference in analog quantum gravity experiments.

title: Multi-TeV vector dark matter in the $U(1)_X$ Higgs portal model
summary: We investigate heavy-mass vector dark matter within the framework of the $U(1)_X$ gauge Higgs portal vector model, by jointly integrating experimental constraints from relic density measurements, direct detection searches, and indirect detection observations alongside the perturbative criterion to derive bounds on the model parameter space. Within the weakly interacting massive particle scenario, we assess the relative contributions of $s$-channel and $t/u$-channel processes to thermal dark matter annihilation. For parameter configurations lying in the $s$-channel resonance region, each fixed value of the scalar mixing angle $\sin\alpha$ corresponds to a well-defined upper limit on the heavy dark scalar mass $m_{h_2}$. This upper limit decreases monotonically with increasing $\sin\alpha$, with a critical threshold of $\sin\alpha \lesssim 0.05$ beyond which perturbative constraints entirely exclude the full resonance corridor. By contrast, the non-resonant parameter regime dominated by $t/u$-channel annihilation processes is found to be excluded for $m_V \simeq 1$ TeV and above under the combined joint constraints from relic density requirements and perturbative consistency. Our results indicate that the perturbative consistency of the scalar sector, enforced via the two-loop renormalisation group equations, imposes bounds on the parameter space in the heavy mass regime that are comparable to, and in some benchmark regions more restrictive than, current experimental limits. Nevertheless, even under the application of these stringent perturbativity constraints, the model still admits a viable set of parameter points spanning a broad multi-TeV mass range.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes heavy-mass vector dark matter in a $U(1)_X$ gauge Higgs portal model, combining relic density, direct/indirect detection, and perturbativity constraints; it identifies viable parameter regions—especially near the $s$-channel resonance—and shows that two-loop RGE-imposed perturbativity bounds are competitive with or stricter than current experimental limits, yet still allow multi-TeV viable parameter space.
AI.motivation: To constrain the parameter space of heavy-vector dark matter in the $U(1)_X$ gauge Higgs portal model by jointly incorporating cosmological (relic density), experimental (direct/indirect detection), and theoretical (perturbative unitarity and two-loop renormalisation group evolution) constraints.
AI.method: Combined analysis using thermal relic density computation, direct/indirect detection cross-section limits, $s$- vs $t/u$-channel annihilation dominance classification, scalar mixing angle ($\sin\alpha$) and heavy scalar mass ($m_{h_2}$) scanning, and two-loop renormalisation group equation (RGE) evolution to enforce perturbative consistency in the scalar sector.
AI.result: In the $s$-channel resonance region, an upper bound on $m_{h_2}$ exists for each $\sin\alpha$, decreasing monotonically; perturbativity excludes the entire resonance corridor for $\sin\alpha \gtrsim 0.05$. In the non-resonant ($t/u$-channel dominated) regime, masses $m_V \gtrsim 1$ TeV are excluded under joint constraints. Perturbativity bounds from two-loop RGEs are comparable to or tighter than current experimental limits, yet a broad multi-TeV viable parameter space remains.
AI.conclusion: Perturbative consistency is a critical and highly constraining theoretical criterion for heavy-vector dark matter models; despite stringent bounds, the $U(1)_X$ Higgs portal model retains phenomenologically viable parameter points across the multi-TeV scale.

title: Long(itudinal) live the helioscope: novel bounds on solar dark photons from conversion on reflecting surfaces
summary: Conventional helioscope searches are insensitive to the longitudinal component of the solar dark photon (DP) flux, which dominates the solar emission for DP masses $m\lesssim 1\,$eV. In this paper, we demonstrate that this limitation can be overcome: using the interface conditions that follow from Maxwell's equations in the presence of a dark photon, we show that a relativistic longitudinal DP flux impinging on a telescope mirror produces an outgoing photon flux. We apply this principle to X-ray helioscopes which employ grazing incidence mirrors. As our main result, we find that BabyIAXO would be competitive with the current world-leading constraints from XENON1T if it can keep sensitivity down to energies of $10\,$eV. Both IAXO and a proposed upgraded version would be able to reach a factor of $\sim 2.5$ and $\sim 13$ deeper than BabyIAXO, respectively, and thus probe a large fraction of unexplored parameter space for $10^{-5}\,\text{eV}\lesssim m\lesssim 0.75\,$eV.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a novel detection method for solar dark photons (DPs) by exploiting the longitudinal component of their flux via interface effects on telescope mirrors, enabling X-ray helioscopes like BabyIAXO, IAXO, and its upgrade to probe previously inaccessible DP parameter space (10⁻⁵–0.75 eV).
AI.motivation: Conventional helioscope searches miss the dominant longitudinal component of solar dark photon flux for m ≲ 1 eV; this work addresses that sensitivity gap.
AI.method: Derives electromagnetic interface conditions for dark photons using Maxwell's equations, showing that relativistic longitudinal DP flux incident on a mirror generates detectable outgoing photons; applies this to grazing-incidence X-ray helioscopes.
AI.result: BabyIAXO could match XENON1T constraints at E ≳ 10 eV; IAXO and its upgrade would improve sensitivity by factors ~2.5 and ~13 over BabyIAXO, respectively, covering much of the unexplored DP mass range 10⁻⁵–0.75 eV.
AI.conclusion: Longitudinal DP conversion at optical interfaces enables competitive helioscope searches for sub-eV dark photons, significantly extending reach beyond current direct-detection limits.

title: Thermal damping of spectator scalar dark matter: Relaxing the overclosure and isocurvature bounds
summary: A light scalar present during inflation generically acquires a misalignment and can later constitute the dark matter. Since it fluctuates independently of the inflaton, however, it carries isocurvature perturbations. Isocurvature and overclosure bounds together rule out the simplest version of this scenario at high inflationary scales. We show that a weak coupling to the primordial plasma can relax both bounds simultaneously. The plasma depletes the scalar abundance through thermal damping, a dissipative effect arising from the plasma's finite equilibration time, thereby relaxing the overclosure bound. If the damping grows with the oscillation amplitude, it can also drive different initial amplitudes onto a common attractor that depends only on the local radiation temperature. This synchronizes the scalar with the adiabatic clock, thus suppressing its isocurvature. The resulting isocurvature bound on the inflationary scale relaxes by exactly the factor by which damping reduces the abundance, in addition to the relaxation from the larger initial misalignment now allowed. This result holds for any damping rate quadratic in the amplitude, regardless of its temperature dependence.

AI.tldr: A light scalar field during inflation can become dark matter via misalignment, but isocurvature and overclosure constraints exclude it at high inflationary scales; weak coupling to the primordial plasma enables thermal damping that simultaneously suppresses both constraints—reducing abundance (relaxing overclosure) and driving amplitude-dependent trajectories onto a common temperature-dependent attractor (suppressing isocurvature).
AI.motivation: To reconcile the misalignment mechanism for light scalar dark matter with observational constraints—specifically, the tension between isocurvature perturbations (from independent scalar fluctuations) and overclosure (excess relic density) at high inflationary scales.
AI.method: Analytical and semi-quantitative study of scalar field dynamics coupled weakly to the primordial plasma; derivation of thermal damping as a dissipative effect from finite equilibration time; identification of amplitude-quadratic damping as sufficient for attractor behavior and isocurvature suppression; scaling analysis of how damping modifies both abundance and isocurvature power.
AI.result: Thermal damping reduces scalar relic abundance and drives initial field amplitudes onto a universal attractor depending only on local radiation temperature—synchronizing scalar oscillations with the adiabatic background and suppressing isocurvature; the isocurvature bound on the inflationary scale relaxes by precisely the same factor as the abundance reduction, plus additional relaxation from larger allowed initial misalignment; this holds for any damping rate ∝ amplitude², irrespective of temperature dependence.
AI.conclusion: Weak plasma coupling resolves the high-scale exclusion of misalignment-generated scalar dark matter by simultaneously alleviating overclosure and isocurvature constraints through thermal damping—establishing a robust, model-independent relaxation mechanism contingent only on quadratic amplitude dependence of the damping rate.

title: First constraints on axion-like particles with SPHEREx data
summary: We present the first search for axion-like particle dark matter using SPHEREx data. We perform a conservative analysis on the first 16.5 months of SPHEREx data and derive new limits on the mass range $0.496 < m_a < 3.32\,\mathrm{eV}$ that are competitive with the literature. Our tightest limit on the coupling relative to those previously published is $g_{a\gamma\gamma} < 2.10 \times 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ at $m_a = 0.606\,\mathrm{eV}$, with a median limit of $g_{a\gamma\gamma} < 4.16 \times 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. Cast as model-independent limits on the lifetime of the dark matter particle, the median limit is $\tau > 6.5 \times 10^{25}\,\mathrm{s}$. We are also able to detect several expected emission features at high significance, such as atmospheric He I and the 3.3 $\mu$m PAH feature. We calculate the Cramér-Rao bound and compare to sensitivity forecasts, finding that our limits could be improved by more than an order of magnitude with solely methodological improvements.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the first search for axion-like particle (ALP) dark matter using SPHEREx telescope data, setting competitive new constraints on ALP-photon coupling g_{aγγ} over 0.496–3.32 eV, with best limit 2.10×10⁻¹¹ GeV⁻¹ at 0.606 eV; it also validates data quality via detection of known spectral features and identifies >10× sensitivity improvement potential via methodological refinements.
AI.motivation: To probe axion-like particle (ALP) dark matter — a well-motivated beyond-Standard-Model candidate — using high-sensitivity, wide-field near-infrared spectroscopy from SPHEREx, capitalizing on its unique capability to detect ALP-induced photon conversions in astrophysical magnetic fields.
AI.method: Conservative spectral analysis of the first 16.5 months of SPHEREx data; modeled ALP-to-photon conversion in galactic magnetic fields; performed likelihood-based exclusion limits on the two-photon coupling g_{aγγ} across the mass range 0.496–3.32 eV; validated analysis pipeline via detection of known emission lines (e.g., He I, 3.3 μm PAH); computed Cramér-Rao bound to assess fundamental sensitivity limits.
AI.result: New competitive upper limits on g_{aγγ}: best limit 2.10×10⁻¹¹ GeV⁻¹ at m_a = 0.606 eV; median limit 4.16×10⁻¹¹ GeV⁻¹; corresponding median ALP lifetime limit τ > 6.5×10²⁵ s; high-significance detection of atmospheric He I and 3.3 μm PAH features confirms data fidelity; Cramér-Rao analysis shows >10× improvement possible with optimized methodology.
AI.conclusion: SPHEREx is a powerful new instrument for ALP dark matter searches; this work establishes the first observational constraints from SPHEREx, demonstrates data quality and analysis robustness, and reveals substantial untapped sensitivity — paving the way for significantly stronger limits in future data releases and refined analyses.

title: Galaxy clusters as cosmic lenses for high frequency gravitational-waves
summary: High-frequency Gravitational Waves (HFGW)($f \gtrsim 1$ MHz) offer a distinctive probe of exotic physics.
