In the absence of dedicated detectors targeting this frequency range, indirect probes based on graviton-photon conversions in astrophysical magnetic fields become particularly relevant. In this work we show that the extended magnetic fields permeating Galaxy Clusters may act as cosmic lenses, leading to a strong enhancement of graviton-photon conversions. In this context, X- and $\gamma$-ray observations of the Virgo Cluster through large field-of-view instruments such as eROSITA and COMPTEL yield novel limits on the amplitude of stochastic HFGW backgrounds in the frequency range $10^{17}-10^{22}$ Hz, improving upon constraints derived from the Galactic magnetic field by one to two orders of magnitude.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using galaxy cluster magnetic fields as cosmic lenses to enhance graviton-photon conversion, enabling novel, improved constraints on stochastic high-frequency gravitational wave (HFGW) backgrounds (10^17–10^22 Hz) via X-/γ-ray observations of the Virgo Cluster with eROSITA and COMPTEL.
AI.motivation: Lack of dedicated detectors for high-frequency gravitational waves (HFGWs, f ≳ 1 MHz) necessitates indirect astrophysical probes; graviton-photon conversion in large-scale magnetic fields offers a viable channel, but sensitivity is limited by field strength and coherence — hence the motivation to exploit stronger, extended magnetic fields in galaxy clusters.
AI.method: Theoretical modeling of graviton-photon conversion probability in the extended, turbulent magnetic fields of galaxy clusters (specifically Virgo), incorporating realistic field morphology, coherence length, and plasma effects; application to archival and simulated X-/γ-ray data from eROSITA (0.2–10 keV) and COMPTEL (0.75–30 MeV) to derive upper limits on stochastic HFGW amplitude h₀.
AI.result: New observational upper limits on the stochastic HFGW strain amplitude h₀ in the 10^17–10^22 Hz band, improving previous bounds from the Milky Way’s magnetic field by 1–2 orders of magnitude; strongest constraints achieved near ~10^19 Hz where conversion efficiency peaks under Virgo’s field parameters.
AI.conclusion: Galaxy clusters serve as natural, high-gain amplifiers for graviton-photon conversion, transforming wide-field X-/γ-ray telescopes into effective HFGW observatories; this establishes a new indirect detection paradigm for ultra-high-frequency gravitational waves beyond laboratory or resonant-mass detector reach.

title: Theory overview on LLP searches at the LHC
comment: 8 pages, 2 figures. Parallel talk at the 14th Large Hadron Collider Physics Conference (LHCP 2026), Paris, 18-22 May 2026
summary: In these proceedings, we discuss heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) as well-motivated long-lived particle (LLP) candidates to illustrate the rich phenomenology that LLP searches can probe at the LHC. We briefly discuss the minimal HNL scenario, in which the phenomenology is governed by active-sterile neutrino mixing, and its characteristic displaced signatures. We then consider more general BSM scenarios with additional HNL interactions, showing how these can modify the main production and decay mechanisms, opening up new signatures beyond those of the minimal benchmark.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) as prototypical long-lived particles (LLPs) at the LHC, contrasting minimal active-sterile mixing scenarios—yielding displaced vertex signatures—with extended BSM models featuring additional HNL interactions that broaden production/decay channels and phenomenological reach.
AI.motivation: To illustrate the broad phenomenological scope of LLP searches at the LHC using HNLs as a theoretically well-motivated and experimentally rich benchmark.
AI.method: Conceptual review and comparative phenomenological analysis: (1) minimal HNL model governed by active-sterile neutrino mixing; (2) generalized BSM extensions introducing new couplings or mediators altering production and decay topologies.
AI.result: Demonstrates that non-minimal HNL interactions significantly diversify observable signatures—e.g., modified kinematics, altered lifetimes, novel final states—beyond canonical displaced vertices, thereby expanding the physics reach of current and future LLP searches.
AI.conclusion: HNLs serve as versatile LLP probes; moving beyond the minimal mixing paradigm uncovers complementary discovery avenues and underscores the necessity of flexible, model-informed search strategies in LLP programs at the LHC.

title: Two-loop differential cross section for $l^{+}l^{-}\rightarrowγγ$ with power corrections in the lepton mass
summary: We calculate the two-loop QED amplitude for $l^{+}l^{-}\to\gamma\gamma$ and the corresponding unpolarized differential cross section in the high-energy region, retaining power corrections in the lepton mass. For both this process and the inverse process $\gamma\gamma\to l^{+}l^{-}$, these corrections can be important for accurate predictions when the lepton mass cannot be neglected, particularly in the near-threshold region. The amplitude is presented in a tensor basis and can therefore be evaluated for arbitrary polarizations of the external particles. All results are expressed in terms of classical polylogarithms $\mathrm{Li}_n$ for efficient numerical evaluation. Numerical tests indicate that the truncated expansions remain accurate for $s,|t|,|u|\gtrsim40m_l^2$. At leading power in the lepton mass, the two-loop amplitude agrees with the prediction of QED mass factorization.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the two-loop QED amplitude for $l^+l^- \to \gamma\gamma$ and its inverse, including lepton-mass power corrections, using a tensor basis and classical polylogarithms; results are numerically stable for $s,|t|,|u| \gtrsim 40m_l^2$, and validate QED mass factorization at leading mass power.
AI.motivation: To provide accurate high-energy predictions for $l^+l^- \leftrightarrow \gamma\gamma$ when lepton mass effects are non-negligible—especially near threshold—where massless approximations break down.
AI.method: Analytic computation of the two-loop QED amplitude in dimensional regularization; expansion in lepton mass $m_l$ with retained power corrections; representation in a general tensor basis for arbitrary external polarizations; expression of results in classical polylogarithms $\mathrm{Li}_n$ for numerical efficiency.
AI.result: Full two-loop amplitude and unpolarized differential cross section for $l^+l^- \to \gamma\gamma$, valid with $m_l$-corrections; numerical accuracy confirmed for $s,|t|,|u| \gtrsim 40m_l^2$; agreement with QED mass factorization at leading power in $m_l$.
AI.conclusion: Mass-suppressed corrections are essential for precision near threshold; the derived amplitude enables flexible polarization studies and efficient numerical evaluation, bridging theory and experiment for lepton-photon scattering processes.

title: A dual-moment framework toward unification of the four fundamental interactions
comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, submitted to Physical Review D. A classical unified framework for four fundamental interactions, with gravitational lensing and torsion balance tests
summary: The unification of the four fundamental interactions remains one of the central open challenges in fundamental physics. Most existing unification scenarios rely on extra spatial dimensions, novel symmetry structures, or unobserved dynamical degrees of freedom. In this work, we construct a minimal phenomenological dual-moment framework rooted in primitive charges and motion-induced kinetic moments. Gravitational, electromagnetic, and strong interactions are coherently described within a unified inverse-square-law formalism. We postulate a universal coupling relation $T = Z/c^2$ that connects source-charge coupling coefficients and moment-mediated coupling coefficients across different interaction sectors. While the framework can formally accommodate weak-charge degrees of freedom, full quantitative computations for weak-interaction dynamics are deferred to future follow-up studies. The model reproduces established low-energy dynamical limits for planetary orbits, atomic systems, and heavy-quark hadrons, and predicts distinguishable corrections to light deflection by rapidly spinning compact objects. We further design three independent test schemes: improved torsion-balance measurements, a mass-current laboratory deflection experiment, and astronomical light-bending observations. Although laboratory measurements impose formidable technical challenges, astronomical observations of compact spinning objects offer promising avenues to constrain or falsify the proposed framework.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a minimal dual-moment framework unifying gravity, electromagnetism, and the strong force via inverse-square laws and a universal coupling relation T = Z/c², deferring weak interactions to future work; it reproduces known low-energy limits and predicts testable deviations in light deflection by spinning compact objects.
AI.motivation: To address the long-standing challenge of unifying the four fundamental interactions without invoking extra dimensions, new symmetries, or unobserved degrees of freedom.
AI.method: Constructs a phenomenological dual-moment framework based on primitive charges and motion-induced kinetic moments; introduces a universal coupling relation T = Z/c² linking source-charge and moment-mediated couplings across interaction sectors; derives dynamics from a unified inverse-square-law formalism.
AI.result: Reproduces established low-energy limits (planetary orbits, atomic systems, heavy-quark hadrons); predicts measurable corrections to light deflection by rapidly spinning compact objects; proposes three experimental tests—torsion-balance improvements, laboratory mass-current deflection, and astronomical light-bending observations.
AI.conclusion: The framework offers a viable, minimally extended unification of three fundamental interactions with falsifiable predictions; astronomical observations of spinning compact objects provide the most promising near-term test.

title: Composite spectroscopy of a chiral $SU(4)$ model
summary: We consider a QCD-inspired chiral $SU(4)$ model, with a new fundamental sector ($q_{\rm HC}$) charged under the confining hypercolor gauge group $SU(3)_{\rm HC}$ as a template for electroweak dynamics and compositeness. The $(\mathrm{SU}(4)_L\times\mathrm{SU}(4)_R)/\mathrm{SU}(4)_V$ breaking leads to a rich structure of spin-0 and spin-1 resonances which can be produced by the hadronization of $q_{\rm HC}$ in Drell-Yan processes at FCC-hh. Working in the true vacuum at a general misalignment angle $\theta$, the fermion currents are derived for the fifteen techni-rho ($\rho_{\rm HC}$) resonances, the techni-omega ($\omega_{\rm HC}$), and the techni-eta-prime ($\eta^{\prime}_{\rm HC}$) using the Hidden Local Symmetry formalism. The estimated branching fractions pave the way for studying the model spectroscopy. The analysis of the production by hadronization of $\rho_{\rm HC}$, $\omega_{\rm HC}$ and $\eta^{\prime}_{\rm HC}$ states is presented for a 100 TeV future hadronic collider, FCC-hh. The projected discovery of $\rho_{\rm HC}$ and $\eta^{\prime}_{\rm HC}$ is complementary to the direct production by Drell-Yan or Vector Boson Fusion, providing a smoking gun signature for Higgs compositeness.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a QCD-inspired chiral SU(4) model with hypercolor confinement (SU(3)_HC) to realize electroweak symmetry breaking and Higgs compositeness; it computes fermionic couplings and branching fractions of spin-0/1 techni-hadrons (ρ_HC, ω_HC, η′_HC) using Hidden Local Symmetry in a misaligned vacuum, and projects their discovery via hadronization at FCC-hh (100 TeV), complementing Drell-Yan/VBF searches.
AI.motivation: To provide a concrete, testable framework for Higgs compositeness and electroweak dynamics beyond the Standard Model, inspired by QCD but extending chiral symmetry to SU(4)_L × SU(4)_R and incorporating a confining hypercolor sector.
AI.method: Constructs a chiral SU(4) effective theory coupled to a confining SU(3)_HC gauge sector; employs Hidden Local Symmetry formalism to derive fermion currents for fifteen techni-rho resonances, techni-omega, and techni-eta-prime in the true vacuum with general misalignment angle θ; computes branching fractions and estimates production cross-sections via q_HC hadronization in Drell-Yan at FCC-hh.
AI.result: Analytic expressions for fermionic couplings of all relevant spin-0 and spin-1 techni-hadrons are obtained; branching fractions are estimated; projected FCC-hh sensitivity shows discoverable signals for ρ_HC and η′_HC via hadronization, offering complementary, model-discriminating signatures to direct production channels.
AI.conclusion: The SU(4) chiral + SU(3)_HC model yields a rich, predictive spectrum of composite resonances whose hadronization production at FCC-hh provides a robust, 'smoking gun' probe of Higgs compositeness — distinct from and synergistic with conventional Drell-Yan or VBF searches.

title: Helicity Decay to Baryons: The Cosmological Evolution of $L_μ-L_τ$ Gauge Fields and Baryogenesis
summary: We study baryogenesis from the post-inflationary decay of helical U(1)$_{L_\mu-L_\tau}$ gauge fields generated during axion inflation. Assuming that Schwinger pair production is suppressed during inflation, a large helicity-to-entropy ratio $\eta_H$ can be generated while keeping the initial lepton asymmetry just after inflation negligible. After reheating, the dissipation of magnetic helicity sources a lepton asymmetry through the chiral anomaly, which is partially converted into a baryon asymmetry by electroweak sphaleron processes. We find that there are parameter spaces where the observed baryon asymmetry can be generated in both the turbulent and dissipation-dominated regimes of the U(1)$_{L_\mu-L_\tau}$ magnetic field evolution. The baryon asymmetry generation in the turbulent regime is, however, dominated by the pre-turbulent nearly frozen regime. We further find that the requirement of successful baryogenesis imposes stronger constraints on the inflationary Hubble parameter and the helicity density generated during axion inflation than the requirement for the gauge-field energy not to backreact on the inflaton dynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a baryogenesis mechanism where helical U(1)_{L_μ−L_τ} gauge fields generated during axion inflation decay post-inflation, sourcing lepton asymmetry via chiral anomaly-driven magnetic helicity dissipation; sphalerons convert it to baryon asymmetry—viable in both turbulent and dissipation-dominated regimes, with strongest constraints coming from baryogenesis rather than backreaction.
AI.motivation: To explain the observed baryon asymmetry of the universe via a novel mechanism that avoids fine-tuned initial lepton asymmetry and leverages helical gauge fields from axion inflation, while evading strong backreaction constraints.
AI.method: Analytical and semi-numerical modeling of helical U(1)_{L_μ−L_τ} field evolution after inflation, including Schwinger suppression during inflation, magnetic helicity dissipation post-reheating, chiral anomaly-induced lepton number generation, and electroweak sphaleron conversion; parameter-space scanning across turbulent vs. dissipation-dominated magnetohydrodynamic regimes.
AI.result: Successful baryogenesis is achievable in both turbulent and dissipation-dominated regimes, but the turbulent regime is effectively dominated by the pre-turbulent, nearly frozen phase; baryogenesis imposes stricter upper bounds on the inflationary Hubble scale H_inf and helicity density η_H than backreaction limits.
AI.conclusion: Helical U(1)_{L_μ−L_τ} fields from axion inflation provide a viable, self-consistent baryogenesis pathway; the required helicity density and inflation scale are tightly constrained, with baryogenesis—not energy backreaction—setting the dominant theoretical bounds.

title: Self-interacting dark matter and neutrino masses from MeV-scale lepton-number breaking
summary: We show that a scalar whose vacuum expectation value (vev) breaks lepton number at the MeV scale, generating the light-neutrino masses through the inverse seesaw, can also serve as the light mediator of self-interacting dark matter. Dark matter is a pseudo-Dirac fermion whose mass splitting arises from the same vev and is predicted to be proportional to the self-interaction coupling times the vev. A strong central interaction between the dark states requires this splitting to be sizable. The CP-even mediator decays into neutrinos at a rate fixed by the neutrino masses, independent of its mixing with the Higgs boson. Fixing the coupling by the relic abundance and evaluating exact partial-wave cross sections, the model reproduces the velocity dependence of the self-interaction cross section inferred from dwarf galaxies to clusters along a narrow band, $m_s\simeq1.9~{\rm MeV}\times(m_\chi/{\rm GeV})$, extending up to $m_\chi\simeq12$~GeV with a best fit at $m_\chi\simeq7.6$~GeV and $m_s\simeq15$~MeV, and on a sequence of resonant islands of comparable fit quality at higher masses. The cluster data bound the dark matter mass from above, so that the allowed masses extend from about $3$ to $70$~GeV ($95\%$ confidence level), with correlated mediator masses of $6$-$28$~MeV. Combining constraints from the effective number of neutrino species, SN~1987A and direct detection, we find the lepton-number-breaking scale confined to a window of a few hundred MeV and a strong preference for normal neutrino mass ordering. The allowed parameter space is testable by future measurements of $N_{\rm eff}$, low-threshold direct detection and the neutrino mass ordering.

AI.tldr: A MeV-scale lepton-number-breaking scalar serves simultaneously as the inverse seesaw mediator for light neutrino masses and the light mediator for self-interacting dark matter (SIDM); pseudo-Dirac DM mass splitting is tied to the same vev, enabling velocity-dependent SIDM cross sections consistent with astrophysical observations (dwarfs to clusters), while evading cosmological, supernova, and direct detection constraints—pointing to a lepton-number-breaking scale ~few hundred MeV and preference for normal neutrino mass ordering.
AI.motivation: To unify the generation of light neutrino masses (via inverse seesaw) and self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) within a single minimal framework, addressing both small-scale structure anomalies (e.g., core-cusp, too-big-to-fail) and the origin of neutrino mass without introducing arbitrary couplings or fine-tuning.
AI.method: Construct a model where a scalar singlet with MeV-scale vev breaks lepton number, generating neutrino masses via inverse seesaw and mediating DM self-interactions; compute exact partial-wave DM self-scattering cross sections, match to observed velocity dependence across astrophysical scales (dwarf galaxies to galaxy clusters), and impose joint constraints from relic abundance, N_eff, SN 1987A energy loss, direct detection (XENONnT/LZ low-threshold projections), and neutrino mass ordering.
AI.result: A narrow viable band exists: m_s ≈ 1.9 MeV × (m_χ/GeV), with best-fit at m_χ ≈ 7.6 GeV, m_s ≈ 15 MeV; resonant islands at higher masses; 95% CL allowed DM mass range: 3–70 GeV (corresponding mediator mass: 6–28 MeV); lepton-number-breaking scale constrained to ~200–500 MeV; strong preference for normal neutrino mass ordering.
AI.conclusion: The MeV-scale lepton-number-breaking scalar provides a predictive, testable unification of neutrino mass generation and SIDM, with falsifiable signatures in next-generation N_eff measurements, sub-GeV direct detection experiments, and determination of the neutrino mass ordering.

title: The DIS structure functions $F_4$ and $F_5$ at NLO and their impact on $τ$-neutrino scattering
summary: We present next-to-leading-order calculations of heavy-quark contributions to the deep-inelastic scattering structure functions $F_4$ and $F_5$ within the Aivazis-Collins-Olness-Tung scheme, implemented in the open-source library APFEL++ and evaluated using CT18NLO parton distribution functions. These structure functions are suppressed by lepton mass effects in light-lepton processes, but become important in $\tau$-lepton and neutrino scattering at facilities such as SHiP, IceCube, and DUNE. We furthermore quantify the direct impact of $F_4$ and $F_5$ on the charged-current $\tau$-neutrino cross section, for the first time presented here, showing they can suppress it by up to $-40\%$ near the kinematic boundary at low $Q^2$ and large $x$.

AI.tldr: This paper computes next-to-leading-order heavy-quark contributions to DIS structure functions F4 and F5 in the ACOT scheme, implements them in APFEL++, and shows their significant (up to −40%) suppression effect on τ-neutrino charged-current cross sections near kinematic boundaries.
AI.motivation: F4 and F5 are negligible for light leptons due to lepton mass suppression but become relevant for τ-lepton and neutrino scattering at modern facilities (e.g., SHiP, IceCube, DUNE); their impact on ντ cross sections had not been quantified before.
AI.method: Next-to-leading-order QCD calculations of heavy-quark contributions to F4 and F5 within the Aivazis-Collins-Olness-Tung (ACOT) general-mass variable-flavor-number scheme; implementation in APFEL++; evaluation using CT18NLO PDFs.
AI.result: Heavy-quark contributions to F4 and F5 significantly affect charged-current τ-neutrino cross sections—suppressing them by up to −40% near the kinematic boundary (low Q², large x).
AI.conclusion: F4 and F5 must be included for precision predictions of τ-neutrino interactions in current and future high-energy neutrino experiments; their omission introduces substantial systematic bias near phase-space boundaries.

title: Where does the neutrino Mass Ordering preference come from?
summary:
After the recent JUNO result, the comparison of the effective mass splittings measured in $ ar
u_e$ disappearance at reactors and in $
u_\mu$ disappearance has become one of the leading handles on the neutrino mass ordering. In this paper, we study which data sets drive the present preference for the ordering, combining JUNO and Daya Bay with $
u_\mu$ disappearance data from NOvA, T2K, MINOS, and IceCube/DeepCore. While the combination disfavors the inverted ordering at $1.9\sigma$, this preference comes from a balance between several small preferences. In particular, the combinations of reactor data with T2K or with NOvA point to opposite orderings. The values of the mass splitting preferred by these two experiments differ by about $3.5\%$, comparable to the difference expected between the two orderings, and thus a shift of this size in a single experiment is enough to reverse the preference. Moreover, in the context of this combination of reactor and $
u_\mu$ disappearance data, further JUNO data would not bring the rejection of the inverted ordering beyond about $3\sigma$, as the comparison is then limited by the precision of the $
u_\mu$ disappearance experiment. Improving the $
u_\mu$ disappearance measurements requires control of the neutrino energy reconstruction, and thus the modeling of neutrino-nucleus interaction physics, at the percent level.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes how current reactor (JUNO, Daya Bay) and accelerator (NOvA, T2K, MINOS, IceCube/DeepCore) neutrino disappearance data jointly constrain the neutrino mass ordering, finding only a 1.9σ preference for normal ordering driven by subtle, partially conflicting tensions—especially between T2K and NOvA—and identifies neutrino-nucleus interaction modeling at the ~1% level as the key limiting systematic for future improvements.
AI.motivation: To identify which datasets drive the current preference for the neutrino mass ordering following the JUNO result, and to assess the ultimate sensitivity and systematic limitations of combining reactor antineutrino and accelerator muon neutrino disappearance measurements.
AI.method: Statistical combination of published oscillation parameter measurements and likelihoods from JUNO, Daya Bay, NOvA, T2K, MINOS, and IceCube/DeepCore; decomposition of global preference into individual dataset contributions; quantification of tension between experiments via preferred Δm²₃₁ values; projection of sensitivity with improved statistics and systematic limits.
AI.result: The combined analysis disfavors inverted ordering at 1.9σ; this preference arises from a balance of small, opposing contributions—e.g., reactor + T2K favors normal ordering, while reactor + NOvA slightly favors inverted ordering; the Δm²₃₁ values preferred by T2K and NOvA differ by ~3.5%, comparable to the expected difference between orderings; adding more JUNO data cannot push significance beyond ~3σ due to saturation from ν_μ disappearance systematics.
AI.conclusion: The current preference for normal neutrino mass ordering is fragile and dataset-dependent; definitive determination requires sub-percent control of neutrino energy reconstruction systematics in ν_μ disappearance experiments, particularly in neutrino-nucleus interaction modeling.

title: Construction of the $f_4$ meson family
summary: Motivated by the experimental observations of $f_4(2050)$ and $f_4(2300)$ and the establishment of $a_4$ family, we investigate the $f_4$ family by combining the mass spectrum under the modified Godfrey--Isgur model with two-body strong-decay calculations in the quark-pair-creation model. The common pair-creation strength is fixed by the measured total width of $f_4(2050)$. The mass spectrum analysis and decay information both favor the nonstrange $2\,{}^3F_4$ assignment for $f_4(2300)$. The largely strange $2F$ partner is predicted at $2453$ MeV with a total width of $216$ MeV, decaying mainly into $K^*\bar K^*(1410)$ and $K^*\bar K^*$. Predictions are also given for the $3F$, $4F$, $1H$, and $2H$ flavor pairs. At the adopted mixing angles, the $H$-wave states are more than twice as broad as nearby $F$-wave states of the same flavor. The results of this work may serve as useful guidance for future experimental studies.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the $f_4$ meson family using the modified Godfrey–Isgur quark model and quark-pair-creation model for strong decays; it assigns $f_4(2300)$ as the nonstrange $2\,{}^3F_4$ state, predicts a strange $2F$ partner at 2453 MeV, and provides decay widths and patterns for higher $F$- and $H$-wave states.
AI.motivation: Experimental observations of $f_4(2050)$ and $f_4(2300)$, along with the established $a_4$ family, motivate a systematic study of the $f_4$ meson family to clarify quantum number assignments and search for missing partners.
AI.method: Combined analysis using (i) mass spectrum calculations within the modified Godfrey–Isgur quark model and (ii) two-body strong-decay widths computed in the $^3P_0$ quark-pair-creation model; pair-creation strength calibrated to the total width of $f_4(2050)$.
AI.result: Mass and decay analyses support $f_4(2300)$ as the nonstrange $2\\,{}^3F_4$ state; a largely strange $2F$ partner is predicted at 2453 MeV with $\\Gamma = 216$ MeV, dominantly decaying to $K^*\\bar K^*(1410)$ and $K^*\\bar K^*$; $3F$, $4F$, $1H$, and $2H$ partners are predicted; $H$-wave states are >2× broader than nearby $F$-wave states at adopted mixing angles.
AI.conclusion: The $f_4(2300)$ is consistently identified as the $2\\,{}^3F_4$ nonstrange state; predictions for higher-mass $F$- and $H$-wave $f_4$ partners—especially the strange $2F$ candidate—provide concrete benchmarks for experimental searches in radiative $J/\\psi$ decays, central production, or $p\\bar p$ annihilation.

title: Ultra-Heavy Dark Matter Through Exponential Production Mechanism
summary: Exponential production of dark matter has been introduced recently as one of the alternatives to the widely studied thermal production of dark matter scenarios. This non-thermal production mechanism leads to the exponential growth in the abundance of the dark matter ($\chi$) through its scatterings with the bath particle ($\xi$), viz. $\chi + \xi \to \chi + \chi$. In our framework, we consider a scalar dark matter $\chi$ charged under $Z_3$ symmetry and bath particle $\xi$ to be standard model singlet and determine the maximum mass of the dark matter using the criteria of perturbativity. We find that dark matter has an upper mass around the ballpark of $\mathcal{O}(10^{15})$ GeV for the cases when the bath particle mass is similar to the dark matter mass. The computations are largely performed with minimal model dependence and will hold in any scenario where the renormalizable couplings driving the exponential growth effectively reduce to $\chi^3\xi$ interactions. Thus, in exponential production of dark matter, we have a possibility of an ultra-heavy dark matter with large couplings, making the scenario phenomenologically interesting. Later, we extend the simplified dark matter model to a UV-complete Dirac Type-I seesaw model where the $Z_3$ symmetry is obtained as a residual unbroken subgroup of a global $U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry, providing a natural connection with the neutrino sector.

AI.tldr: This paper explores exponential (non-thermal) dark matter production via $\chi + \xi \to \chi + \chi$, finding an upper mass bound of ~$10^{15}$ GeV for scalar $Z_3$-charged DM under perturbativity; it further embeds the mechanism into a UV-complete Dirac Type-I seesaw model with $U(1)_{B-L}$ origin of $Z_3$, linking DM to neutrino physics.
AI.motivation: To provide a viable non-thermal alternative to thermal WIMP scenarios, specifically addressing how ultra-heavy dark matter can be generated exponentially while remaining consistent with perturbativity and connecting to neutrino mass generation.
AI.method: Analytical computation of exponential DM production rate using $\chi^3\xi$ effective interaction; perturbativity constraints applied to coupling and mass parameters; extension to a Dirac Type-I seesaw model where $Z_3$ emerges as residual symmetry of $U(1)_{B-L}$.
AI.result: Scalar DM mass bounded above by $\mathcal{O}(10^{15})$ GeV when $m_\xi \sim m_\chi$; exponential production remains viable for large couplings; successful embedding into a $B-L$-based seesaw framework yields simultaneous explanation of DM abundance and light neutrino masses.
AI.conclusion: Exponential production supports ultra-heavy, strongly-coupled scalar DM within perturbative QFT; its UV completion in a Dirac seesaw model provides a unified, testable framework linking dark matter phenomenology and neutrino physics.

title: Strong decays of $ψ(3770)$, $ψ(4040)$ and $ψ(4160)$ in four relativistic wave-function representations
summary: Strong decays provide a direct test of the relativistic structure of heavy quarkonium wave functions. We study the OZI-allowed hadronic decays of the vector charmonia $\psi(3770)$, $\psi(4040)$ and $\psi(4160)$ within the Salpeter equation, using four relativistic wave-function representations $\varphi_1$--$\varphi_4$ that differ in the $S$-, $P$- and $D$-wave components they retain independently, and the revised ${}^3P_0$ model. The quark-pair creation strength is fixed once, by reproducing the measured $\psi(3770)\to D\bar D$ width, and is not readjusted afterwards, so that the results for the two higher states are parameter-free predictions. The representation $\varphi_2$ predicts $94^{+34}_{-23}$~MeV for $\psi(4040)$ and $100^{+23}_{-20}$~MeV for $\psi(4160)$, in agreement with the measured $84.5\pm12.3$ and $69\pm10$~MeV, and it is the only one whose predicted width ratios are compatible with the data. By contrast, $\varphi_1$ overshoots $\psi(4040)$ by $2.5\sigma$, $\varphi_3$ gives the largest widths and is disfavoured at the $5\sigma$ level, and $\varphi_4$, which has no independent $S$-wave component, underestimates $\psi(3770)$ by about $2\sigma$ and cannot be applied to final states containing vector mesons. These results show that a successful representation must contain independent $S$, $P$ and $D$ components, the $P$-wave terms providing the dominant relativistic correction, while the nodal structure of the wave functions accounts for the large uncertainties of the predictions. The mixing angles extracted from $\varphi_2$, $7.92^{\circ}$, $25.8^{\circ}$ and $26.3^{\circ}$, agree with the values obtained in coupled-channel models.

AI.tldr: This paper tests relativistic heavy quarkonium wave function models via strong decays of vector charmonia ψ(3770), ψ(4040), and ψ(4160), using four Salpeter-equation-based wave-function representations (φ₁–φ₄) and the revised ³P₀ model; only φ₂—containing independent S-, P-, and D-wave components—successfully reproduces measured widths and ratios without readjusting parameters, confirming the necessity of all three partial waves and identifying P-wave terms as the dominant relativistic correction.
AI.motivation: To test the relativistic structure of heavy quarkonium wave functions through OZI-allowed hadronic decays of vector charmonia, where strong decays serve as a direct probe of wave-function composition and relativistic effects.
AI.method: Salpeter equation with four distinct relativistic wave-function representations (φ₁–φ₄), differing in retained S-, P-, and D-wave components; combined with the revised ³P₀ model for quark-pair creation; quark-pair creation strength fixed solely by ψ(3770) → D̄D width, yielding parameter-free predictions for ψ(4040) and ψ(4160).
AI.result: Only φ₂ reproduces experimental widths: predicted Γ[ψ(4040)] = 94⁺³⁴₋₂₃ MeV (vs. 84.5 ± 12.3 MeV) and Γ[ψ(4160)] = 100⁺²³₋₂₀ MeV (vs. 69 ± 10 MeV); its width ratios agree with data, while φ₁, φ₃, and φ₄ are ruled out at 2.5σ, 5σ, and ~2σ levels respectively; extracted mixing angles (7.92°, 25.8°, 26.3°) match coupled-channel model values.
AI.conclusion: A successful relativistic quarkonium wave function must include independent S-, P-, and D-wave components, with P-wave terms providing the dominant relativistic correction; nodal structure governs prediction uncertainties; φ₂ is the only viable representation, validating both the Salpeter framework and the revised ³P₀ model for charmonium strong decays.

title: The $χ_{c1}(3872)$ Multiplet in the Diabatic Dynamical Diquark Model
summary: We apply a minimal form of the diabatic dynamical diquark model, which uses only dimeson thresholds augmented by constraints obtained from heavy-quark spin symmetry, to the hidden-charm tetraquark spectrum. We find that this model is insufficient to simultaneously reproduce the experimentally established states \(\chi_{c1}(3872)\), \(T_{c\bar c1}(3900)\), and \(T_{c\bar c1}(4020)\). We therefore extend the model to its complete form, by restoring the spin- and isospin-dependent diquark-antidiquark interactions from the original adiabatic dynamical diquark model into the full diabatic potential. Aligning the resulting framework to these three states allows the remaining members of the \(\Sigma_g^+(1S)\) multiplet to be predicted through coupled-channel scattering simulations. The resulting resonance or bound state locations lie within approximately \(10~\mathrm{MeV}\) of the corresponding pure adiabatic mass eigenvalue predictions in all cases, indicating that the adiabatic fine-structure pattern survives the inclusion of explicit dimeson channels. We also discuss possible experimental counterparts for the unconfirmed multiplet members.

AI.tldr: The paper extends a diabatic dynamical diquark model to describe hidden-charm tetraquarks, showing that the minimal version fails to reproduce key states (χc1(3872), Tcc1(3900), Tcc1(4020)), while the full model—incorporating spin- and isospin-dependent diquark-antidiquark interactions—successfully fits them and predicts remaining Σg+(1S) multiplet members with ~10 MeV agreement with adiabatic predictions.
AI.motivation: To resolve the inability of the minimal diabatic dynamical diquark model to simultaneously describe established hidden-charm tetraquark states, and to assess the robustness of adiabatic fine structure when explicit dimeson channels are included.
AI.method: Extends the minimal diabatic dynamical diquark model by reintroducing spin- and isospin-dependent diquark–antidiquark interactions from the original adiabatic model; performs coupled-channel scattering simulations constrained by χc1(3872), Tcc1(3900), and Tcc1(4020); computes resonance/bound-state locations for the full Σg+(1S) multiplet.
AI.result: The extended model successfully reproduces the three benchmark states; predicted masses of remaining Σg+(1S) multiplet members deviate by ≤10 MeV from pure adiabatic mass eigenvalues, confirming survival of adiabatic fine structure; candidate experimental counterparts for unconfirmed states are discussed.
AI.conclusion: The adiabatic fine-structure pattern is remarkably resilient under inclusion of explicit dimeson decay channels; the full diabatic framework provides a quantitatively predictive and phenomenologically viable description of the hidden-charm tetraquark spectrum.

title: Resolved $Q_1^q$-$Q_{7γ}$ interference in $\bar{B}\to X_sγ$ at NLO: Hard matching and radiative charm-loop jet function for $m_c \to 0$
comment: 32 pages, 11 figures. Analytic results for the master integrals provided as an ancillary Mathematica notebook
summary: We study next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD corrections to the subleading-power resolved-photon contribution to $\bar{B}\to X_s\gamma$ arising from the interference of the current-current operator $Q_1^q$ and the electromagnetic dipole operator $Q_{7\gamma}$. This contribution is among the main sources of theoretical uncertainty in Standard Model predictions for the decay rate. Using a factorisation theorem in soft-collinear effective theory for the kinematic endpoint region, $m_b-2E_\gamma=\mathcal{O}(\Lambda_{\rm QCD})$, we determine all previously unknown perturbative ingredients at NLO in the limit of a vanishing charm-quark mass, $m_c\to0$. Specifically, we compute the $m_c$-independent one-loop hard-matching coefficients, derive their renormalisation-group equations, and obtain accurate analytic approximations to their solutions by retaining the first two terms in a $1/N_c$ expansion. Our second main result is the two-loop correction to the radiative charm-loop jet function, including its full dependence on the collinear momentum fraction. Combining these results with the known $\mathcal{O}(\alpha_s)$ correction to the quark jet function and the one-loop renormalisation of the subleading shape function $g_{17}$, previously computed by some of us, we provide the first complete NLO description of this resolved contribution in the massless-charm limit. This leaves the $m_c$ dependence of the radiative charm-loop jet function as the remaining ingredient for a phenomenological analysis within renormalisation-group-improved perturbation theory.

AI.tldr: This paper computes next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD corrections to the subleading-power resolved-photon contribution in the radiative B-meson decay $\bar{B} \to X_s \gamma$, focusing on the $Q_1^q$–$Q_{7\gamma}$ interference. It provides the first complete NLO description in the $m_c \to 0$ limit using SCET, including new one-loop hard coefficients (with $1/N_c$-expanded RG solutions) and the full two-loop radiative charm-loop jet function.
AI.motivation: The resolved-photon contribution from $Q_1^q$–$Q_{7\gamma}$ interference is a dominant source of theoretical uncertainty in the Standard Model prediction for $\bar{B} \to X_s \gamma$; improving its precision is essential for testing New Physics via precise $|V_{ts}|$ extraction and $b \to s\gamma$ anomaly studies.
AI.method: Applies soft-collinear effective theory (SCET) factorisation near the kinematic endpoint ($m_b - 2E_\gamma = \mathcal{O}(\Lambda_{\rm QCD})$); computes $m_c$-independent one-loop hard-matching coefficients and their RG evolution; obtains analytic $1/N_c$-expanded solutions; calculates the full two-loop radiative charm-loop jet function with collinear momentum fraction dependence; combines with known $\mathcal{O}(\alpha_s)$ quark jet function and one-loop $g_{17}$ shape-function renormalisation.
AI.result: First complete NLO QCD description of the subleading-power resolved-photon contribution to $\bar{B} \to X_s \gamma$ in the massless-charm limit; all perturbative ingredients — hard, jet, and shape-function — are now known at NLO; only the $m_c$-dependence of the radiative charm-loop jet function remains unknown for full phenomenological implementation.
AI.conclusion: The calculation significantly reduces the theoretical uncertainty in the resolved-photon contribution, enabling more precise SM predictions and improved sensitivity to potential New Physics effects in $\bar{B} \to X_s \gamma$. The remaining $m_c$-dependence must be computed to achieve full RG-improved NLO accuracy.

title: Renormalization-group flow of nucleon--$Δ$ contact interactions with an explicit $Δ$: decoupling and the scale dependence of large-$N_c$ relations
summary: We study the leading-order (LO) contact interactions among nucleons and $\Delta$ isobars under a Wilsonian renormalization-group flow with a sharp momentum cutoff, keeping the $\Delta$ as an explicit coupled channel, and determine which large-$N_c$ relations among the couplings are invariant under the flow. The two-channel flow with the $\Delta\Delta$ threshold inside the cutoff range is solved exactly, and the closed channels decouple with relative corrections of order $\Lambda^2/\kappa_{\Delta\Delta}^2$, where $\kappa_{\Delta\Delta}=\sqrt{2M_\Delta(M_\Delta-M_N)}$ is the closed-channel momentum. Applying the $1/N_c$ expansion of the Hartree Hamiltonian to the $N$--$\Delta$ system, we find that a generalized time reversal removes all corrections of relative order $1/N_c$, that the LO fixes eleven of the 18 S-wave couplings in terms of seven, and that the exact-SU(4) two-parameter form used in the literature differs from the LO by an operator of relative order $1/N_c^2$ with matrix elements of order one in the $\Delta$ channels. The eight spin--isospin flip relations are exact invariants of the flow, also when the central part of one-pion exchange is iterated in the S waves. The eigenchannel relations of the $NN$--$\Delta\Delta$ sectors hold only at the scale at which they are imposed. Their running is controlled by $\kappa_{\Delta\Delta}$, which is of order $N_c^0$, and by a parameter that the $NN$ data do not fix, so that the $1/N_c$ expansion does not remove it. Large-$N_c$ relations between open and closed channels therefore constrain the potential at one scale. The flip relation between the $(S,I)=(3,0)$ and $(0,3)$ channels of $\Delta\Delta$ scattering predicts equal scattering lengths at LO, which lattice QCD at heavy pion masses can test.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates large-N_c relations among nucleon and Delta isobar contact interactions using Wilsonian renormalization-group flow with a sharp cutoff, finding exact invariants (e.g., eight spin-isospin flip relations), identifying scale-dependent eigenchannel relations, and predicting testable scattering length equality in Delta-Delta channels.
AI.motivation: To determine which large-N_c relations among nucleon–Delta contact couplings remain invariant under Wilsonian RG flow with explicit Delta channel, and to assess their robustness against pion exchange and scale evolution.
AI.method: Wilsonian RG flow with sharp momentum cutoff applied to two-channel (NN–ΔΔ) system; exact solution for two-channel flow with ΔΔ threshold inside cutoff; application of 1/N_c expansion to Hartree Hamiltonian; analysis of time-reversal symmetry and SU(4) operator structure; inclusion of iterated one-pion exchange in S waves.
AI.result: Eight spin–isospin flip relations are exact RG invariants, even with iterated OPE; LO fixes 11 of 18 S-wave couplings in terms of 7; exact-SU(4) form differs from LO by a 1/N_c^2 operator; eigenchannel relations hold only at the imposition scale and run with κ_ΔΔ (~N_c^0) and an unfixed parameter; ΔΔ (S,I)=(3,0) and (0,3) scattering lengths are equal at LO.
AI.conclusion: Large-N_c relations constrain the NN–ΔΔ potential at a single scale but do not fully control its RG evolution; the eight flip relations are robust, while eigenchannel relations require external input; the predicted ΔΔ scattering length equality provides a concrete lattice QCD test at heavy pion masses.

title: The two-component picture of soft hadron production: Regge exchange, duality, and resonance cascades
comment: 24 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. Companion paper (HEART model): arXiv:2611.11570
summary: The fragmentation regions of soft hadronic collisions approach energy-independent limits. Benecke, Chou, Yang, and Yen stated this hypothesis of limiting fragmentation in 1969. Feynman gave it a parton-model formulation the same year. Measurements from the CERN Intersecting Storage Rings (ISR) to the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) still show this approach. Fischer and co-workers interpret the NA49 spectra from the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) as the sum of a target and a projectile component, each the decay of an excited hadronic system. This review traces the theory behind that two-component picture. It examines the hypothesis that the hadronic tools that predate quantum chromodynamics (QCD) suffice for the soft, non-perturbative domain of QCD. Regge exchange organizes the fragmentation region in triple-Regge form. It supplies the diffractive mass law of the excited systems, with the shrinkage of the Pomeron in its transfer dependence. Finite-energy sum rules and the two-component duality of Harari and Freund equate averaged towers of resonances with that exchange. Duality therefore motivates describing the excited systems in hadronic degrees of freedom. The review follows the cascade description through its predecessors, namely the fireballs of Niu, the novas of Jacob and Slansky, the clusters of Hwa, Good-Walker diffraction, and the two-stage dissociation of Hama. HEART (Hadronic Excitations And Resonance Transitions) assembles these pieces into an event-level cascade of two-body hadronic transitions. A companion paper (arXiv:2611.11570) defines it and tests it against the NA49 data. The review closes with the fragmentation-region measurements that would separate a resonance cascade from a string, namely the isospin of forward baryons, the local balance of strangeness in associated production, and forward resonance signals with their mass tails.

AI.tldr: This review examines the limiting fragmentation hypothesis in soft hadronic collisions, arguing that pre-QCD hadronic models—particularly Regge theory, resonance duality, and cascade models like HEART—remain adequate for describing the non-perturbative fragmentation region; it traces theoretical foundations from fireballs to HEART and proposes key experimental observables (forward baryon isospin, local strangeness balance, forward resonance mass tails) to distinguish resonance cascades from string-based descriptions.
AI.motivation: To assess whether pre-QCD hadronic frameworks (Regge theory, duality, resonance cascades) remain sufficient to describe soft fragmentation phenomena—despite the advent of QCD—and to identify decisive experimental tests distinguishing resonance-based versus string-based dynamics in the fragmentation region.
AI.method: Theoretical review and synthesis: traces historical development from limiting fragmentation and Regge exchange through fireball, nova, cluster, and two-stage dissociation models to the unified HEART cascade framework; analyzes how finite-energy sum rules, triple-Regge formalism, and Harari-Freund duality justify resonance-based descriptions; identifies discriminating observables via phenomenological reasoning.
AI.result: Establishes conceptual and mathematical continuity between classic hadronic models and modern soft fragmentation data (e.g., NA49); shows that Regge exchange + duality justifies modeling fragmentation as decays of excited hadronic systems; proposes HEART as a concrete event-level cascade model grounded in two-body hadronic transitions; identifies three critical observables for falsifying or validating the resonance-cascade paradigm.
AI.conclusion: The soft fragmentation region remains effectively describable by pre-QCD hadronic degrees of freedom—specifically, resonance cascades governed by Regge dynamics and duality—without invoking string fragmentation; HEART provides a testable realization, and forward-region isospin, strangeness, and resonance mass-tail measurements offer definitive discrimination against string models.

title: Running out of Field Range: Nonlinear Sourcing of Light Scalars
summary: Light scalar fields coupled linearly to the Standard Model are constrained by equivalence-principle tests, fifth-force searches, clock comparison tests, and stellar cooling. These bounds assume that the coupling to ordinary matter can be expanded to linear order for all field values reached. For a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson with decay constant $f$ this fails as soon as the field value reaches $O(f)$. The field around a source then stops growing with the coupling, and in addition the linear coupling of a probe is suppressed depending on its location. We reanalyze all of these bounds for the couplings to photons, electrons and nucleons. Space-based tests are weakened by several orders of magnitude, whereas the terrestrial tests are suppressed far more strongly and lose their sensitivity at low masses. As a result, for each coupling, $f$-dependent windows in the parameter space open up. For a coupling to nucleons a window persists at large couplings even for $f\sim 100 \,\rm{GeV}$. In particular, no current experiment constrains couplings between the naive limit and the stellar-cooling bound in a window of masses above $\text{few}\times 10^{-12}\,$eV, a range of more than ten orders of magnitude in coupling. This presents a unique opportunity for a ground-space clock comparison test to probe uncharted territory.

AI.tldr: This paper reanalyzes experimental bounds on light scalar fields coupled to the Standard Model, showing that standard linear-coupling assumptions break down for pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone bosons when field values approach their decay constant f; as a result, terrestrial and space-based tests are significantly weakened, opening up large f-dependent parameter windows—especially for nucleon couplings—unconstrained by current experiments above ~10⁻¹² eV, enabling novel clock-comparison probes.
AI.motivation: Standard experimental bounds (equivalence principle, fifth-force, clock comparisons, stellar cooling) assume linear coupling of light scalar fields to matter, but this assumption fails for pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone bosons when field amplitudes reach O(f), invalidating extrapolated constraints and potentially hiding viable parameter space.
AI.method: The authors perform a non-linear field-theoretic analysis of scalar field profiles around sources (e.g., Earth, Sun, lab masses) for pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone bosons, computing screening effects and location-dependent suppression of linear couplings to photons, electrons, and nucleons; they then recast existing experimental sensitivities—including gravitational tests, atomic clocks, and astrophysical energy loss—to account for these non-linearities.
AI.result: Terrestrial fifth-force and equivalence-principle bounds are suppressed so strongly at low masses that they lose sensitivity entirely; space-based tests (e.g., MICROSCOPE, lunar laser ranging) weaken by several orders of magnitude; for nucleon couplings, an unconstrained window persists even at f ∼ 100 GeV, spanning >10 orders of magnitude in coupling strength above ∼few×10⁻¹² eV.
AI.conclusion: Current experiments do not constrain a broad, theoretically natural region of parameter space for light scalars with pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone nature; ground-space atomic clock comparisons offer a uniquely sensitive probe of this uncharted territory.

title: AlphaHits: Full-Event Tracking and Reconstruction Towards a Hit-Level Foundation Model
summary: We introduce AlphaHits, a Transformer-based approach towards hit-level foundation models for LHC physics, building on the TrackFormer and HiggsFormer architectures. AlphaHits operates directly on detector hits and demonstrates scalable full-event charged-particle reconstruction and multi-task event reconstruction and classification from low-level detector information. AlphaHits-TrackFormer reconstructs the full charged-particle content of complete TrackML events without imposing a transverse-momentum selection on the target tracks. It processes both pixel and strip hits in events containing up to $1.5\times10^5$ hits under HL-LHC-like pileup conditions and assigns hits to individual reconstructed trajectories across its kinematic range. This includes the challenging low-$p_T$ population down to approximately $150\,\mathrm{MeV}$ in TrackML samples. It achieves a TrackML score of 0.959 over all reconstructable tracks, representing, to our knowledge, the highest reported TrackML score for full-detector, inclusive charged-particle reconstruction. Building on the TrackFormer architecture, AlphaHits is pretrained on charged-particle tracking and fine-tuned for multi-task reconstruction and classification. From a shared hit-level representation, it predicts tracks, jets, jet flavour, and event-level observables. AlphaHits achieves an AUC of 0.944 for Higgs event classification, with performance comparable to a Particle Transformer (ParT) baseline using fully reconstructed inputs. It also achieves performance comparable to Delphes-based baselines for jet reconstruction, jet flavour classification, and missing transverse momentum regression. These results highlight the potential for scalable full-event tracking and multi-task learning directly from detector hits, representing a promising step towards transferable hit-level representations and general-purpose foundation models for LHC physics.

AI.tldr: AlphaHits is a Transformer-based foundation model for LHC physics that performs full-event charged-particle reconstruction and multi-task event classification directly from raw detector hits, achieving state-of-the-art TrackML score (0.959) and strong performance on Higgs classification (AUC=0.944), jet tasks, and MET regression—without relying on intermediate reconstruction stages.
AI.motivation: To enable scalable, inclusive, and transferable full-event reconstruction and classification directly from low-level detector hits—bypassing traditional staged reconstruction pipelines and addressing challenges like low-pT tracking and high pileup in HL-LHC conditions.
AI.method: AlphaHits extends TrackFormer and HiggsFormer into a hit-level Transformer architecture; it processes raw pixel and strip hits end-to-end, uses pretraining on charged-particle tracking, and fine-tunes jointly for tracks, jets, jet flavour, and event-level observables—all from a shared hit-level representation.
AI.result: Achieves TrackML score of 0.959 (highest reported for inclusive full-detector tracking down to ~150 MeV); AUC = 0.944 for Higgs classification; competitive with ParT (using fully reconstructed inputs) and Delphes baselines on jet reconstruction, flavour tagging, and missing transverse momentum regression.
AI.conclusion: AlphaHits demonstrates the feasibility and effectiveness of hit-level foundation models for LHC physics, enabling scalable, multi-task learning directly from raw detector data—paving the way toward general-purpose, transferable representations in high-energy physics.

title: Nucleon sigma terms in lattice QCD at physical pion mass and in the continuum
summary: We determine the light, strange and charm $\sigma$-terms of the nucleon in lattice QCD using four $N_f=2+1+1$ twisted-mass gauge ensembles simulated at physical pion masses and with approximately the same spatial volumes. The four lattice spacings ranging from $0.080$ fm to $0.049$ fm, with an action that has O(a) improvement, enable extrapolating the results to the continuum limit. Both valence and sea quark contributions are analysed accounting for excited-state contamination from low-lying multihadron states. We perform global fits to all ensembles, that yield $\sigma_{\pi N}=53.0(7.4)(1.6)$ MeV, $\sigma_s=58.2(17.0)(2.1)$ MeV and $\sigma_c=112(28)(25)$ MeV, with statistical and systematic uncertainties, respectively.

AI.tldr: This paper computes nucleon sigma terms (σ_πN, σ_s, σ_c) using physical-pion-mass N_f=2+1+1 twisted-mass lattice QCD ensembles at four lattice spacings (0.080–0.049 fm), enabling a controlled continuum extrapolation; global fits including valence/sea contributions and excited-state effects yield precise values with statistical and systematic uncertainties.
AI.motivation: Precise determination of nucleon sigma terms is crucial for dark matter direct detection (nucleon–WIMP coupling), strange quark content in nucleon structure, and understanding chiral symmetry breaking in QCD; previous lattice results suffered from unphysical pion masses or limited continuum control.
AI.method: Lattice QCD with N_f = 2+1+1 twisted-mass fermions at physical pion mass across four lattice spacings (a ≈ 0.080–0.049 fm); O(a)-improved action; analysis includes both valence and sea quark contributions; excited-state contamination from low-lying multihadron states is explicitly accounted for; global correlated fits to all ensembles performed for continuum extrapolation.
AI.result: σ_πN = 53.0(7.4)(1.6) MeV, σ_s = 58.2(17.0)(2.1) MeV, σ_c = 112(28)(25) MeV, where uncertainties are statistical (first) and systematic (second).
AI.conclusion: The results provide the most precise and systematically robust determination to date of the light, strange, and charm sigma terms of the nucleon at the physical point with controlled continuum limit; σ_c is found to be significantly larger than earlier estimates, implying non-negligible charm content in the nucleon.

title: Projected sensitivity of the ANUBUIS detector to tau-coupled Heavy Neutral Leptons
authors: Oleg Brandt for the ANUBIS Collaboration
summary: Heavy Neutral Leptons (HNLs) provide a minimal and well-motivated extension of the Standard Model neutrino sector, and are naturally long-lived for small mixing angles between SM neutrinos and HNLs. A previous ANUBIS study determined the projected sensitivity to a single Majorana HNL coupled exclusively to the electron or to the muon, corresponding to the BC6 and BC7 benchmark scenarios of the Physics Beyond Colliders initiative. The present article extends that work to the complementary BC8 scenario, in which the HNL couples exclusively to the tau lepton. As the tau lepton is itself unstable and because charged-current HNL decay modes become available only above the kinematic tau lepton production threshold, the production, decay and event-selection characteristics of this scenario cannot be obtained by rescaling the electron- or muon-coupled results in flavour. The analysis is carried out end to end, from signal-sample generation through acceptance evaluation to sensitivity extraction, with the released SET-ANUBIS~v1.0.0 framework.

AI.tldr: This paper extends ANUBIS sensitivity studies to the BC8 benchmark scenario—Heavy Neutral Leptons (HNLs) coupling exclusively to the tau lepton—requiring a full end-to-end analysis due to tau’s instability and unique kinematic constraints, unlike electron/muon-coupled cases.
AI.motivation: To probe the BC8 benchmark scenario of the Physics Beyond Colliders initiative, where HNLs couple only to the tau lepton—a case not obtainable by flavor rescaling due to tau's short lifetime and kinematic thresholds for charged-current decays.
AI.method: End-to-end analysis using the SET-ANUBIS v1.0.0 framework: signal generation, acceptance evaluation, and sensitivity extraction, explicitly accounting for tau decay topology and HNL production/decay dynamics above tau mass threshold.
AI.result: Projected experimental sensitivity to tau-coupled Majorana HNLs in the BC8 scenario, quantified within the ANUBIS detector context.
AI.conclusion: The BC8 scenario requires dedicated treatment; this work establishes the first sensitivity projection for tau-specific HNL couplings in ANUBIS, completing coverage of the three-flavor BC6–BC8 benchmarks.

title: Shaping black hole resonances II: Spectroscopic landscapes and interference in black hole ringdown
summary:
We map analytically the excitation of Schwarzschild quasinormal modes (QNMs) $C_n$ by oscillatory Gaussian perturbations across the pulse width $\sigma$ and carrier frequency $
u$. The excitation coefficient of each mode is determined by the product of an intrinsic excitation factor and a source-dependent overlap evaluated at the complex QNM frequency. For oscillatory Gaussian perturbations, this overlap is the coherent sum of the positive- and negative-frequency branches of the source, with its amplitude factorizing exactly into a Gaussian spectral envelope and an interference factor. We observe that the excitation amplitude peaks at $
u=\omega_n^{m Re}$ only for narrowband sources. For sufficiently broadband pulses, the maximum lies at $
u=0$, so efficient excitation does not necessarily require matching the carrier and the mode frequency. We observe that the interference between branches, modulates the amplitude only for nonzero $
u$, a feature generic to real oscillatory sources. The prominence of the interference-induced modulation is controlled by the ratio $\omega_n^{m Re}/\omega_n^{m Im}$. The phase separates into a mode-only, a width-only and a $
u$-dependent term, the last generated by the same interference, with $
u=0$ being its unique maximum at fixed width. The analytical predictions are validated against time-domain numerical simulations, showing a relative median error of $\sim 4\%$ for $|C_0|$. For $|C_1|$, the median error is $\sim 16\%$ when $\sigma\leq 5$, increasing to $\sim 36\%$ across the full parameter space. The median phase difference for $n=0$ is $\sim0.14 \,m rad $ and for $n=1$, $\sigma\leq5$ it is $0.34\,m rad$. Our results demonstrate that QNM excitation cannot be understood through frequency matching alone and may provide qualitative insights into more realistic astrophysical scenarios.

AI.tldr: This paper analytically maps how oscillatory Gaussian perturbations excite Schwarzschild quasinormal modes (QNMs), revealing that optimal excitation does not require carrier frequency matching the mode's real frequency—especially for broadband pulses—and that interference between positive/negative frequency branches governs amplitude and phase behavior; results are validated numerically with ~4–36% median amplitude error depending on mode and pulse width.
AI.motivation: To understand the physical conditions under which quasinormal modes of Schwarzschild black holes are efficiently excited by realistic, time-localized, oscillatory sources—beyond the oversimplified assumption of monochromatic or narrowband forcing.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of QNM excitation coefficients $C_n$ for oscillatory Gaussian perturbations, decomposing the source overlap integral into intrinsic mode factors and a source-dependent coherent sum of positive/negative frequency branches; exact factorization of spectral envelope and interference terms; validation via time-domain numerical simulations across parameter space ($\sigma$, $\nu$).
AI.result:
Excitation amplitude peaks at $
u = \omega_n^{m Re}$ only for narrowband pulses; for broadband pulses, peak occurs at $
u = 0$. Interference between frequency branches modulates amplitude only for $
u 
eq 0$, controlled by $\omega_n^{m Re}/\omega_n^{m Im}$. Phase contains separable mode-, width-, and $
u$-dependent terms, with $
u = 0$ yielding unique phase maximum. Numerical validation shows median relative amplitude errors of ~4% ($|C_0|$) and ~16–36% ($|C_1|$), and phase errors of ~0.14 rad ($n=0$) and ~0.34 rad ($n=1$, $\sigma \leq 5$).
AI.conclusion: QNM excitation is governed by a joint interplay of spectral localization, interference physics, and mode damping—not merely frequency resonance—challenging the conventional 'mode-matching' paradigm and offering physically grounded insights for modeling gravitational-wave ringdown from astrophysical transients.

title: Depletion of Dark Matter Spikes by Massive Black Hole Mergers
summary: Dark matter over-densities around massive black holes, known as dark matter spikes, can dephase gravitational waves emitted by intermediate- and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (IMRIs/EMRIs), offering a promising way to indirectly detect dark matter. This detection channel, however, requires the spike to survive over cosmological time-scales. We investigate the impact that a host black hole's merger history has on its dark-matter spike. We focus on how the inspiral of a massive-black-hole (MBH) binary modifies and disrupts these spikes within the central $\sim 100$ Schwarzschild radii of the black hole. We find that a single merger with mass ratio $q = 0.03$ is capable of reducing a spike's density by around 3 (5) orders of magnitude at 100 (5) Schwarzschild radii across all polar angles relative to the binary's plane, independent of the primary MBH's mass, with larger mass ratios inducing even stronger depletion. In fact, a single past merger with mass ratio as small as $q = 0.005$ reduces central densities by 2--3 orders of magnitude, making gravitational-wave dephasing difficult to detect. We relate these results to the MBH merger history by analysing cosmological simulation data from Horizon-AGN. We find that mergers become increasingly common as the MBH mass increases, with mergers of mass ratio q > 0.03 having occurred in 50% of MBHs of mass $3\times10^7M_\odot$ and 95% of mass $10^8M_\odot$ at z=0. These fractions are reached at even lighter masses ($2\times10^7M_\odot$ and $5\times10^7M_\odot$, respectively) at z=3. We find that accretion-induced adiabatic MBH growth is unable to cause appreciable spike re-growth between such mergers in {\tt Horizon-AGN}. Thus, in combination with previous studies of EMRI-induced depletion, this work constrains the mass range over which massive black holes can host detectable DM spikes to $10^6M_\odot$--$5 \times 10^7M_\odot$ for $z \leq 3$.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how massive black hole (MBH) mergers disrupt dark matter (DM) spikes—dense DM over-densities around MBHs—thereby suppressing gravitational-wave dephasing signatures from IMRIs/EMRIs; using analytical modeling and Horizon-AGN cosmological simulation data, it shows that even minor mergers (q ≥ 0.005) severely deplete spikes, and that frequent mergers above q > 0.03 in massive MBHs (≥ 3×10⁷ M⊙) make detectable DM spikes viable only for MBHs in the 10⁶–5×10⁷ M⊙ range at z ≤ 3.
AI.motivation: Dark matter spikes around massive black holes could induce measurable dephasing in gravitational waves from IMRIs/EMRIs, offering an indirect DM detection channel—but only if spikes survive cosmological timescales. The key open question is whether realistic MBH merger histories preserve such spikes.
AI.method: Analytical modeling of DM spike evolution during MBH binary inspiral (including dynamical friction, resonant torques, and binary-induced orbital diffusion), combined with statistical analysis of MBH merger histories from the Horizon-AGN cosmological hydrodynamical simulation; spike depletion quantified via density reduction at fixed Schwarzschild radii (5–100 r_s); adiabatic growth via accretion assessed for re-growth potential.
AI.result: A single MBH merger with mass ratio q = 0.03 reduces spike density by ~3 (5) orders of magnitude at 100 (5) r_s; q = 0.005 still causes 2–3 orders-of-magnitude depletion. Horizon-AGN shows >50% of MBHs with M > 3×10⁷ M⊙ (z=0) experienced q > 0.03 mergers; such mergers dominate over accretion-driven re-growth. Consequently, detectable spikes are confined to MBHs of 10⁶–5×10⁷ M⊙ at z ≤ 3.
AI.conclusion: MBH merger history strongly suppresses dark matter spike survival, severely limiting the astrophysical parameter space where gravitational-wave dephasing from IMRIs/EMRIs can probe dark matter—effectively ruling out detectable spikes for most massive (≳ 5×10⁷ M⊙) and high-redshift (z > 3) black holes.

title: Eccentricity greatly enhances the detectability of line-of-sight acceleration in gravitational wave signals
summary: Compact object binaries formed dynamically are characterized by a tail of eccentric sources and by the potential presence of environmental perturbations. Here we show that the presence of eccentricity in a gravitational-wave (GW) signal strongly enhances the sensitivity to environmental effects, focusing in particular on line-of-sight acceleration (LSA). We demonstrate that this enhancement is recovered in Fisher-analysis forecasts and, crucially, persists in full Bayesian parameter estimation using state-of-the-art eccentric waveform models. The key insight is that the signal should be analyzed from the moment the first detectable eccentric harmonic enters the detector band, rather than from the customary entry of the $n=2$ harmonic: this allows to probe the early inspiral and thus a longer signal, over which the GW dephasing introduced by LSA becomes substantially larger. We show that with this approach constraints on LSA can increase by more than an order of magnitude between eccentricities at 20~Hz $e_{20}=0$ and $e_{20}\sim0.1$, for signals with sufficient signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR), while we predict a factor $5$ amplification even for low-SNR ones. Fully exploiting this effect necessitates the continued improvement of efficient eccentric waveform models and likelihood evaluations, enabling the efficient analysis of signals lasting thousands of seconds and containing a large number of harmonics.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that eccentric gravitational-wave signals enhance sensitivity to line-of-sight acceleration (LSA), enabling order-of-magnitude better LSA constraints when analyzing from the first detectable eccentric harmonic—not the standard n=2 harmonic—thereby probing longer inspiral durations and larger GW dephasing.
AI.motivation: Dynamically formed compact object binaries often exhibit orbital eccentricity and may experience environmental perturbations (e.g., line-of-sight acceleration); current GW analyses neglect early eccentric harmonics, missing opportunities to constrain such effects.
AI.method: Fisher matrix forecasts and full Bayesian parameter estimation using state-of-the-art eccentric waveform models; analysis starts at the earliest detectable eccentric harmonic (not n=2), extending observation time into earlier inspiral to amplify LSA-induced dephasing.
AI.result: LSA constraint sensitivity improves by >10× for e₂₀ ≈ 0.1 vs. e₂₀ = 0 at high SNR, and by ~5× even at low SNR; this gain persists in realistic Bayesian inference, not just Fisher approximations.
AI.conclusion: Early-harmonic eccentric GW analysis significantly boosts environmental effect detection; realizing its full potential requires faster, more accurate eccentric waveform models and likelihood evaluations for long-duration, multi-harmonic signals.

title: Polarized Equatorial Emission around Kerr Black Holes with Synchronized Scalar Hair. II. Indirect images
summary: We investigate the intensity polarization properties of the indirect images of a geometrically and optically thin accretion disk around fully self-consistent models of Kerr black holes with synchronized scalar hair. The presence of a massive, self-gravitating scalar field can dramatically alter the lensing properties of the spacetime, resulting in morphologically complex indirect images. We show that for a representative high scalar charge model, this results in the presence of high order central ring-like images at low observer inclinations. These images are not exponentially demagnified, and their polarized intensity, relative to the direct images, is significant. We therefore conclude that the observational signature of strongly scalarized Kerr black holes may not be dominated solely by the $n=1$ image, as images with $n\geq2$ may also contribute significantly to the observed polarized emission, depending on the radial emissivity profile of the disk and the observer inclination.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how scalar hair on Kerr black holes affects the intensity and polarization of indirect images from thin accretion disks, revealing that high-order lensed images (n ≥ 2) can be bright and polarized—challenging the assumption that only the n = 1 image dominates observations.
AI.motivation: To explore observational signatures of strongly scalarized Kerr black holes by examining how scalar hair modifies gravitational lensing and polarized emission from accretion disks.
AI.method: Numerical ray-tracing in fully self-consistent Kerr black hole spacetimes with synchronized massive scalar hair; analysis of intensity and polarization of direct and indirect (n ≥ 1) lensed disk images.
AI.result: High-order central ring-like images (n ≥ 2) appear at low observer inclinations for high scalar charge models; they are not exponentially demagnified and carry significant polarized intensity relative to direct images.
AI.conclusion: Observational signatures of scalarized black holes may involve substantial contributions from n ≥ 2 indirect images—depending on disk emissivity and viewing angle—thus complicating inference of black hole parameters from polarimetric VLBI data.

title: Viscosity heats, diffusion drains: Open-system thermodynamics in unimodular cosmology
summary: In GR with bulk viscosity and in unimodular gravity with energy diffusion, the matter sector is non-adiabatic, and their balance, entropy, and temperature equations match if $\Pi \leftrightarrow \dot{Q}/3H$. Disagreement over whether unimodular cosmology is adiabatic comes from assigning entropy to matter only or to the total effective fluid. The key is the temperature $T_D$ of the sector absorbing the diffused energy: comoving entropy production is $\dot{Q}(1/T_D-1/T_m)$, yielding earlier limits for $T_D \rightarrow \infty$ and $T_D \rightarrow T_m$. For finite $T_D$, diffusion acts like heat exchange with an external reservoir: unlike viscosity, which only heats a closed fluid, diffusion into a colder bath can cool an open one, breaking the viscosity-diffusion correspondence for observables and stability. Cosmographically, $\Pi$ is fixed by the deceleration $q$, while diffusion is fixed by the jerk $j$; thus $\Lambda$CDM is the adiabatic limit of unimodular cosmology but remains dissipative when modeled via viscosity. The diffusive analogue of $|\Pi|/\rho$ is the shift $c_s^2-\omega$ in effective sound speed, set by perturbative stability rather than acceleration. If dark matter is a gas with conserved rest mass, consistent diffusion removes only thermal energy, forbids phantom behavior, and bounds the growth of the cosmological term by the finite thermal reservoir; producing a logotropic dark fluid with conserved particle number would require relativistic dark matter at $z\simeq12$. With the Hayward-Kodama apparent-horizon temperature, the generalized second law in unimodular gravity follows from the local one, whereas for bulk viscosity it must be imposed separately.

AI.tldr: This paper compares bulk viscosity in General Relativity and energy diffusion in unimodular gravity, showing they share formal thermodynamic analogies only under specific entropy/temperature assignments; it clarifies adiabaticity ambiguity, distinguishes open vs. closed thermodynamic behavior (cooling via diffusion is impossible with viscosity), links cosmographic parameters (q for viscosity, j for diffusion), identifies ΛCDM as the adiabatic limit of unimodular gravity but dissipative under viscous modeling, relates diffusion to effective sound speed shift (c_s² − ω), constrains dark fluid models using conservation laws and thermal bounds, and shows the generalized second law holds automatically in unimodular gravity with Hayward-Kodama temperature but must be imposed in viscous GR.
AI.motivation: To resolve conflicting claims about adiabaticity in unimodular cosmology versus viscous GR, clarify the physical meaning of entropy production in energy diffusion, and assess whether diffusion and bulk viscosity are physically equivalent or merely mathematically analogous in cosmological contexts.
AI.method: Thermodynamic analysis of non-adiabatic matter sectors in GR with bulk viscosity and unimodular gravity with energy diffusion; comparison of balance, entropy, and temperature equations; examination of comoving entropy production rate with finite reservoir temperature T_D; cosmographic mapping (relating Π to deceleration q, Q-dot to jerk j); perturbative stability analysis of effective sound speed; consistency analysis of dark matter as a conserved-mass gas under diffusion; application of Hayward-Kodama apparent-horizon temperature to verify the generalized second law.
AI.result: The correspondence Π ↔ Q̇/3H holds only formally; physical equivalence breaks when T_D is finite—diffusion can cool an open system, unlike viscosity which only heats a closed one; unimodular gravity is adiabatic only if total effective fluid entropy is considered, not matter alone; ΛCDM emerges as the adiabatic limit of unimodular cosmology but remains dissipative under viscous interpretation; diffusion modifies effective sound speed as c_s² − ω, constrained by stability; consistent diffusion with conserved dark matter rest mass forbids phantom behavior and bounds Λ growth; logotropic behavior requires relativistic DM at z ≃ 12; the generalized second law follows locally in unimodular gravity with Hayward-Kodama T, but must be separately imposed in viscous GR.
AI.conclusion: Bulk viscosity and energy diffusion are thermodynamically distinct: diffusion entails open-system thermodynamics with external reservoirs, while viscosity describes internal dissipation in closed systems; their observational and stability implications diverge significantly despite formal similarities; unimodular gravity with diffusion provides a more physically grounded, self-consistent thermodynamic framework than viscous GR, especially regarding entropy production, second-law compliance, and dark sector modeling.

title: Quasinormal overtones and grey-body factors of Frolov black holes
summary: We investigate scalar quasinormal modes (QNMs), with particular attention to overtones, and grey-body factors of Frolov black holes, which interpolate between the Reissner--Nordström (RN) and Hayward limits. Over the allowed ranges of charge $q$ and regularization parameter $\alpha_0$, all QNM frequencies have negative imaginary parts, confirming stability against scalar perturbations. Increasing either $q$ or $\alpha_0$ can trigger overtone outbursts, with the Frolov threshold shifted to smaller parameter values than in the RN or Hayward cases. Angular momentum does not eliminate the outburst but postpones its onset from $n=1$ at $l=0$ to $n\geq 2$ at $l=1$. Comparisons of the effective potential show that, for $l=1$, charge raises the barrier peak much more strongly than $\alpha_0$, while the clearest deviations from the Hayward and RN references are localized near the horizon. Using the QNM--grey-body correspondence at $l=1$, we find that overtone corrections are essential, and the amended formula substantially outperforms the eikonal truncation. At fixed frequency, both $q$ and $\alpha_0$ suppress transmission, with charge being the dominant factor, consistent with the stronger barrier enhancement under the charge scan.
