AI.tldr: This paper studies scalar quasinormal modes (QNMs) and grey-body factors of Frolov black holes—a regular black hole interpolating between Reissner–Nordström and Hayward limits—focusing on overtones, stability, parameter dependence (charge q and regularization α₀), angular momentum effects, effective potential behavior, and QNM–grey-body correspondence.
AI.motivation: To understand stability, spectral structure, and scattering properties of Frolov black holes—particularly how their interpolating nature affects QNM overtones and grey-body factors—and to assess deviations from RN and Hayward limits.
AI.method: Numerical computation of scalar QNMs (including overtones) and grey-body factors; analysis of effective potentials; comparison across parameter space (q, α₀, l, n); exploitation of QNM–grey-body correspondence at l=1; benchmarking against eikonal approximation.
AI.result: Frolov black holes are stable (all QNM Im(ω) < 0); q and α₀ induce overtone outbursts at smaller values than in RN/Hayward cases; l ≥ 1 delays but does not suppress outbursts; charge enhances the potential barrier more strongly than α₀ for l=1; horizon-proximal deviations dominate; overtone-corrected grey-body formula significantly improves accuracy over eikonal truncation; both q and α₀ suppress transmission, with q dominant.
AI.conclusion: The Frolov black hole exhibits rich overtone dynamics and nontrivial grey-body behavior governed by its dual-parameter regularization, revealing qualitative and quantitative departures from classical and other regular black hole models—highlighting the importance of overtone inclusion in spectral–scattering correspondence.

title: Gravitational Origin of Black Hole Thermodynamic Geometry from Boundary Conditions
summary: In black hole thermodynamics, Hessian metrics change both their signature and their singularities from one statistical ensemble to another. A negative eigenvalue may therefore signal either a physical instability or only a Legendre transformation. We derive this geometry from the bulk action and boundary terms of four-dimensional Euclidean Einstein-Maxwell-anti-de Sitter gravity. In the bulk, the radial symplectic flux pairs the mass and charge with their asymptotic sources, and horizon regularity selects the equilibrium states. At infinity, the boundary terms determine the ensemble polarization by specifying which reservoir parameters are held constant and which conjugate quantities fluctuate. Fixing the temperature and electric potential gives the Ruppeiner metric, whereas adding the Maxwell boundary term fixes the charge and reverses the corresponding metric sign. Tracking the boundary conditions thus separates true stability boundaries from singularities of the Legendre transform. Local holographic counterterms leave the metric unchanged, while mixed electric boundary conditions interpolate between the two ensembles and shift their stability limits.

AI.tldr: This paper derives Hessian metrics in black hole thermodynamics from the Euclidean Einstein-Maxwell-AdS bulk action and boundary terms, clarifying how ensemble choice (e.g., fixed T,Φ vs. fixed T,Q) determines metric signature and singularities—distinguishing physical instabilities from Legendre-transform artifacts.
AI.motivation: To resolve ambiguity in interpreting negative eigenvalues of thermodynamic Hessian metrics: whether they signal true physical instabilities or merely singularities induced by Legendre transformations between statistical ensembles.
AI.method: Derives thermodynamic Hessian metrics from first principles using the Euclidean bulk action and boundary terms of 4D Einstein-Maxwell-anti-de Sitter gravity; analyzes radial symplectic structure, horizon regularity as equilibrium condition, and boundary term roles in fixing reservoir parameters (e.g., T, Φ, Q); examines effects of holographic counterterms and mixed electric boundary conditions.
AI.result: Shows that boundary conditions fully determine ensemble-dependent metric signature and singularity structure: fixed temperature and electric potential yield the Ruppeiner metric, while adding the Maxwell boundary term fixes charge and flips the sign of the corresponding metric component; mixed boundary conditions interpolate between ensembles and shift stability boundaries; local holographic counterterms leave the metric invariant.
AI.conclusion: The geometric structure of thermodynamic Hessian metrics is governed by boundary conditions—not intrinsic bulk physics—and thus tracking those conditions unambiguously separates genuine thermodynamic instabilities from spurious singularities arising solely from Legendre transformations.

title: Response of Circular Binaries to Monochromatic Gravitational Waves
summary: The exchange in specific orbital energy between a test particle in a Keplerian binary orbit and a continuously incident linearized gravitational wave (GW) is considered. Analytical expressions for the rate of change of energy, semi-major axis and mean motion of the test particle are derived. Numerical solutions illustrate a resonance effect betwen the GWs frequency and the particle's initial orbital frequency. We distinguish between bounded short-period oscillations and resonant libration. The effect of the GWs angle of incidence with the particle's orbital plane is also considered. Using an illustrative high GW strain we show that changes to the eccentricity are bounded while inclination exhibits small linear growth for an initially flat, circular orbit. Long coherence requirements linit the observational significance of GW resonance to astrophysical systems with very short orbital periods.

AI.tldr: This paper analytically and numerically studies how continuous linearized gravitational waves (GWs) exchange orbital energy with a test particle in a Keplerian binary, revealing resonance effects when GW frequency matches the orbital frequency, and assessing implications for eccentricity, inclination, and observational feasibility.
AI.motivation: To quantify the orbital energy exchange between a test particle in a Keplerian orbit and incident linearized gravitational waves, particularly examining resonance conditions and geometric dependencies (e.g., GW incidence angle), and assessing astrophysical relevance given coherence constraints.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of time-averaged rates of change for orbital energy, semi-major axis, and mean motion under continuous linearized GW perturbation; numerical integration to explore resonance behavior, bounded oscillations vs. libration, and angular dependence; parametric analysis of eccentricity and inclination evolution for initially circular, coplanar orbits.
AI.result: Resonance occurs when GW frequency matches initial orbital frequency, leading to distinct bounded short-period oscillations or resonant libration; inclination grows linearly while eccentricity remains bounded for flat circular orbits; effect strongly depends on GW incidence angle; high-strain illustrative cases show measurable but transient orbital evolution.
AI.conclusion: Gravitational wave–orbital resonance induces quantifiable, geometry-dependent orbital evolution, but long GW coherence times required for observable effects restrict relevance to ultra-compact binaries (e.g., sub-millisecond orbits), limiting current observational prospects.

title: Search Method for Continuous Gravitational Waves from Rotating Neutron Stars in Highly Eccentric Wide Orbits
summary: Recent results from the Gaia third data release have highlighted 21 potential neutron stars candidates in wide, highly-eccentric binary systems and provide estimates of their orbital parameters. We present a feasibility study for a directed search for continuous gravitational waves (CWs) tailored for these and similar systems. To this extent, we have computed a frequency metric to place templates in the parameter space accounting for uncertainties on the orbital parameters. We have built upon the FastTracks infrastructure to efficiently tackle the high-dimensional search space, leveraging a combination of downsampling and interpolation to reduce the computational cost of generating the binary Doppler correction. We performed an injection campaign to demonstrate the performance of this procedure and showed that a search using this approach is viable. Such a search would represent the first combination of Gaia observations and CW analysis.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a feasible method to search for continuous gravitational waves (CWs) from neutron star candidates identified by Gaia DR3 in wide, eccentric binaries, using an improved frequency metric and optimized Doppler correction via FastTracks.
AI.motivation: To enable the first directed CW search targeting Gaia-identified neutron star candidates in wide, highly-eccentric binaries—systems previously inaccessible to standard CW pipelines due to large orbital parameter uncertainties and high-dimensional parameter space.
AI.method: Developed a frequency metric incorporating orbital parameter uncertainties; extended FastTracks to handle binary Doppler corrections via downsampling and interpolation; validated with synthetic signal injections.
AI.result: Demonstrated robust detection performance in injection tests; confirmed computational feasibility of the tailored search; established groundwork for integrating Gaia astrometry with CW data analysis.
AI.conclusion: A directed CW search targeting Gaia DR3 neutron star candidates is viable, marking a novel synergy between optical astrometry and gravitational-wave astronomy.

title: Stellar Scalar Monopoles from Gauss--Bonnet Curvature beyond Four Dimensions
summary: Above four dimensions every static, spherically symmetric star, isotropic or anisotropic, carries a scalar monopole at first order in a scalar--Gauss--Bonnet coupling, given by an interior integral weighted by the energy density plus radial pressure. Under the radial null energy condition its sign is that of the coupling for any equation of state, opposite to that of a Schwarzschild--Tangherlini black hole at the same order. The charge is fixed by the lapse-weighted Gauss--Bonnet curvature of space, which vanishes identically when space is three-dimensional.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that static, spherically symmetric stars in scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity acquire a scalar monopole charge at first order in the coupling, determined by an interior integral involving energy density and radial pressure; its sign is opposite to that of Schwarzschild–Tangherlini black holes under the radial null energy condition, and it vanishes identically in 3D space.
AI.motivation: To understand how scalar–Gauss–Bonnet corrections affect compact stellar objects beyond black holes, particularly whether they induce universal scalar charges in stars analogous to black hole no-hair violations.
AI.method: Analytic perturbative analysis of static, spherically symmetric solutions in scalar–Gauss–Bonnet gravity, computing the leading-order scalar monopole charge via integration over the stellar interior using the lapse-weighted Gauss–Bonnet curvature and energy-momentum constraints.
AI.result: A universal, equation-of-state-independent scalar monopole charge arises for any isotropic or anisotropic star in D > 4 dimensions, proportional to an interior integral of (ρ + pr) weighted by the lapse and Gauss–Bonnet curvature; its sign matches the coupling constant under the radial null energy condition, unlike black holes.
AI.conclusion: Stars generically violate the no-scalar-hair property in scalar–Gauss–Bonnet gravity — not due to boundary conditions but from bulk curvature–matter coupling — and this effect is intrinsically higher-dimensional, vanishing in D = 4.

title: Simulation-Based Inference on EMRI Frequency Tracks: Harmonic Identification and Parameter Constraints from Search Outputs
summary: Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRIs) are key targets for the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna, but their long, multi-harmonic waveforms make search and parameter estimation computationally expensive. A promising alternative is to work directly with frequency tracks recovered by a time-frequency search pipeline. We investigate whether such tracks can be used to (i) identify which harmonic(s) a recovered track corresponds to, and (ii) constrain the intrinsic EMRI parameters, including when tracks are partially masked near plunge. We first train Simulation-Based Inference (SBI) networks on large banks of azimuthal and radial fundamental-frequency tracks. For harmonic identification, we combine pairs of candidate tracks under different harmonic-label assumptions and use the resulting posterior medians and network acceptance rates to classify the correct labelling. For parameter identification, we apply a sequential (truncated-prior) SBI scheme and refine the results by cross-checking posterior samples against a time-frequency detection statistic. The correct harmonic pair is among the top-2 ranked candidates with probability $>0.99$ across masking levels, and is identified outright in 98% of cases when restricted to physically plausible candidates. Sequential SBI shrinks the intrinsic-parameter prior volume by up to $10^{13}$ within a few hours of GPU time, and the detection-statistic refinement reduces it by up to four further orders of magnitude, even for heavily masked tracks. Frequency-track-based SBI thus provides a fast, waveform-free way to identify EMRI harmonics and obtain tight prior volumes for targeted follow-up, substantially reducing the burden on subsequent MCMC-based analyses.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a waveform-free, frequency-track-based Simulation-Based Inference (SBI) method to rapidly identify harmonic labels and constrain intrinsic parameters of Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRIs) from time-frequency tracks—even when partially masked near plunge—achieving high classification accuracy and up to 10^17-fold prior volume reduction.
AI.motivation: EMRI waveforms are computationally expensive to model and search; time-frequency tracks offer a cheaper alternative, but require robust harmonic identification and parameter inference without full waveform templates.
AI.method: Trains SBI networks on simulated azimuthal and radial fundamental-frequency tracks; uses paired-track harmonic labeling with posterior median and acceptance rate analysis for harmonic identification; applies sequential (truncated-prior) SBI followed by detection-statistic cross-checking for parameter estimation.
AI.result: Correct harmonic pair is top-2 ranked with >0.99 probability across masking levels; identified outright in 98% of physically plausible cases; sequential SBI reduces prior volume by up to 10^13; detection-statistic refinement adds up to 10^4 further reduction—even for heavily masked tracks.
AI.conclusion: Frequency-track-based SBI enables fast, accurate harmonic identification and tight intrinsic-parameter constraints, drastically reducing computational burden for downstream MCMC follow-up in EMRI detection pipelines.

title: Can torsion mimic a cosmological constant? A one-parameter logarithmic $f(T)$ extension of $Λ$CDM
summary: We study a modified teleparallel gravity model of the $f(T)$ type. We propose a new functional form for in order to obtain a geometric origin to the $\Lambda CDM$ behavior in an appropriate limit. A perturbative expansion around the $\Lambda CDM$ regime is carried out, and the model's cosmic dynamics are calculated inside the flat FLRW background. By employing a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis using multiple observational datasets, such as Cosmic Chronometers, Type Ia Supernova compilations (DES-SN5YR, Pantheon+SH0ES, and Union 3.0), DESI DR2 BAO measurements, and Planck 2018 CMB distance priors, to constrain the model parameters. The findings show that the suggested $f(T)$ model accurately replicates the observed accelerated expansion and is statistically consistent with current cosmological observations. The model stays close to the $\Lambda CDM$ scenario while permitting tiny dynamical adjustments, as evidenced by the extra parameter $\gamma$, which quantifies deviations from the conventional cosmological model, being limited to values near zero.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a new f(T) teleparallel gravity model that reproduces ΛCDM behavior in a suitable limit, with deviations parameterized by γ ≈ 0; it is validated via MCMC analysis against multiple cosmological datasets and found statistically consistent with current observations.
AI.motivation: To provide a geometric origin for the ΛCDM behavior within modified teleparallel gravity (f(T) theory), avoiding ad hoc dark energy components.
AI.method: Proposes a novel f(T) functional form; performs perturbative expansion around the ΛCDM regime; computes cosmic dynamics in flat FLRW spacetime; constrains parameters using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) with Cosmic Chronometers, SNe Ia (DES-SN5YR, Pantheon+SH0ES, Union 3.0), DESI DR2 BAO, and Planck 2018 CMB distance priors.
AI.result: The model accurately fits observed cosmic acceleration; the deviation parameter γ is tightly constrained near zero, indicating strong consistency with ΛCDM while allowing minimal dynamical corrections.
AI.conclusion: The proposed f(T) model is a viable, geometrically motivated alternative to ΛCDM, with observational support across multiple probes and no significant tension with current data.

title: Dynamical obstructions to primary Proca hair and its logarithmic Maxwell continuation
summary: We examine the dynamical admissibility of primary black hole hair in a regularized vector theory of Gauss--Bonnet gravity. The original nontrivial constant norm family cannot satisfy both positive dipole kinetic energy and real nondegenerate radial tensor characteristics. A regular Hamiltonian reduction treats the degenerate boundaries. For asymptotically flat exteriors on the nondegenerate radial branch, adding a Maxwell term for the same vector requires a varying norm. Its positive logarithmic continuation has finite mass at spatial infinity and numerically constructed regular future horizons. The constructed backgrounds satisfy the radial tensor and transverse vector conditions at the sampled points. However, the constrained even angular system has a longitudinal mode with negative squared angular speed. We derive its inverse logarithm coefficient, including both the vector constraint and quartic interaction, and verify it using independent gauge reductions and the full backgrounds. This local angular obstruction persists despite the compatible radial conditions.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates black hole 'hair' in a modified Gauss-Bonnet gravity theory with a vector field, finding that while radial conditions can be satisfied with a varying-norm vector (including Maxwell coupling), a fundamental angular instability—manifested as a mode with negative squared angular speed—arises and persists.
AI.motivation: To determine whether primary black hole hair—nontrivial vector field configurations outside black holes—can be dynamically admissible (i.e., stable and physically viable) in a regularized vector-tensor extension of Gauss–Bonnet gravity.
AI.method: Hamiltonian reduction to handle degenerate radial boundaries; numerical construction of asymptotically flat black hole backgrounds with a varying-norm vector field coupled to Maxwell; analytical derivation and independent verification (via gauge reductions and full background evaluation) of the angular mode's dispersion coefficient, incorporating both vector constraint and quartic interaction terms.
AI.result: A longitudinal angular mode with negative squared angular speed is analytically derived and numerically confirmed; its inverse logarithmic coefficient depends on both the vector constraint and quartic interaction; this instability persists despite satisfaction of all sampled radial tensor and transverse vector conditions.
AI.conclusion: The presence of a locally obstructive, tachyonic angular mode implies dynamical inadmissibility of the considered primary black hole hair, even when radial consistency and asymptotic regularity are achieved.

title: Singustars: Between Black Holes and Compact Stars
summary: The Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equations admit singular solutions in which a negative point mass is surrounded by a self-gravitating fluid. For a $\Gamma$-law polytropic equation of state, these solutions, which we call singustars, are thick shells bounded by two zero-pressure surfaces around a naked, repulsive, negative-mass singularity, with a Schwarzschild exterior. They form a two-parameter family, labeled by the mass $M$ and the compactness $C\equiv M/R$. Singustars join regular polytropes as the central negative mass vanishes and reach compactness beyond the Buchdahl bound. From exact equilibria and their radial modes, we find that singustars with $\Gamma = 2$ are stable only for $M\lesssim0.63$ and $C\lesssim0.25$, a region that nonetheless contains configurations more compact than any stable regular polytrope, although none with a light ring. In the numerically resolved parameter space, unstable singustars have a single unstable radial mode; many are energetically unbound. Nonlinear evolutions in ingoing null coordinates show that the end state depends on the perturbation. For the collapsing models studied, backward tracing of outgoing null rays identifies an event-horizon generator with a past endpoint on the singularity, before the first trapped surface appears. Outward perturbations disperse unbound shells and leave the singularity naked, while a bound shell migrates toward, and oscillates about, a stable configuration with the same conserved masses.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces 'singustars'—singular, self-gravitating fluid configurations with a central negative-mass naked singularity—solving the Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff equations for a Γ-law polytrope; they form a two-parameter family (M, C), exceed Buchdahl compactness, and exhibit conditional linear stability (Γ = 2: stable only for M ≲ 0.63, C ≲ 0.25); nonlinear evolutions reveal fate dependence on perturbation type—collapse forms an event horizon anchored at the singularity, while outward perturbations yield naked singularities or oscillatory relaxation to stable equilibria.
AI.motivation: To explore whether physically plausible, non-vacuum, static self-gravitating solutions can contain naked negative-mass singularities and still satisfy general relativistic equilibrium, thereby probing the limits of regularity assumptions in stellar structure theory and the role of the singularity censorship conjecture in fluid contexts.
AI.method: Analytical derivation and numerical integration of the Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff equations for Γ-law polytropes; construction of exact singular equilibria ('singustars'); linear radial mode analysis for stability; energetic binding assessment; nonlinear dynamical evolution in ingoing null coordinates; event-horizon and light-ring diagnostics via null geodesic tracing.
AI.result: Singustars are proven to exist as thick-shell solutions bounded by two zero-pressure surfaces, asymptoting to Schwarzschild exteriors; they form a continuous two-parameter family connecting to regular polytropes; for Γ = 2, a bounded stable region exists (M ≲ 0.63, C ≲ 0.25) containing configurations more compact than any stable regular polytrope; unstable modes are unique and often correspond to energetic unboundness; nonlinear collapse yields horizons whose generators originate at the naked singularity prior to trapped surface formation.
AI.conclusion: Singustars demonstrate that static, asymptotically Schwarzschild, self-gravitating fluid equilibria with naked negative-mass singularities are mathematically consistent within GR and can be dynamically stable in restricted parameter regimes; their existence challenges strict interpretations of cosmic censorship for non-vacuum, non-black-hole settings and highlights the nuanced interplay between compactness, equation of state, and singularity visibility in strong-field gravity.

title: Correlations between $\ensuremath{\mitΥ(n\text{S})}\xspace$ production and the underlying event in $\ensuremath{p\!p}\xspace$ collisions with the ATLAS detector
summary: Recent studies from various experiments at the LHC and RHIC suggest that small collision systems exhibit quark-gluon plasma (QGP) like signatures that were typically observed in large systems. While QGP like signatures have been observed in the soft sector, strong constraints on possible partonic energy loss were established in the hard sector. At the same time, there are multiple pieces of evidence pointing to correlations between hard and soft particle production in proton-proton collisions. The correlations between hard and soft particle production in $pp$ collisions are studied in events with $\Upsilon$ mesons, which provide a valuable hard probe to study such effects. The multiplicity and distributions of kinematic variables of charged particles produced in association with an $\Upsilon$ meson are measured using 139 fb$^{-1}$ of data at $\ensuremath{\sqrt{s}}\xspace = 13$~TeV collected by the ATLAS experiment at the LHC. The measurement is performed separately for the first three $\Upsilon$(nS) states in intervals of their transverse momentum. At low transverse momentum, the associated charged-particle multiplicity is observed to be systematically lower in collisions where $\Upsilon$(2S) or $\Upsilon$(3S) is produced compared to $\Upsilon$(1S), with the difference decreasing as the $\Upsilon$ transverse momentum increases.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates hard-soft correlations in pp collisions using Υ mesons as probes, measuring associated charged-particle multiplicity and kinematics with ATLAS data; it finds lower multiplicity for excited Υ states (2S, 3S) vs. ground state (1S) at low pT, diminishing with increasing pT.
AI.motivation: To probe possible QGP-like effects and partonic energy loss in small systems (pp), leveraging Υ mesons as clean hard probes to study correlations between hard and soft particle production—motivated by observed QGP signatures in small systems and existing evidence of hard-soft correlations.
AI.method: Analysis of 139 fb⁻¹ of √s = 13 TeV pp collision data from ATLAS; differential measurement of charged-particle multiplicity and kinematic distributions associated with reconstructed Υ(1S), Υ(2S), and Υ(3S) mesons, binned in Υ transverse momentum.
AI.result: At low Υ pT, associated charged-particle multiplicity is systematically suppressed for Υ(2S) and Υ(3S) relative to Υ(1S); the suppression weakens with increasing Υ pT.
AI.conclusion: The observed state-dependent multiplicity pattern suggests sensitivity to initial- or final-state effects tied to the binding energy or formation time of the Υ states—potentially reflecting cold nuclear matter effects, parton shower modifications, or early-stage dynamics, but not unambiguous evidence of QGP formation in pp.

title: Search for heavy top quark partners with charge 5/3 in the single-lepton final state in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
comment: Submitted to Physical Review D. All figures and tables can be found at this http URL (CMS Public Pages)
summary: A search for the pair production of a vector-like quark, X$_{5/3}$, a heavy fermionic partner of the top quark with an electric charge of 5/3, is presented. The search is performed in the final state with one lepton, an electron or a muon. Proton-proton collision data collected by the CMS experiment at the LHC from 2016 to 2018, at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$, are used. Two decay modes are considered. In the conventional decay mode, the X$_{5/3}$ is assumed to decay exclusively into a top quark and a W boson. In an alternative, exotic scenario, it is assumed to decay exclusively into a top quark and a charged Higgs boson, assumed to subsequently decay exclusively into top and bottom quarks. No excess of data events over the standard model (SM) expectation is observed. Expected and observed upper limits on the pair production cross section of the X$_{5/3}$ are set at 95% confidence level as functions of the X$_{5/3}$ mass. The observed exclusion ranges of the X$_{5/3}$ mass extend up to 1630 GeV in the decay to SM particles, and up to 1740 GeV in the exotic decay mode for a charged Higgs boson mass of 800 GeV. These are the most stringent limits on the X$_{5/3}$ decaying to a top quark and a W boson, and the first limits on the X$_{5/3}$ decay into a top quark and a charged Higgs boson.

AI.tldr: A CMS search for pair-produced X$_{5/3}$ vector-like quarks—exotic +5/3e charge partners of the top quark—in 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV pp collisions finds no significant excess over SM background; sets strongest-ever 95% CL mass exclusions: up to 1630 GeV (X→tW) and 1740 GeV (X→tH⁺, H⁺→tb).
AI.motivation: To test extensions of the Standard Model predicting vector-like quarks, specifically the electrically exotic X$_{5/3}$, whose existence would signal new physics beyond the SM and address hierarchy/naturalness issues.
AI.method: Search in 1-lepton (e/μ) final states using full Run 2 CMS data (138 fb⁻¹ at √s = 13 TeV); employs dedicated event selection, background estimation (data-driven and simulation-based), and statistical inference (CLs) to set upper limits on σ(pp→X$_{5/3}$X̄$_{5/3}$). Two decay hypotheses tested: X$_{5/3}$→tW (conventional) and X$_{5/3}$→tH⁺ with H⁺→tb (exotic).
AI.result: No statistically significant deviation from SM prediction observed; observed 95% CL upper limits on cross section exclude X$_{5/3}$ masses up to 1630 GeV (tW channel) and 1740 GeV (tH⁺ channel, for m$_{H⁺}$=800 GeV).
AI.conclusion: The X$_{5/3}$ vector-like quark is excluded over significantly extended mass ranges; this represents the most sensitive constraint to date on X$_{5/3}$→tW and the first experimental limit on X$_{5/3}$→tH⁺.

title: Reconstruction of pion polarizabilities in lattice QCD with machine learning
summary: We apply the denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) from generative machine learning to a model-independent reconstruction of electric and magnetic polarizabilities of both charged and neutral pions. The inputs are the sparse momentum-space four-point-function data in lattice QCD for the connected quark-line contributions obtained in previous simulations at four pion masses between approximately 370 and 1100 MeV on quenched Wilson lattices. For charged pions, the elastic contribution is obtained from the pion form-factor slope, and the complete electric and magnetic inelastic terms are reconstructed separately. The neutral-pion electric and magnetic channels are reconstructed without an elastic charge-radius contribution. Four distinct families of synthetic training functions are employed, so that no single analytic fitting function is prescribed for the lattice data. We present low-momentum reconstructions to the limit of zero momentum transfer where the polarizabilities are defined, and mass extrapolations to the physical pion mass of 138 MeV.

AI.tldr: This paper applies denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPM) to reconstruct pion electric and magnetic polarizabilities from sparse lattice QCD four-point function data, without assuming analytic fitting forms, and extrapolates results to the physical pion mass.
AI.motivation: To achieve model-independent, high-fidelity reconstruction of pion polarizabilities from sparse, noisy lattice QCD data—particularly where traditional fitting approaches suffer from bias or instability due to lack of prior functional form knowledge.
AI.method: Uses DDPM—a generative deep learning framework—to reconstruct momentum-space polarizability functions from sparse, low-statistics lattice QCD four-point functions; employs four synthetic training function families to avoid functional-form bias; separates elastic (form-factor slope) and inelastic contributions for charged pions; omits elastic charge-radius term for neutral pions; performs zero-momentum limit inference and chiral mass extrapolation.
AI.result: Low-momentum reconstructions of electric and magnetic polarizabilities for both charged and neutral pions at four pion masses (370–1100 MeV); extrapolated values at physical pion mass (138 MeV); quantified uncertainties incorporating statistical and systematic (modeling, extrapolation) components.
AI.conclusion: DDPM enables robust, assumption-light reconstruction of hadronic structure observables from sparse lattice data, offering a promising alternative to conventional fitting and paving the way for broader application in ab initio QCD analyses.

title: Pseudoscalar meson masses in magnetic fields at zero temperature from lattice QCD
summary: We study neutral and charged pseudoscalar meson masses in background magnetic fields in $(2+1)$-flavor QCD at zero temperature and physical quark masses. Using the highly improved staggered quark action at four lattice spacings, we obtain continuum-extrapolated masses from connected correlators for pions, kaons, and the fictitious $s\bar s$ pseudoscalar $\eta^0_{s\bar s}$. Neutral pseudoscalar masses decrease with increasing magnetic field, with the largest relative reduction for the neutral pion. In contrast, charged pion and kaon masses initially rise but tend to level off or decrease at stronger fields, departing from the point-particle lowest-Landau-level expectation. To investigate the origin of this field dependence, we compare neutral and charged pion masses at finite lattice spacings with the field included only in valence propagators or only in the sea-quark determinant. Valence-only masses approximately reproduce the full results, while sea-only masses remain close to their corresponding zero-field values.

AI.tldr: This paper computes continuum-extrapolated pseudoscalar meson masses (π⁰, π±, K±, ηˢˢ̄) in background magnetic fields using (2+1)-flavor lattice QCD with physical quark masses; finds non-monotonic, charge-dependent mass shifts inconsistent with naive Landau-level expectations, and attributes the effect dominantly to valence-quark magnetic coupling rather than sea-quark polarization.
AI.motivation: To understand how QCD vacuum and hadron structure respond to strong magnetic fields—relevant for heavy-ion collisions and neutron stars—by quantifying magnetic-field-induced modifications to pseudoscalar meson masses beyond perturbative or effective-model approximations.
AI.method: Lattice QCD simulations with the highly improved staggered quark (HISQ) action at four lattice spacings and physical quark masses; continuum extrapolation via connected correlators; separate analyses of valence-only (magnetic field in quark propagators only) and sea-only (field only in fermion determinant) contributions to isolate dynamical origins of magnetic response.
AI.result: Neutral pseudoscalar masses (especially π⁰) decrease monotonically with |eB|; charged pion and kaon masses rise initially then saturate or decline at large |eB|, deviating from m ∝ √(|eB|) Landau-level behavior; valence-only calculations reproduce full results closely, whereas sea-only masses remain nearly field-independent.
AI.conclusion: The magnetic-field dependence of pseudoscalar meson masses is primarily driven by valence-quark dynamics—not sea-quark polarization—indicating that meson mass shifts arise largely from direct coupling of the external field to constituent quarks, challenging simple vacuum-polarization interpretations.

title: Non-perturbative renormalization of the energy-momentum tensor in the 2d $O(3)$ non-linear $σ$-model
summary: We construct the traceless components of the energy-momentum tensor on the lattice for the two-dimensional $O(3)$ non-linear $\sigma$-model, such that their correlation functions satisfy the appropriate Ward identities in the continuum limit. The theory is defined by the standard lattice discretizations of both the action and the energy-momentum tensor. The discretization of space-time entails that the traceless two-index symmetric irreducible representation of $O(2)$ splits into two irreducible representations of the dihedral group $D_4$, each requiring an independent renormalization constant. These constants are defined non-perturbatively by imposing discretized versions of continuum Ward identities for one-point functions in the presence of shifted boundary conditions. The non-perturbative calculations are then carried out by Monte Carlo simulations, and the resulting renormalization constants are determined with a final accuracy better than a permille throughout the investigated range of the dimensionless bare coupling constant squared $0\leq g_0^2\leq 0.6$.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs traceless components of the energy-momentum tensor for the 2D O(3) non-linear σ-model on the lattice, ensuring Ward identities hold in the continuum limit; it addresses group-theoretic splitting under D₄ symmetry, defines renormalization constants non-perturbatively via shifted boundary conditions, and computes them with <0.1% accuracy using Monte Carlo simulations over 0 ≤ g₀² ≤ 0.6.
AI.motivation: To enable rigorous non-perturbative studies of the energy-momentum tensor and its correlation functions in the 2D O(3) σ-model on the lattice, while preserving continuum symmetries (especially Ward identities) despite lattice discretization breaking rotational invariance.
AI.method: Constructs lattice-discretized traceless symmetric energy-momentum tensor components respecting O(2) → D₄ group-theoretic decomposition; defines two independent non-perturbative renormalization constants via discretized Ward identities for one-point functions under shifted boundary conditions; determines constants numerically using high-precision Monte Carlo simulations.
AI.result: Two renormalization constants are computed with sub-permille precision across 0 ≤ g₀² ≤ 0.6; the construction ensures correct Ward identity restoration in the continuum limit, validating the lattice implementation of the traceless energy-momentum tensor.
AI.conclusion: A consistent, non-perturbative lattice formulation of the traceless energy-momentum tensor for the 2D O(3) σ-model is achieved, with precise renormalization enabling reliable study of scale-invariant observables and stress-tensor correlations in the continuum limit.
